Overview

The Modern Analytics & Insights organization enables data-driven decision making across Small, Medium, Enterprise & Channel (SME&C) by delivering trusted business intelligence, actionable insights, and scalable analytical capabilities.

SME&C is one of Microsoft’s largest and fastest-growing businesses, focused on empowering customers through the Microsoft Cloud. Within the global SME&C Analytics organization, this role will specifically support the Corporate Accounts business, with a primary focus on Corporate Accounts Intelligence Platform (CAIP) and Azure business intelligence and analytics.

We are seeking a Business Analytics Specialist to own and evolve key business intelligence (BI) and analytical capabilities supporting Corporate Accounts. The role will be responsible for translating Corporate Accounts business priorities into scalable reporting, semantic models, and analytical products that enable leaders and field organizations to understand business performance and take action.

The successful candidate will play a hands-on role across the analytics lifecycle, from understanding business questions and defining metrics through designing semantic models, developing BI solutions, validating data, and driving adoption.

A major focus of the role will be CAIP and the Corporate Accounts Azure analytical experience, including ensuring that Azure performance, customer trends, pipeline and execution signals, and business outcomes are represented through a consistent, trusted analytical framework.

The role will also contribute to the broader evolution of SME&C’s data and analytics architecture by building reusable semantic models, reducing fragmented reporting, improving data quality and performance, and preparing analytical assets for self-service and AI-enabled experiences.

Approximately 60% of the role will focus on Corporate Accounts BI, including CAIP and Azure analytics, with approximately 40% focused on semantic models, data architecture, AI readiness, and self-service analytics enablement.



Responsibilities
  • Serve as a primary analytics partner for the Corporate Accounts CAIP business, developing an understanding of its business priorities, performance drivers, customer segments, sales motions, and execution model.
  • Own and evolve BI experiences supporting Corporate Accounts CAIP and Azure analytics, ensuring leaders and field stakeholders have trusted and actionable views of business performance.
  • Develop and maintain executive scorecards, dashboards, KPIs, business review views, and analytical products supporting Corporate Accounts.
  • Develop analytical experiences that help stakeholders understand Azure performance, growth trends, customer performance, pipeline and execution signals, and areas of business opportunity or risk.
  • Partner with Corporate Accounts business leaders, Sales Excellence, Finance, Strategy, and Operations teams to define reporting requirements, metrics, analytical priorities, and success measures.
  • Translate business requirements into scalable BI solutions rather than one-off reports or analyses.
  • Proactively identify trends, performance drivers, risks, and opportunities and communicate them through clear analytical narratives.
  • Ensure CAIP and related reporting experiences provide consistent definitions and reconcile appropriately across executive, field, and operational views.
  • Continuously improve the usability, performance, and relevance of Corporate Accounts BI based on stakeholder needs and changing business priorities.

Data Architecture, Semantic Models & AI Readiness

  • Design, develop, and maintain the semantic models and analytical data products that underpin Corporate Accounts, CAIP, and Azure reporting.
  • Build and optimize Power BI and Microsoft Fabric semantic models that provide a trusted foundation for Corporate Accounts BI, self-service analytics, and AI-enabled experiences.
  • Translate business concepts into well-structured dimensions, measures, hierarchies, relationships, and reusable analytical logic.
  • Establish consistent definitions for key Corporate Accounts metrics and ensure that business logic is implemented consistently across reporting experiences.
  • Partner with data engineering teams to improve source data quality, model scalability, refresh reliability, governance, and platform performance.
  • Identify opportunities to consolidate semantic models, rationalize overlapping reporting assets, remove technical debt, and simplify the Corporate Accounts BI architecture.
  • Design analytical assets to support natural-language querying, Copilot-enabled experiences, agentic analytics, and other AI-driven analytical scenarios.
  • Ensure semantic models contain the appropriate definitions, metadata, relationships, descriptions, and business context required for both human and AI consumption.
  • Support certification of data assets and semantic models for enterprise use, ensuring they are trusted, governed, documented, and discoverable.
  • Monitor and continuously improve model performance, scalability, usability, and reliability.

Data Analysis & Business Evaluation

  • Analyze Corporate Accounts performance across multiple data sources to identify customer, product, sales, and execution trends.
  • Investigate performance changes and determine the underlying drivers behind business results.
  • Conduct deeper analysis where existing BI views identify potential risks, opportunities, or areas requiring further investigation.
  • Evaluate the impact of business initiatives, investments, programs, and changes in execution.
  • Develop repeatable analytical approaches rather than relying on one-time analyses.
  • Convert analysis into clear recommendations that business leaders can act upon.
  • Connect detailed analytical findings to broader Corporate Accounts and Azure business outcomes.

Stakeholder Partnership & Influence

  • Build trusted relationships across Corporate Accounts leadership, Finance, Strategy, Sales Excellence, Operations, Engineering, and Analytics organizations.
  • Work directly with business stakeholders to understand the decisions they need to make and determine the analytical capabilities required to support those decisions.
  • Challenge unclear or inconsistent metric definitions and help establish common analytical standards.
  • Translate complex business questions into data requirements, semantic model requirements, KPIs, and analytical experiences.
  • Communicate analytical findings and technical concepts effectively to both business and technical audiences.
  • Influence decisions through business understanding, analytical rigor, and fact-based recommendations.

Analytics Excellence & Innovation

  • Promote consistent analytics practices across Corporate Accounts, including metric governance, reporting standards, documentation, testing, and quality assurance.
  • Identify and eliminate duplicated or low-value reporting while increasing reuse of trusted semantic models and common analytical components.
  • Automate recurring analytical processes and reduce manual reporting wherever practical.
  • Evaluate new Microsoft Fabric, Power BI, Copilot, and AI capabilities and apply them where they materially improve the Corporate Accounts analytics experience.
  • Support SME&C’s broader AI-first analytics strategy by ensuring Corporate Accounts data and semantic models can be safely consumed by both traditional BI and emerging AI experiences.

Qualifications

Business Analytics & BI Expertise

  • Experience building business intelligence solutions using Power BI, including dashboards, scorecards, executive reporting, and interactive analytical experiences.
  • Analytical and problem-solving skills with demonstrated ability to convert complex business questions into analytical solutions.
  • Experience working with sales, commercial, finance, operations, or customer performance data.
  • Demonstrated ability to move beyond reporting results to explain why performance is changing and what actions should be considered.
  • Experience translating business requirements into scalable analytical products rather than standalone reports.
  • Ability to independently own BI solutions from requirements through development, validation, deployment, and ongoing improvement.

Corporate / Cloud Business Performance

  • Experience supporting sales operations, business operations, finance, strategy, performance management, or commercial organizations.
  • Understanding of business performance measurement, KPI design, pipeline and execution metrics, and executive reporting frameworks.
  • Experience analyzing customer, product, revenue, consumption, pipeline, or sales performance.
  • Experience with cloud, Azure, enterprise software, or technology-industry business models is preferred.
  • Ability to connect operational and sales indicators to broader business outcomes.

Data Architecture & Analytics Engineering

  • Hands-on experience designing and maintaining Power BI semantic models and enterprise analytical solutions.
  • Understanding of dimensional modeling, star schemas, relationships, measures, hierarchies, and semantic layer design.
  • Experience with DAX and SQL and the ability to independently investigate and validate data.
  • Experience building or optimizing solutions using Power BI and Microsoft Fabric.
  • Experience working with large or complex datasets and optimizing models for performance, usability, and scalability.
  • Understanding of data pipelines, data transformation, data quality, lineage, governance, and certification.
  • Experience consolidating fragmented semantic models or reporting solutions into reusable analytical foundations.
  • Understanding of how semantic models, metadata, business definitions, and data quality enable Copilot, natural-language analytics, and AI-agent scenarios.

Data Storytelling & Communication.

  • Ability to explain complex analytical findings in simple business terms.
  • Experience creating executive-ready scorecards, presentations, and analytical narratives.
  • Ability to distinguish between reporting a metric and explaining the business drivers behind it.
  • Ability to communicate effectively with both technical teams and business stakeholders.

Collaboration & Execution

  • Proven ability to work across business, analytics, engineering, and operations organizations.
  • Ability to independently manage BI products and analytical workstreams from definition through delivery.
  • Prioritization and execution skills with the ability to balance business urgency with long-term architectural quality.
  • Comfortable working in an environment where business priorities and analytical requirements evolve rapidly.
  • Demonstrated focus on quality, accuracy, scalability, and user experience.

  • Master's Degree in Mathematics, Analytics, Engineering, Computer Science, Marketing, Business, Economics or related field AND 3+ years experience in data analysis and reporting, business intelligence, or business and financial analysis OR Bachelor's Degree in Statistics, Finance, Mathematics, Analytics, Engineering, Computer Science, Marketing, Business, Economics or related field AND 4+ years experience in data analysis and reporting, business intelligence, or business and financial analysis OR equivalent experience.

Additional or preferred qualifications

  • Master's Degree in Mathematics, Analytics, Engineering, Computer Science, Marketing, Business, Economics or related field AND 6+ years experience in data analysis and reporting, business intelligence, or business and financial analysis OR Bachelor's Degree in Statistics, Finance, Mathematics, Analytics, Engineering, Computer Science, Marketing, Business, Economics or related field AND 8+ years experience in data analysis and reporting, business intelligence, or business and financial analysis OR equivalent experience.

Call for Machine Learning, AI, & Statistics Researchers at Microsoft Research New England 

Microsoft Research New England in Cambridge, Massachusetts, is seeking candidates for full-time Principal Researcher positions in artificial intelligence, machine learning, and related areas.  If your research background is in these fields or a related one, we would like to hear from you!   

 

Microsoft Research offers a supportive environment for cutting-edge theoretical and applied research across disciplines. Current areas of focus at MSR NE include the science of deep learning and generative AI, post-training, data curation and synthesis, test-time scaling, and new model architectures and training paradigms; these themes are illustrative rather than exhaustive. Researchers benefit from access to a wide range of large and small data sources, an open publication policy, and close connections with leading academic institutions. We seek candidates who can define and pursue an independent research program and who have demonstrated research impact through a strong publication record at leading venues. 

Microsoft Research New England brings together full-time researchers, postdoctoral researchers, data scientists, engineers, and program managers working across machine learning, statistics, healthcare, computational biology, theoretical computer science, algorithmic game theory, economics, and other disciplines. The lab fosters collaboration across fields and maintains active connections with the academic and technology communities in the Cambridge and Boston area. 

 

We are committed to building an inclusive, diverse, and pluralistic research environment. In keeping with this, Microsoft Research New England is a place where all are able to do their very best work.

Our mission is to make Windows the best platform for AI development and deployment, enabling efficient execution of machine learning workloads across CPUs, GPUs, and NPUs from a broad ecosystem of silicon partners. CGC sits at the heart of the Windows ML ecosystem, powering experiences used by millions of developers and customers worldwide.
 
Our technologies enable computer vision, audio, video, gaming, and generative AI workloads across the Windows platform, including emerging AI-first experiences and next-generation Copilot+ PC capabilities. As AI becomes a fundamental platform shift, CGC is responsible for the compiler infrastructure, optimization frameworks, execution engines, and hardware abstractions that unlock the performance and efficiency of modern AI accelerators. We work closely with Microsoft AI platform teams, hardware partners, and operating system components to define the future of AI execution on Windows.

Microsoft Silicon, Cloud Hardware, and Infrastructure Engineering (SCHIE) is the team behind Microsoft’s expanding Cloud Infrastructure and responsible for powering Microsoft’s “Intelligent Cloud” mission. SCHIE delivers the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's over 200 online businesses including Bing, MSN, Office 365, Xbox Live, Teams, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform globally with our server and data center infrastructure, security and compliance, operations, globalization, and manageability solutions. Our focus is on smart growth, high efficiency, and delivering a trusted experience to customers and partners worldwide and we are looking for passionate engineers to help achieve that mission. 

As Microsoft's cloud business continues to grow the ability to deploy new offerings and hardware infrastructure on time, in high volume with high quality and lowest cost is of paramount importance. To achieve this goal, the Cloud Hardware Systems Engineering (CHSE) team is instrumental in defining and delivering operational measures of success for hardware manufacturing, improving the planning process, quality, delivery, scale and sustainability related to Microsoft cloud hardware. We are looking for engineers with a dedicated passion for customer focused solutions, insight and industry knowledge to envision and implement future technical solutions that will manage and optimize the Cloud infrastructure.  

We are seeking a Principal Optical Engineer to lead the implementation, integration, qualification, and high-volume deployment of optical interconnect solutions for Microsoft cloud and AI infrastructure. Working in partnership with platform and optical architecture teams, this role translates approved architectures and technology selections into module, fiber, connector, rack-integration, supplier, validation, and manufacturing requirements and drives them from product definition through fleet deployment. 

#SCHIE 



Responsibilities
  • Partner with platform and optical architecture teams to translate approved optical architectures and technology selections into deployable product requirements, interfaces, acceptance criteria, and implementation plans. 
  • Own product-level requirements and tradeoffs for optical modules and engines, fiber assemblies, connectors, fiber-management systems, and rack-level optical paths across performance, power, thermal constraints, reliability, serviceability, manufacturability, cost, schedule, and supply continuity.
  • Drive optical interconnect productization from product definition through design maturity, prototype integration, interoperability, qualification, production release, manufacturing ramp, and fleet deployment.
  • Lead cross-functional implementation and design reviews spanning optics, electrical interfaces, SI/PI, mechanical tolerances, thermal integration, firmware and telemetry, rack integration, validation, reliability, manufacturing, and serviceability.
  • Define and drive component-, module-, assembly-, rack-, and system-level validation, qualification, reliability, inspection, and production-test strategies with evidence-based coverage and exit criteria.
  • Lead resolution of complex module-, fiber-, connector-, rack-, manufacturing-, and field-level issues by organizing cross-team debug, correlating supplier and system data, and driving verified corrective and preventive actions.
  • Provide technical direction to optical-module, fiber, cable, connector, ODM, contract-manufacturing, and test-equipment partners; establish deliverables, design-review criteria, quality expectations, yield targets, escalation paths, and readiness gates.
  • Drive supplier selection and production readiness across design maturity, DFM/DFT/DFR, process capability, yield, quality, cost, capacity, continuity of supply, and change control. \
  • Identify productization and deployment risks early, communicate options and consequences to senior stakeholders, and drive decisions that balance performance, reliability, serviceability, schedule, cost, and fleet-scale operability.
  • Mentor engineers and create reusable implementation specifications, qualification methods, manufacturing controls, supplier scorecards, design guides, and lessons learned across optical-interconnect programs. 


Qualifications

Required Qualifications

  • Master's Degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related field AND 7+ years technical engineering experience
    • OR Bachelor's Degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or related field AND 8+ years technical engineering experience
    • OR equivalent experience

Other Requirements:

  • Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to, the following specialized security screenings:
    • Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Optical Engineering, Photonics, Electrical Engineering, Physics, or a related field and 10+ years of technical engineering experience, or equivalent experience.
  • 10+ years of experience developing and delivering optical modules, fiber assemblies, connectors, fiber-management systems, or rack-level optical interconnects across the hardware product lifecycle.
  • Experience leading optical hardware implementation, integration, validation, qualification, manufacturing readiness, and production deployment for complex cloud, networking, or AI infrastructure.
  • Experience providing technical leadership across internal organizations and external module, cable, connector, ODM, contract-manufacturing, or test partners.
  • Experience productizing high-speed optical modules, optical engines, fiber assemblies, connector systems, or rack-scale optical interconnects for cloud, networking, or AI infrastructure.
  • Knowledge of pluggable, near-packaged, or co-packaged optical solutions sufficient to translate architecture interfaces into implementable module, fiber, connector, thermal, mechanical, telemetry, and serviceability requirements.
  • Experience with 112G/224G-class electrical interfaces, PAM4 optical links, link budgets, FEC considerations, interoperability, and end-to-end system margin analysis.
  • Deep knowledge of fiber-optic connector and fiber-management technologies, including MPO, MMC, LC, lensed or expanded-beam interfaces, blind-mate designs, routing, cleaning, inspection, and high-density rack integration.
  • Hands-on experience with optical and high-speed electrical characterization, system bring-up, margin analysis, and correlation of supplier data, laboratory measurements, and production results.
  • Experience defining DVT, qualification, reliability, inspection, production-test, DOE, FMEA, process-capability, yield, and quality-control plans for high-volume optical hardware.
  • Experience directing optical-module, fiber, cable, connector, ODM, contract-manufacturing, and test-equipment partners across design maturity, cost, quality, capacity, supply continuity, change control, and ramp.

Our mission is to build and ship the products we love. 

The Americas Sales & Operations Execution Manager role will have end-to-end responsibility for the management of the Surface Devices and Accessories Consumer business for all regions. Key responsibilities include managing stakeholder relationships across the Devices Supply Chain, Finance and Sales Operations organizations. The role will lead the demand and supply planning processes, aligning them with product strategy and financial plans to ensure our field teams can provide retail partners with reliable product availability.

You will demonstrate proven skills in managing complex internal and external relationships and demonstrate experience in leading strategic projects from requirements to implementation. Solid verbal and written communication skills, leadership and analytical thinking are also necessary to have the right level of impact and influence.

The S&OE partners closely with supply chain leads, Finance, Category leads and customer operations teams to identify inefficiencies, surface risks, build scalable reporting frameworks, and support scenario-based planning that enables resilient and efficient supply chain performance

In qualità di Tecnico Senior degli Ambienti Critici (CET) nel team Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) di Microsoft, ti occuperai della manutenzione dell’infrastruttura critica che garantisce il funzionamento dei nostri data center. Le tue mansioni potranno spaziare dal coordinamento con fornitori e venditori, alla stretta collaborazione con la direzione per affrontare situazioni operative, di rischio e di sicurezza, alla formazione di altri tecnici CE, fino alla comprensione pratica del funzionamento delle apparecchiature degli ambienti critici, all’esecuzione di vari tipi di manutenzione, alla gestione degli incidenti in loco in coordinamento con altri professionisti delle strutture critiche e all’utilizzo della telemetria e di altre piattaforme per monitorare le prestazioni e il funzionamento delle apparecchiature.Il team Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) di Microsoft è il motore che alimenta i nostri servizi cloud. In qualità di tecnico degli ambienti critici CO+I, ricoprirai un ruolo chiave nella fornitura dell’infrastruttura di base e delle tecnologie fondamentali per i servizi online di Microsoft, tra cui Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive e la piattaforma Microsoft Azure. Come gruppo, CO+I è incentrato sullo sviluppo personale e professionale di tutti i dipendenti e offre formazione e opportunità, tra cui programmi di rotazione professionale, formazione ed eventi su diversità e inclusione, nonché certificazioni professionali.La nostra infrastruttura è costituita da un ampio portafoglio globale di oltre 200 data center in 32 paesi e milioni di server. The cloudOS System Software Engineering team is at the forefront of developing secure server software and is responsible for building the Apple Silicon server platform that powers Private Cloud Compute. We own the trust boundary between the physical hardware in our data centers and the services that run on it: before a node can serve a user request, we cryptographically prove its authenticity and integrity. We are looking for an exceptional security engineer with experience architecting and developing low-level, secure software to build new technologies to support Apple’s product security and customer privacy principles.

In this role, you will be part of a team that builds and maintains system software such as kernel drivers, runtime libraries, frameworks, and daemons, and you will own the attestation architecture for the server platform. You will bring new chassis designs into attestation from the ground up, defining what is measured, how component identities are sealed during manufacturing, and how they are verified after deployment. And you will build the services that turn those measurements into one authoritative answer to whether every machine in our data centers is in a known good state.

The right candidate will have a successful track record of securing compute platforms and building end-to-end security solutions. You should have a strong mix of educational and practical experience, be comfortable working from silicon and firmware up through the services that verify them, and have a passion for diving head first into challenging problems.

Description

You will work cross-functionally with security teams throughout Apple as well as system software, platform design, SOC architects, manufacturing, data center operations, and cloud services teams to develop and integrate best in class hardware, software, and services. You will be responsible for the security of the platform that powers the next generation of data centers.

This position requires someone with strong technical strengths and an enthusiastic drive to secure systems by showing how they can be broken. Our controls have to hold against a remote attacker and against someone with physical access to a chassis who wants a modified machine to look genuine.

We are a dynamic, growing team spanning many disciplines, and we expect members to be willing to step out of their comfort zones to contribute to team objectives. A successful engineer in this role is one that is happy to have a wide breadth of influence as well as deep focus areas in the context of a rapidly evolving project.

Responsibilities

Own the attestation architecture and strategy for the server platform, and extend the chassis attestation chain to every component that carries firmware.
Bring new chassis designs into attestation from the ground up, working with silicon, platform design, and manufacturing partners to define measurements, seal component identities into a signed manifest, and verify them in the field.
Develop the on-node attestation software, and partner with the teams building the services that verify its results continuously across the fleet.
Review code and designs, document end-to-end security models, and perform security assessments on systems software and services.

Minimum Qualifications

7+ years of experience.
Proficiency in C/C++.
Background in developing and maintaining code security-critical codebases.
Understanding of applied cryptography, cryptography hardware, and key management, including PKI and HSM-backed certificate issuance.
Experience with mutual authentication and hardware-based attestation, including Secure Boot, firmware measurement, and challenge-response protocols.
Strong understanding of hardware/software interactions and low-level software.

Preferred Qualifications

Background in definition and design of secure embedded systems, and in bringing new hardware platforms from manufacturing into production.
Experience with server component firmware, such as ARM SoC architecture, baseboard management controllers, system-management microcontrollers, and power delivery.
Understanding of past, current, and emerging security exploit types targeting low-level systems, including physical and insider attacks on data center hardware.
Experience building and operating production services that verify security posture across a large fleet and detect drift over time.
Experience with Swift, Objective-C, and Apple development tools.

Future AR and VR devices occupy ever-smaller, glasses-like form factors and thus require ever-tighter power budgets. At the same time, we require higher-quality passthrough rendering and scene understanding. In particular, depth estimation, which reconstructs scene geometry in real time from sensor signals, is one of the biggest power consumers in AR and VR devices. However, most existing work targets datacenter GPUs, or at best mobile silicon with an order of magnitude more power headroom than what glasses form factors allow. Reality Labs is Meta's innovation engine for next-generation AR/VR and wearable technology and XR Graphics is involved in building the next-generation imaging and reconstruction stack that closes this gap. We are looking for a Research Scientist Intern to work on low-power real-time reconstruction of scene geometry for AR/VR. Today, VR passthrough, hand interaction, and environment understanding run on separate pipelines, each tuned for different accuracy, latency and power target. We are interested in deduplicating the compute (and thus reducing power): - What is the right depth estimation and processing strategy, from the ground up, for a glasses power budget? - Can we train a single lightweight scene representation that can serve passthrough, hand occlusions, and background occlusions simultaneously? These are open questions, and you would help define the approach. This is a research internship. You will own a genuinely open problem, choose the methods, build the evaluation, and present your results, with support for publication where the work warrants it.

Responsibilities

  • Plan and execute research to advance the state of the art in low-power, real-time scene reconstruction for AR/VR — spanning depth estimation, occlusion, and geometric scene understanding.
  • Explore the extent to which a shared, learned scene representation can serve multiple downstream consumers at different latency and accuracy points.
  • Define evaluation methodology and run experiments measuring geometric accuracy, temporal stability, rendering distortion, latency, and compute and power cost on real multi-sensor device captures.
  • Collaborate with researchers and engineers across the passthrough, scene understanding, and on-device compute teams to assess feasibility within headset and glasses power envelopes.
  • Document and present findings, and contribute to publications and patents where the results warrant it.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Currently has, or is in the process of obtaining, a PhD degree in the domain of computer vision, machine learning, computer graphics, robotics, or a related technical field
  • Must obtain work authorization in the country of employment at the time of hire, and maintain ongoing work authorization during employment
  • Knowledge and hands-on experience in at least one of: depth or stereo estimation, 3D reconstruction (TSDF, implicit or neural fields, Gaussian splatting), video or instance segmentation, or neural scene representations
  • Experience designing and running quantitative experiments, and communicating technical results

Preferred Qualifications

  • Intent to return to a degree-program after the completion of the internship
  • Proven track record of achieving significant results as demonstrated by grants, fellowships, patents, as well as first-authored publications at leading workshops or conferences such as CVPR/ECCV/ICCV, SIGGRAPH/SIGGRAPH Asia, 3DV, ICLR, NeurIPS, etc
  • Experience with efficient or on-device inference: quantization, distillation, pruning, or deployment to mobile NPU, DSP or GPU targets
  • Experience with multi-sensor fusion across heterogeneous sensors — RGB, IR/CV cameras, time-of-flight — including camera calibration and cross-sensor registration
  • Experience with temporal filtering and state estimation over scene state
  • Familiarity with AR/VR passthrough, reprojection, occlusion rendering, or SLAM and scene reconstruction
  • Experience with C++, and with profiling or optimizing real-time computer vision or graphics pipelines
  • Experience working in a Unix environment
  • Experience reasoning about compute and power budgets as a first-class design constraint

Agios is a full stack research organization within Reality Labs Research, spanning materials and manufacturing, sensors and actuators, simulation, and learned control. Our mission is to build systems that enhance human capabilities through intelligent machine collaboration. Today that work centers on what we call the last bottleneck: AI has compressed the digital side of research and development, while the physical side still moves at human speed. Dexterous Manipulation is the pillar attacking that problem directly, pairing a custom dexterous robotic hand with in-house wearable sensing, high accuracy simulation, and glove-driven teleoperation. As a Research Scientist Intern, you will work at the intersection of robot learning, dexterous control, and human-to-robot transfer, with mentors who span hardware, simulation, controls, and policy learning. Your focus will be learned models that turn human demonstration data into executable robot behavior, covering retargeting, manipulation policies, and teleoperation. Our internships are twelve (12) to twenty-four (24) weeks long and we have various start dates throughout the year.

  • Develop representations that fuse multimodal human and robot data, including video, hand pose, tactile and contact force, and IMU, into a shared action space.
  • Construct data collection pipelines and benchmarks for dexterous manipulation, including held-out and out-of-distribution protocols that test generalization across objects, motions, and embodiments.

The Meta Reality Labs Research Team brings together a world-class team of researchers, developers, and engineers to create the future of virtual and augmented reality, which together will become as universal and essential as smartphones and personal computers are today. Just as personal computers have done over the past 45 years, AR, VR and MR will ultimately change everything about how we work, play, and connect. We are developing all the technologies needed to enable breakthrough AR glasses and VR headsets, including optics and displays, computer vision, audio, graphics, brain-computer interfaces, haptic interaction, eye/hand/face/body tracking, perception science, and true telepresence. Some of those will advance much faster than others, but they all need to happen to enable AR, VR and MR that are so compelling that they become an integral part of our lives. In particular, the Meta Reality Labs Research Audio team is focused on two goals; creating virtual sounds that are perceptually indistinguishable from reality and redefining the human hearing. These two initiatives will allow us to connect people by allowing them to feel together despite being physically apart and allow them to converse in even the most difficult listening environments. The Devices and Hardware Research team of the Reality Labs Research Audio is looking for innovative PhD student interns interested in one or more of the following areas: > Electrophysiological and bio-signal sensing technologies and the associated signal processing — EEG, EMG, EOG, ECG, PPG, EDA, and other wearable biopotential/physiological modalities, including electrode and front-end design, artifact rejection, and robust on-body signal quality. > Extremely low-power, energy-autonomous wearable design — sub-milliwatt and duty-cycled sensing architectures, analog/mixed-signal front ends, event-driven and always-on wake-up circuits, and self-powered operation via energy harvesting. > Embedded real-time signal processing on resource-constrained hardware — ANC, echo cancellation, hear-through, adaptive filtering, and efficient implementations on MCUs and DSPs. > Hearing biomechanics characterized through experimentation and numerical simulation. > Conventional and ML-based signal processing — feature extraction, classification, regression and event detection, sequence/temporal modeling, self-supervised and transfer learning for scarce physiological labels, subject-independent generalization and calibration, sensor fusion across modalities, and on-device/TinyML inference (quantization, pruning, distillation) under tight compute and energy budgets. Meta runs one of the largest server fleets on earth, and every product bet (AI training, ranking, inference, storage) turns into a demand for compute that we must forecast, shape, and match to a physical supply of servers, racks, power, and data center space. As a technical owner within Server Demand Planning, you drive server demand forecasting and demand-supply matching for your area and close on feasible supply requirements: you forecast near- and long-term server capacity demand by rack/hardware type and region, and you build the operations research models that match that demand to supply so we land the right long-term DC & hardware infra requirements, in the right place, at the right time. You choose the right modeling approach for the problems you own, deciding when to ship a production-grade optimization system versus a fast lightweight model to unblock a decision, and you partner closely across product/service capacity owners, capacity engineering, supply chain, data center planning, and finance.

Responsibilities

  • Own and drive a multi-horizon server/MW demand forecast (near term through 2-5+ years), producing trusted, reproducible release to inform decisions
  • Aggregate and normalize demand signals from short-term demand and product groups into a single trusted statistical long-term demand plan
  • Formulate and solve the demand-supply matching problem using operations-research models that reconcile forecasted demand with hardware roadmaps, cooling, lead times, and power constraints to inform the Plan of Record
  • Build across the full modeling spectrum: production-grade optimization and forecasting systems and prototype models and heuristics that answer a leadership question or unblock a decision
  • Partner with IDC engineering, site selection, and hardware strategy teams to align next-generation data center designs, rack sizing, and hardware roadmaps with demand, eliminating stranded power, cooling, and space capacity

Minimum Qualifications

  • 6+ years applying operations research / management science to real planning problems in demand planning, capacity planning, supply-demand matching, network optimization, or inventory
  • Deep operations-research toolkit: mathematical optimization (LP, MILP, stochastic/robust optimization), simulation, queuing theory, and probabilistic/statistical forecasting
  • Demonstrated ability to build BOTH production-grade models/systems (deployed, maintained, driving real decisions) AND lightweight/prototype models delivered fast under ambiguity
  • Experience with demand-to-supply matching: reconciling forecasted demand against constrained supply, lead times, and inventory
  • Fluency with optimization solvers (Gurobi, CPLEX, Xpress, or OR-Tools) and with SQL + Python for modeling, analysis, and pipelines

Preferred Qualifications

  • Direct experience with server/compute or data center capacity planning at hyperscale
  • PhD in Operations Research, Industrial Engineering, Management Science, or a related quantitative field
  • Experience with planning platforms (Kinaxis, SAP IBP, o9, Blue Yonder, Demantra, E2open) and internal capacity tools (MCP/ICPC, Capacity Explorer)
  • Statistical/ML forecasting depth (time series, hierarchical/probabilistic forecasting, forecast reconciliation)
  • Publications, patents, or recognized technical leadership in OR / optimization / forecasting

About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

As a Federal Civilian Account Executive at Anthropic, you'll drive the adoption of safe, frontier AI across federal civilian agencies. You'll leverage your deep understanding of federal civilian operations and consultative sales expertise to propel revenue growth while becoming a trusted partner to customers, helping them embed and deploy AI while uncovering its full range of capabilities. In collaboration with GTM, product, and marketing teams, you'll help refine our approach to the federal civilian market while maintaining the highest standards of security and compliance.

Responsibilities:

  • Drive new business and revenue growth specifically within federal civilian agencies, owning the full sales cycle from initial outreach through deployment
  • Navigate the unique requirements of federal civilian procurement, including FAR compliance, security standards, and agency-specific regulations
  • Build and maintain relationships with key decision-makers across federal civilian agencies, becoming a trusted advisor on AI capabilities and implementation
  • Develop and execute strategic account plans that align with agency missions and modernization initiatives
  • Coordinate closely with cloud service providers (AWS, GCP) and system integrators to ensure successful deployment and integration
  • Provide detailed market intelligence and customer feedback to product teams to ensure our offerings meet federal civilian requirements
  • Create and maintain sales playbooks specific to federal civilian use cases and procurement processes
  • Take a leadership role in growing our federal civilian presence while maintaining hands-on engagement with key accounts
  • Collaborate across teams to ensure coordinated delivery of commitments and maintain appropriate documentation of customer engagements

You may be a good fit if you have:

  • 8+ years of enterprise sales experience in the federal civilian space, with a proven track record of driving adoption of emerging technologies
  • A deep understanding of federal civilian agency missions, challenges, and technology needs
  • Demonstrated the ability to balance strategic leadership with hands-on sales execution
  • Experience navigating complex federal procurement processes and compliance requirements
  • A strong track record of exceeding revenue targets in the federal civilian space
  • Extensive experience with federal civilian contracting vehicles and procurement mechanisms
  • Excellent relationship-building skills across all levels, from technical teams to senior agency leadership
  • A proven ability to coordinate across multiple stakeholders, including cloud providers and system integrators
  • Strategic thinking combined with attention to detail in execution
  • A passion for safe and ethical AI development, with the ability to articulate its importance in government contexts

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. 

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$380,000—$450,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed.  Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

This role will be dynamic and full of new engagement, challenges, and opportunities to bring the core elements of success for a calibration program - measuring the process, managing tracking software, schedules, accuracy & precision of equipment, equipment history, traceability methods, accreditation and reporting.  As Anduril grows, the role and support around calibration will grow too. If you are someone who has passion for the quality of their work, is hands-on with engineering, production, and vendors, and be accountable for calibration results, then this role is for you.


WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Analyze & drive improvements in the core calibration activities for calibrated devices. 
  • Define new project milestones, develop detailed execution plans, and monitor progress to meet deadlines and quality standards for enhancements to the quality management system.
  • Develop In-House Calibration Roadmap: Create and implement a strategic plan to analyze the calibration processes and optimize for work done with external vendors or in-house capabilities.
  • Evaluate and implement new technologies and methods to improve calibration efficiency and effectiveness.
  • Manage the database and ensure that it is updated when appropriate, including but not limited to updating location and owners of tools.
  • Improve processes to ensuring that equipment rotations do not starve users or production.
  • Improve the existing infrastructure for equipment flagged for calibration (i.e. Drop location for assets requiring calibration, standardization of calibration intake information, providing instructions for 3rd party vendor)

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience managing calibration at a large organization and production environment
  • Experience working with and managing 3rd party calibration vendors
  • Experience with automated calibration tools and software.
  • Experience improving processes and procedures (specifically around calibration) with an emphasis on process creation.
  • Familiar with common industry calibration standards and methods
  • Proven track record of designing and delivering calibration systems for manufacturing facilities.
  • In-depth knowledge of AS9100 and AS6500 standards and their application in calibration processes.
  • Strong leadership, project management, and problem-solving skills across multiple sites.
  • Excellent communication and collaboration abilities.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Quality Management, or a related field.

  • Experience with developing In-house calibration process

ABOUT THE JOB

Anduril's Space Manufacturing team is seeking a hands-on Cleanroom Lead to join our team. The Space Manufacturing team is responsible for the assembly, integration, and test of ground support equipment, PCBA, unit-level, and integrated systems that are vital for our aerospace and defense operations. This role keeps the day-to-day operation, readiness, and discipline of our Space Manufacturing lab spaces running across three locations — our operational space lab, the temporary cleanroom now being built, and the new facility (graded ISO 5–8) now being built to support development and low-rate builds of spaceflight hardware.


This is a working, hands-on role — you are the person on the floor who keeps the labs and cleanrooms running. You will personally maintain and troubleshoot lab equipment and facility systems, run the gowning and contamination-control routines, handle consumables and material flow, support safety and hazardous-material handling, and keep each space ready for build and test. You will coordinate vendors and specialists for work beyond your scope, and over time you may help bring on and guide additional technicians as the sites scale — but the core of this job is doing the hands-on work yourself to keep demanding lab and cleanroom environments operating to spec, in a fast-paced, resource-limited environment. If you are someone who likes to roll up your sleeves and be the person the floor relies on, this role is for you.

WHAT YOU’LL DO 

  • Keep the three Space Manufacturing lab spaces — the space lab, the temporary cleanroom (under construction), and the new facility (under construction) — running day-to-day, including gowning/anterooms, air showers, test bays, subassembly and assembly zones, and storage, so build and test run without facility-driven downtime.
  • Perform hands-on maintenance, troubleshooting, and repair of lab equipment and critical components, and coordinate specialists or vendors for work beyond your scope to keep equipment available through regularly scheduled maintenance.
  • Run the day-to-day contamination-control routines for each cleanroom (graded ISO 5–8): gowning and air-shower discipline, particle monitoring, supporting certification cadence, and keeping consumables (garments, gloves, wipes) stocked and flowing.
  • Operate and maintain cleanroom and facility support systems hands-on — HVAC/air conditioning, environmental monitoring, compressed and specialty gases (including nitrogen purge), pumps, chillers, compressors, and DI water systems — taking readings, servicing on schedule, and coordinating vendors for larger work.
  • Serve as the day-to-day, floor-level safety point of contact: follow and enforce safe work practices, handle and store hazardous materials and specialty gases safely, ensure safety instructions are in place before hazardous lab work begins, and support EHS on chemical handling, permits, and inspections.
  • Manage lab equipment, assets, and material flow: tool/fixture check-in/check-out and asset tracking, calibration/metrology scheduling (in-house and via vendors), preventive maintenance, and receiving/kitting/stores/consumables flow in coordination with supply chain and quality.
  • Keep each space audit-ready: maintain cleanroom operating procedures, gowning and contamination-control work instructions, safety procedures, and certification/monitoring records.
  • Support the stand-up and transition of work into the new facility as it comes online — help set up new areas, move and install equipment, and support the wind-down of temporary space as capability moves.
  • Partner day-to-day with AI&T, manufacturing engineering, and program teams to keep work and WIP moving across the sites, and communicate statuses, issues, and suggestions clearly.
  • Over time, help onboard and guide additional technicians/specialists as the sites scale (potential growth into a team-lead/people-manager scope).

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS 

  • 4+ years of hands-on experience maintaining and operating lab, cleanroom, or manufacturing facility equipment and systems in a controlled production or lab environment.
  • Hands-on experience with mechanical, electrical, and facility-systems — experience with diagnosing, maintaining, repairing, and troubleshooting equipment and building/lab systems (e.g., HVAC/air conditioning, pumps, chillers, compressors, DI water), and reading and interpreting procedures, manuals, and instructions.
  • 2+ years of hands-on experience working in or supporting an ISO-classified cleanroom (ISO 5–8 or equivalent) or other contamination-controlled environment, including gowning and cleanliness discipline.
  • Hands-on safety experience with hazardous-material and compressed/specialty-gas handling and storage, including serving as a floor- or lab-level safety point of contact.
  • Experience maintaining lab equipment and supporting calibration/metrology scheduling, preventive maintenance, and inventory/consumables flow to keep equipment available and reduce downtime.
  • High school diploma or equivalent; technical training, trade certifications, military technical experience, or equivalent hands-on experience.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.
  • In this role, you will be subject to pre-employment and randomized substance screening, as required by the Company.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 

  • Hands-on experience in aerospace, defense, semiconductor, medical-device, or optics/sensor manufacturing, including support of prototype or flight-hardware testing.
  • Familiarity with ISO 5 (Class 100) operations and ESD precautions and cleanliness requirements for sensitive hardware.
  • Experience helping stand up or set up a new lab or cleanroom, including equipment moves, installation, and setup.
  • Hands-on experience with specialty-gas and pressure systems (e.g., regulators, pressure relief valves, nitrogen purge, gloveboxes) and hazardous-waste handling/recycling programs.
  • Prior experience as a team lead or supervising/scheduling a small facilities/technician team (growth path toward people-management).
  • Strong organization, multitasking, and documentation discipline, comfortable in a fast-paced, resource-limited environment.
  • Active U.S. Secret or Top Secret security clearance.

Anduril is building the future of defense technology, and a critical component of this mission is a trusted, unified, and intelligently structured data foundation. We are seeking a technically capable and investigative Master Data Management Analyst to ensure our master data is accurate, governed, and trusted at the source. Reporting to the Master Data Management Lead, this role sits within the MDM Center of Excellence and is focused on data quality investigation, root-cause analysis, governance operationalization, and business enablement within the MDM domain.

You will be the person who assists in root-causing data quality issues, determining whether the problem is a source system issue (e.g., ERP, PLM, CRM, MES), process gap, or a transformation logic issue in the analytics pipeline. You will populate and maintain MDM metadata (RACI, ownership, SLAs, critical attributes) within our semantic layer platform in partnership with business domain stewards who own their data within their functional orgs while operating within MDM's governance framework. You will also partner with analytics engineering teams by reading their transformation code to validate data lineage and quality, ensuring what's built matches golden record rules and critical attribute definitions established through the MDM Center of Excellence. You will also contribute to the semantic layer's design and data definitions from an MDM perspective, ensuring that golden record standards, business definitions, and governance requirements are reflected in ontology objects and semantic models.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Operationalize MDM Governance & Enable Business Stewards: Populate and maintain MDM metadata within the semantic layer platform in partnership with business domain stewards, including RACI ownership fields, critical attribute definitions, data quality SLAs, and stewardship assignments. Establish realistic quality thresholds and monitor adherence, notifying responsible parties when metrics fall below acceptable levels. Train functional data stewards on what MDM governance means tactically for their domain, including their RACI responsibilities, how to maintain data quality at the source, what SLAs they are accountable for, and how to use governance tooling to self-monitor. Support the definition of golden record rules, critical attribute lists, and cross-domain governance standards through the CoE, helping drive alignment when competing definitions arise across business domains.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Discovery is Anduril's team for the hard concepts: the ones that are not yet proven or built. We take the newest and hardest problems across space, missiles, air, sensors, autonomy, and cyber, decide what is worth building, and prove it out: we build the models, break the assumptions, run the tests, and carry what works to the point where a program can pick it up. We work with hardware and software engineering teams across the company, driving cross-functional collaboration across different business lines. 

ABOUT THE JOB

We are building an expeditionary force: a small group of engineers who want to do big, new, hard things and who move into unfamiliar territory as a matter of course. As Deputy Chief Engineer in Discovery, you lead the technical work on concepts nobody has proven, usually several at once. You learn whatever domain each one lives in and build the thing that tests it: the prototype, the test article, the demonstration. Analysis gets a concept to the point where it is worth building; building it is how we find out. You are the technical authority for the concepts you own: you set the approach, review the work, and decide, on the evidence, which concepts continue and which stop. The problems change; the approach does not: reason from first principles, build it, test it, and reach a solution.

You are not hired for a particular skill set. You are hired for a record of building things: taking a concept from an idea to hardware or software that works, across different areas, and getting to solutions. You are also the adversary to our own ideas. The rigor that validates a good concept is the same rigor that kills a bad one early, while it is still cheap, and you apply it to your own work first.

This is a hands-on technical leadership role on both internally and externally funded programs within Anduril's Discovery Business Line, on operationally relevant timelines.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Own new concepts from first idea through analysis, prototype, and test, and drive them to a validated answer
  • Learn new domains fast enough to do real work in them: read the references, build the model, check it against known results, then extend it
  • Build or adapt the models, simulations, and test setups the question needs, using existing tools where they fit and building where they do not
  • Pressure-test your own and others' work: hunt failure modes, surface hidden assumptions, and stress trade studies before decisions are locked in
  • Use AI tools as a force multiplier for research, code, and analysis, and know when their output has to be checked against a reference
  • Work shoulder to shoulder with Hardware, Software, GNC, and the other teams at Anduril, and translate results into decisions that change the design
  • Communicate results to engineers, leadership, and customers, including strong visual presentation of complex data

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Currently possesses and is able to maintain an active U.S. Top Secret security clearance
  • Demonstrated experience working in more than one technical area
  • You have done things: designed, built, tested, or fielded something real, in any field
  • Proficiency in at least one physics-math scripting environment (Python with numpy/scipy, MATLAB/Simulink, Julia, or similar)
  • Strong written, verbal, and visual communication

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 12+ years in a relevant science/engineering field
  • Math, physics, or engineering degree, or similar
  • Proficiency with AI tools (coding assistants, agents, model-driven research) in day-to-day engineering work, and judgment about when to trust their output
  • Experience in several of: space systems, missiles and missile defense, air vehicles, GNC, sensors and sensor fusion, radar, EW, acoustics, autonomy, or similar. Breadth across these counts for more than depth in any one
  • Familiarity with domain analysis tools as relevant (STK/Astrogator, AFSIM, HFSS, Fluent, or similar)

ABOUT THE JOB

Anduril's Air Dominance & Strike (AD&S) Manufacturing Engineering team is seeking a DFx Engineer to support design for manufacturability, assembly, and cost analysis across our mechanical, structural, thermal management, and fluid systems (fuel, hydraulics, pneumatics) subsystems. This role spans our full portfolio of autonomous aircraft, cruise missiles, and loitering munitions — and is an excellent opportunity for an early-career engineer to develop deep expertise in how design decisions impact producibility, supplier selection, and unit cost.
Working under the guidance of Staff and Senior DFx Engineers, you will learn to evaluate designs through the lenses of manufacturability, assembly, and cost — the three factors that determine whether hardware can be produced at rate, by a qualified supplier, at an affordable price point. You will work alongside subject matter expert (SME) manufacturing engineers and design engineers, building the technical judgment and cross-functional relationships that make DFx effective.
You will also gain hands-on exposure to contract manufacturer evaluation and qualification — visiting supplier facilities, participating in process assessments, and learning how to match supplier capabilities to production requirements. This is an inherently cross-functional role: you will work daily with supply chain, quality, operations, and program teams in addition to ME and DE. You will grow quickly here — our programs move fast, the hardware is real, and the impact of your work shows up on the production floor and in the cost model.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Support DFx analysis across mechanical, structural, thermal, and fluid systems subsystems for AD&S programs, working under the guidance of Staff and Senior DFx Engineers, with a focus on manufacturability, assembly, and cost.
  • Participate in structured DFM/DFA/DFC reviews at key design milestones, learning and applying the scoring methodology to identify producibility and cost risks and recommend design changes.
  • Participate in DFMEAs with cross-functional teams. Use FMEA outputs to drive design changes, inspection strategies, and control plans.
  • Work with SME manufacturing engineers and design engineers to provide manufacturing and cost feedback on designs, learning to translate constraints into actionable recommendations.
  • Support the evaluation and qualification of contract manufacturers — participating in facility reviews, process audits, and capability assessments under the guidance of senior team members.
  • Help build and maintain should-cost models and cost-driver analyses for mechanical and fluid system assemblies.
  • Help develop and maintain DFx standards, guidelines, and scorecards specific to mechanical manufacturing processes including CNC machining, sheet metal fabrication, welding, brazing, composite layup and bonding, tube bending and swaging, and mechanical assembly.
  • Analyze designs across key lenses — manufacturability/assembly, cost structure, adherence to specification, process capability, and technology maturity — contributing to risk assessments that inform engineering and program decisions.
  • Work with supply chain to understand how DFx requirements connect to sourcing strategy and supplier selection.
  • Collaborate with quality engineering to understand how DFx findings translate into inspection plans, acceptance criteria, and supplier quality requirements.
  • Spend time on the production floor and at supplier sites to build firsthand understanding of how mechanical hardware, thermal systems, and fluid components are manufactured.
  • Contribute to the DFx toolkit — templates, scoring rubrics, cost models, lessons-learned databases, and training materials.
  • Travel to production sites, contract manufacturers, and supplier facilities (~20%, depending on business needs).

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related field.
  • 5+ years of experience in manufacturing engineering, process engineering, or a related role with exposure to mechanical systems, thermal management, or fluid systems. Co-op, internship, or capstone project experience in a manufacturing environment counts.
  • Foundational knowledge of mechanical manufacturing processes: CNC machining, sheet metal fabrication, welding, composite fabrication, or mechanical assembly.
  • Ability to read mechanical drawings, interpret GD&T, and review 3D models with an eye toward producibility.
  • Interest in understanding manufacturing cost drivers and how design decisions impact unit cost.
  • Familiarity with aerospace mechanical standards or a willingness to learn and apply them quickly.
  • Strong communication skills and a willingness to engage directly with design engineers, manufacturing engineers, quality, supply chain, and operations — cross-functional collaboration is the core of this job, not a side task.
  • Comfort working in a fast-paced environment across multiple programs simultaneously.
  • A genuine interest in manufacturing and a drive to understand how things are actually built and what they cost to produce. Personal experience in a machine shop, fabrication shop, or working on hardware (machining, welding, assembly, personal projects) is a strong plus.
  • An attitude of world-class mission assurance, quality, attention to detail, and dedication.
  • Self-motivated and proactive — you take initiative, ask good questions, and close the loop on what you commit to.
  • Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Master's degree in engineering or a related field.
  • Internship or co-op experience in aerospace or defense mechanical manufacturing.
  • Exposure to DFM/DFA review processes, producibility engineering, or cost analysis.
  • Familiarity with AS9100 or similar quality management systems.
  • Experience visiting or evaluating manufacturing suppliers in any capacity.
  • Proficiency in CAD software (NX, CATIA, SolidWorks, or similar) sufficient to navigate and review designs.
  • Exposure to composite manufacturing, fluid system fabrication, or thermal management hardware production.
  • Experience with data analysis, cost modeling, or presentation development.
  • Experience with Full Size Determinant Assembly (FSDA).
  • Currently possesses and is able to maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance with Full-Scope Polygraph.

Anduril's Air Dominance & Strike (AD&S) Manufacturing Engineering team is seeking a DFx Engineer to support design for manufacturability, assembly, and cost analysis across our avionics, electronics, wiring,and harnessing subsystems. This role spans our full portfolio of autonomous aircraft, cruise missiles, and loitering munitions — and is an excellent opportunity for an early-career engineer to develop deep expertise in how design decisions impact producibility, supplier selection, and unit cost.

Working under the guidance of Staff and Senior DFx Engineers, you will learn to evaluate designs through the lenses of manufacturability, assembly, and cost — the three factors that determine whether hardware can be produced at rate, by a qualified supplier, at an affordable price point. You will work alongside subject matter expert (SME) manufacturing engineers and design engineers, building the technical judgment and cross-functional relationships that make DFx effective.

You will also gain hands-on exposure to contract manufacturer evaluation and qualification — visiting supplier facilities, participating in process assessments, and learning how to match supplier capabilities to production requirements. This is an inherently cross-functional role: you will work daily with supply chain, quality, operations, and program teams in addition to ME and DE. You will grow quickly here — our programs move fast, the hardware is real, and the impact of your work shows up on the production floor and in the cost model.

WHAT YOU’LL DO 

  • Support DFx analysis across avionics, electronics, wiring, and harnessing subsystems for AD&S programs, working under the guidance of Staff and Senior DFx Engineers, with a focus on manufacturability, assembly, and cost.
  • Participate in structured DFM/DFA/DFC reviews at key design milestones, learning and applying the scoring methodology to identify producibility and cost risks and recommend design changes.
  • Work with SME manufacturing engineers and design engineers to provide manufacturing and cost feedback on designs, learning to translate constraints into actionable recommendations.
  • Support the evaluation and qualification of contract manufacturers — participating in facility reviews, process audits, and capability assessments under the guidance of senior team members.
  • Help build and maintain should-cost models and cost-driver analyses for electronics and harnessing assemblies.
  • Help develop and maintain DFx standards, guidelines, and scorecards specific to electronics manufacturing processes including SMT, wave/selective solder, conformal coating, potting, wire harness fabrication, and box-build assembly.
  • Analyze designs across key lenses — manufacturability/assembly, cost structure, adherence to specification, process capability, and technology maturity — contributing to risk assessments that inform engineering and program decisions.
  • Work with supply chain to understand how DFx requirements connect to sourcing strategy and supplier selection.
  • Collaborate with quality engineering to understand how DFx findings translate into inspection plans, acceptance criteria, and supplier quality requirements.
  • Spend time on the production floor and at supplier sites to build firsthand understanding of how electronics and harnesses are manufactured.
  • Contribute to the DFx toolkit — templates, scoring rubrics, cost models, lessons-learned databases, and training materials.
  • Travel to production sites, contract manufacturers, and supplier facilities (~20%, depending on business needs).


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related field.

  • Foundational knowledge of electronics and/or harnessing manufacturing processes: SMT, soldering, conformal coating, wire harness fabrication, or electromechanical assembly.
  • Ability to read electrical schematics, PCB layouts, and harness drawings with an eye toward producibility.
  • Interest in understanding manufacturing cost drivers and how design decisions impact unit cost.
  • Familiarity with IPC standards (IPC-A-610, J-STD-001, IPC-620) or a willingness to learn and apply them quickly.
  • Strong communication skills and a willingness to engage directly with design engineers, manufacturing engineers, quality, supply chain, and operations — cross-functional collaboration is the core of this job, not a side task.
  • Comfort working in a fast-paced environment across multiple programs simultaneously.
  • A genuine interest in manufacturing and a drive to understand how things are actually built and what they cost to produce. Personal experience physically building or working on hardware (soldering, harness build, assembly, personal projects) is a strong plus.
  • An attitude of world-class mission assurance, quality, attention to detail, and dedication.
  • Self-motivated and proactive — you take initiative, ask good questions, and close the loop on what you commit to.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Discovery is Anduril's team for the hard concepts: the ones that are not yet proven or built. We take the newest and hardest problems across space, missiles, air, sensors, autonomy, and cyber, decide what is worth building, and prove it out: we build the models, break the assumptions, run the tests, and carry what works to the point where a program can pick it up. We work with hardware and software engineering teams across the company, driving cross-functional collaboration across different business lines. 

ABOUT THE JOB

We are building an expeditionary force: a small group of engineers who want to do big, new, hard things and who move into unfamiliar territory as a matter of course. As a Discovery Engineer you pick up a concept nobody has proven, learn whatever domain it lives in, build the analysis or prototype that tests it, and get to an answer. The problems change; the approach does not: reason from first principles, do the work, check it, and reach a solution.

You are not hired for a particular skill set. You are hired for a record of getting engaged in problems across different areas, being analytic, testing new concepts, and getting to solutions. You are also the adversary to our own ideas. The rigor that validates a good concept is the same rigor that kills a bad one early, while it is still cheap, and you apply it to your own work first.

This is a hands-on technical role on both internally and externally funded programs within Anduril's Discovery Business Line, on operationally relevant timelines.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Own new concepts from first idea through analysis, prototype, and test, and drive them to a validated answer
  • Learn new domains fast enough to do real work in them: read the references, build the model, check it against known results, then extend it
  • Build or adapt the models, simulations, and test setups the question needs, using existing tools where they fit and building where they do not
  • Pressure-test your own and others' work: hunt failure modes, surface hidden assumptions, and stress trade studies before decisions are locked in
  • Use AI tools as a force multiplier for research, code, and analysis, and know when their output has to be checked against a reference
  • Work shoulder to shoulder with Hardware, Software, GNC, and the other teams at Anduril, and translate results into decisions that change the design
  • Communicate results to engineers, leadership, and customers, including strong visual presentation of complex data

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Currently possesses and is able to maintain an active U.S. Top Secret security clearance
  • Demonstrated experience working in more than one technical area
  • You have done things: designed, built, tested, or fielded something real, in any field
  • Proficiency in at least one physics-math scripting environment (Python with numpy/scipy, MATLAB/Simulink, Julia, or similar)
  • Strong written, verbal, and visual communication

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 4+ years in a relevant science/engineering field
  • Math, physics, or engineering degree, or similar
  • Proficiency with AI tools (coding assistants, agents, model-driven research) in day-to-day engineering work, and judgment about when to trust their output
  • Experience in several of: space systems, missiles and missile defense, air vehicles, GNC, sensors and sensor fusion, radar, EW, acoustics, autonomy, or similar. Breadth across these counts for more than depth in any one
  • Familiarity with domain analysis tools as relevant (STK/Astrogator, AFSIM, HFSS, Fluent, or similar)
