About the Team

Anduril's Pricing Operations team sits at the core of driving domestic and international market expansion by building and implementing corporate-wide pricing frameworks. The team partners cross-functionally with Growth, Proposal & Capture, Legal, FP&A, and Program teams to streamline proposal processes while ensuring accuracy, compliance, and a deliberate balance of competitiveness, profitability, and revenue growth. As Anduril scales its portfolio, this central team sets the standard that individual business lines execute against.

About the Role

As a Lead Analyst, Pricing Operations, you will partner with Anduril's Product Line leadership — Business Development, Proposal & Capture, Program Management, and FP&A — to execute financial analyses and proposal cost volumes, and to build the models, templates, and processes that business-line pricing teams rely on. Your core focus is corporate pricing operations, but you will flex to support individual business divisions on strategic pursuits as demand requires.

The right person has a deep understanding of cost estimating, pricing strategy, financial modeling, and regulatory compliance, and is energized by a fast-paced environment where you scale frameworks rather than just complete one-off tasks. If you think strategically, move without being told to, and enjoy having your work seen by senior leadership, this role is for you.

What You'll Do

Strategic Proposal Leadership

  • Lead and track strategic proposals from opportunity to award — be a stakeholder in proposal kick-offs and review while ensure progress, compliance, and financial alignment with business objectives.
  • Prepare timely, high-quality, detailed, and compliant cost and price proposals for federal and commercial solicitations — including U.S. DoD and International customers — across RFPs, RFQs, and RFIs.
  • Generate submission-ready cost proposal artifacts, ensuring all cost elements are accounted for, assumptions are documented, and necessary cross-referencing is included.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to understand technical requirements, basis of estimates, risks, and opportunities, and translate them into compliant cost proposals.
  • Coordinate with contracts and capture and proposal teams on proposal documents and responses to government requests while adhering to deadlines and submission requirements.

Financial Modeling & Analysis

  • Develop comprehensive pricing models, templates, and training utilized by business-line pricing teams, and maintain them for both internal and external use.
  • When required, exercise significant autonomy in analyzing statistical and proposal data to develop independent pricing recommendations that support customer negotiations.
  • Conduct risk analysis, what-if scenarios, and cost realism assessments to ensure pricing accuracy and executability.

Process, Compliance & Operations

  • Continually assess and improve the estimating processes and tools used by the team to maintain efficiency and accuracy, leading process-improvement projects as needed.
  • Ensure cost proposals comply with solicitation instructions, government regulations (FAR, DFARS, TINA), and corporate policies, including requirements specific to CPFF, T&M, and FFP contracts.
  • Maintain accurate, complete records of pricing templates, proposal files, supporting documentation, and historical data, and keep proposal tracking metrics current.
  • Support DCAA and DCMA audit reviews as required, ensuring transparency and adherence to cost estimating policies and procedures.

Required Qualifications

  • Bachelor's Degree in Business, Accounting, Engineering, a mathematical field, or a related discipline.
  • 8+ years of directly related experience in proposal / pricing / cost development, with demonstrated experience developing both government and commercial proposals, and familiarity across CPFF, FFP, and T&M contracts and subcontracts — specifically a strong understanding of how indirect rates and burden costs work in relationship to cost modeling.
  • Demonstrated extensive work experience and full understanding of the Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR), Defense Federal Acquisition Regulation Supplement (DFARS), and Truth in Negotiations Act (TINA).
  • Demonstrated ability to design, develop, and implement financial analysis tools and processes — such as pricing cost models.
  • Highly proficient in Microsoft Excel (financial modeling, pivot tables, complex formulas); proficient in Word and PowerPoint.
  • Deep hands-on working experience with ProPricer.
  • Self-driven and relentlessly proactive. You don't need someone to tell you to “move” — you just move, and you step into the gap to offer solutions yourself.
  • Comfortable communicating broadly and having many eyes on your work, including comms to large groups and senior leadership.
  • S. Person status is required; must be able to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret clearance.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience contributing to investment strategy and financial management for a business line or division (e.g., investment cases, portfolio prioritization, and business-outcome analysis).
  • Experience in Material Estimating, or Defense Contracting Finance.
  • Experience in Engineering, Supply Chain, or Operations finance.
  • Experience with ERP systems (e.g., Salesforce, Oracle, Palantir Foundry) and financial reporting tools.
  • Active Secret clearance.

Anduril’s Drones team is seeking a highly motivated and experienced Lead Manufacturing Engineer to join our rapidly growing team. In this pivotal role, you will be responsible for bridging the gap between cutting-edge design and efficient, high-volume production for our advanced Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS) like Bolt, Ghost, Anvil, and future autonomous platforms.

As a Lead Manufacturing Engineer in Drones, you will support products from the early design phase, develop/improve the manufacturing process and support production ramps for several products. The diverse responsibilities of this role will require you to leverage your technical expertise as well as leadership skills to set objectives, build cross-functional teams, and drive rapid project execution. You will play a crucial role in optimizing manufacturing processes, reducing costs, and increasing efficiencies on existing technologies while also developing new products and scaling to full scale production.

WHAT YOU’LL DO 

  • Build, mentor, and lead a high-performing team of Manufacturing Engineers with deep product knowledge in mechanical, electrical, system integration, and end of line tests
  • Lead the transition of products from concept to prototype, pilot, and full production with speed, flexibility, scalability, and first-time quality.
  • Provide daily sustaining support to ensure each product line performs as intended, including real-time problem-solving related to mechanical fitment issues, electrical and harnessing issues, as well as software and firmware issues.
  • Work with cross functional team (design, quality, supply chain, etc.) during the development process to drive design for manufacturing best practices into the design effort, and help facilitate the transition from design to prototype to rate production.
  • Own documentation required for successfully manufacturing product group hardware at scale, such as MBOM’s, work instructions & requirements, etc.
  • Uphold and advise on quality management and business application programs as they pertain to manufacturing within your area.
  • Facilitate make versus buy decisions, and coordinate with internal supply chain teams to manage vendors to ensure quality deliveries on time.
  • Contribute to end-customer hardware mechanical or electrical design, including interconnects, board fabrication and inspection, etc.
  • Analyze metrics for continuous improvement initiatives (cost reduction, QI reduction & capacity increase).
  • Instill a culture of innovation, teamwork, and accountability within the manufacturing engineering product team.


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Degree in a technical field such as engineering, math, or a hard science.
  • 5+ years in manufacturing or similar prototyping position.
  • Demonstrated in-kind or direct team leadership skills, with backing examples.
  • An attitude of world-class mission assurance, quality, attention to detail, and dedication.
  • A genuine interest in manufacturing and thirst for learning.
  • Demonstrated ability to creatively deliver hardware in a resource-constrained environment
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 

  • Experience building or transforming successful production operation organizations and leading large-scale change management initiatives that influence culture, define tools & processes and improve competencies.
  • Harness & PCBA fabrication experience including prior work with or setup/modification/monitoring SMT processes.
  • Experience leading and managing teams on fast-paced, complex projects.
  • Hands-on experience with R/C and/or autonomous flight vehicles, flight controllers, or other related control systems.
  • Software scripting experience in any language.
  • Experience in NX/Teamcenter

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril’s Space Manufacturing team is seeking a Lead Manufacturing Engineer for Propulsion and Energetics to join our team. Your expertise will help ensure that our products meet the highest standards of quality and reliability at Anduril.

As the Lead Manufacturing Engineer for Propulsion and Energetics, you will own the manufacturing and integration processes for the highest-consequence hardware on the vehicle. Your responsibilities span solid rocket motor integration, divert and attitude control and thruster installation, pressurant and fluid systems, and the ordnance and initiator installation that arms the vehicle — together with the hazard classification, safety controls and handling discipline that make all of it survivable. You will lead cross-functional initiatives, mentor engineers and technicians, and grow this discipline as the production ramp builds.

This role owns the integration and handling of qualified propulsion and energetic hardware. Solid rocket motors arrive qualified from Anduril RMS and thrusters and control systems arrive from our propulsion partners; you own how they are received, handled, installed, mated and closed out — not propellant casting, loading or pyrotechnic device manufacture. The ideal candidate is a hands-on propulsion integration engineer who has worked flight or comparably high-consequence energetic hardware under a formal safety program, and who is comfortable working from incomplete design data in a fast-paced environment.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 

  • Own solid rocket motor integration processes: receipt and inspection of qualified motors from Anduril RMS, handling and lift operations, mating to the vehicle, alignment, and torque and close-out.
  • Own divert and attitude control system and thruster installation processes — mounting, alignment, plumbing and leak verification — for both development and vendor-supplied units.
  • Own pressurant and fluid system build and installation: tanks, lines, fittings, valves, proof and leak testing, and cleanliness control for propulsion-grade fluid systems.
  • Own ordnance installation processes — initiators, pyrotechnic separation systems and flight termination system installation — including safe-and-arm handling, electrical safing, stray voltage and RF hazard controls, and the two-person and lockout discipline that goes with them.
  • Partner with Anduril's Explosive Engineering & Operations team on hazard classification and own the manufacturing safety controls that follow — siting, storage and licensing compliance, and the hazardous operating procedures the floor works to.
  • Author and maintain work instructions, travelers and as-built records for the propulsion and ordnance operations you own, and own root cause analysis, PFMEA, process validation and first article inspection for those processes.
  • Drive Design for Manufacturability and Assembly into propulsion and ordnance designs before CDR — access, handling provisions, safing points, line and connector routing, and installation order.
  • Specify and qualify handling equipment, lift fixtures and installation tooling for propulsion hardware, working with the Automation and Tooling engineer who designs it.
  • Serve as the manufacturing technical interface to Anduril RMS and to our propulsion partners on motor and thruster producibility, and support energetics integration on site at our launch and motor sites.
  • Act as an owner of Anduril's Manufacturing Development Process (MDP), use Foundry and Teamcenter as the system of record, and mentor the engineers and technicians who will grow this discipline.

 

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 

  • Bachelor’s degree in Aerospace, Mechanical, Chemical, Manufacturing or Industrial Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
  • 8+ years of manufacturing or integration engineering experience in aerospace, space, defense or another high-reliability industry, including 4+ years hands-on work on propulsion, ordnance or other energetic hardware.
  • Has worked under a formal explosives or energetics safety program and can describe the controls in practice — quantity-distance and magazine siting under DESR 6055.09 or ATF 27 CFR, two-person discipline, electrical safing, and stray voltage and RF hazard controls.
  • Hands-on experience in at least two of: solid rocket motor handling and integration; liquid or cold-gas thruster installation; pressurant and fluid system build with proof and leak testing; ordnance installation, including separation systems or flight termination systems.
  • Has authored or approved procedures for hazardous operations on flight or comparably high-consequence hardware, and can walk through how a procedure changed after first execution.
  • Experience specifying handling and lift equipment for heavy or hazardous articles, including load path and proof load requirements.
  • Experience serving as the manufacturing technical interface to a propulsion supplier or an internal motor or thruster producer — deliverability, producibility and acceptance.
  • Demonstrated expertise in root cause analysis (8D, 5-Why, Fishbone), PFMEA, corrective and preventive action, and first article inspection, applied to hazardous processes.
  • Currently possesses and is able to maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance
  • Willingness to travel up to 25%

 

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 

  • Formal explosives safety certification or qualification — DoD 4145.26, DOT hazardous materials, range safety, or an equivalent service or agency program.
  • Solid rocket motor production or integration experience on a flight program.
  • Launch site integration experience, including range safety approval of hazardous procedures.
  • Working familiarity with the governing standards and regulations — DESR 6055.09, DoD 4145.26, ATF 27 CFR, DOT 49 CFR, OSHA Process Safety Management, MIL-STD-882E system safety, and AS9100.
  • Cleanroom manufacturing with contamination control for solid and liquid propellant systems.

As the Lead Manufacturing Engineer for Space Vehicle Integration, you will be a technical leader responsible for owning the manufacturing strategy and execution for complex spacecraft hardware. Your responsibilities span the entire vehicle integration value chain, including Design for Manufacturability, advanced manufacturing process development, tooling design & selection, supplier technical management, quality system implementation, and comprehensive work documentation. You will lead cross-functional initiatives, mentor junior engineers, and drive integration excellence across vehicle structures, mechanisms, harness installation, and final close-out.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

 

  • Own the vehicle-level build flow for both production vehicle lines: define assembly and integration sequence, station and zone content, takt, and the work instructions and travelers that execute it for each vehicle line.
  • Own the post-environmental close-out stations — weight and balance, mass properties verification, sealing, final mechanical close-out and ship preparation. These stations are the throughput bottleneck in every flow we have modeled; making them faster is the single highest-value thing this role does.
  • Develop and qualify vehicle integration processes: precision fastening and torque control, bonded and shimmed joints, mechanism and propulsion module installation, harness routing and installation, and alignment to metrology-defined datums.
  • Drive Design for Manufacturability and Assembly into vehicle-level designs before CDR — access, fastener reach, tool clearance, integration order, and testability of the assembled vehicle — partnering directly with structures, mechanisms and systems design engineers.
  • Act as a principal stakeholder in deploying Anduril's Manufacturing Development Process (MDP) on this program. The Manager and Senior Manager of Manufacturing Engineering are the full process owners; every manufacturing engineer is an owner and an evangelist. You will be expected to carry MDP into design forums rather than wait for it to be handed to you.
  • Mature manufacturing readiness artifacts concurrently with design readiness milestones — producibility assessments, process and tooling plans, build flow definition and manufacturing readiness evidence timed to PDR and CDR rather than assembled after them.
  • Adopt and master our manufacturing execution and product lifecycle toolchain — Foundry and Teamcenter — and use it as the system of record for build definition, work instruction authoring, as-built records and production data. Fluency here is a requirement of the role, not a training objective.
  • Specify and deploy mechanical ground support equipment and tooling: handling and lift fixtures, rotation and transport fixtures, integration stands, alignment tooling and torque tooling, including custom design in CAD.
  • Partner with Supply Chain and Quality to define, deploy and monitor manufacturing best practices at the vendors and outside partners who deliver finished vehicle assemblies into our production facility — workmanship and process requirements, first article and source inspection expectations, and the as-built and nonconformance records that must arrive with the hardware. Incoming assemblies that are not integration-ready stop this line, so this interface is yours to own, not to inherit.
  • Hire, mentor and lead the integration engineers who will each own a single vehicle line, while retaining cross-line ownership of integration process, tooling and workmanship standards; provide hands-on technical leadership to integration technicians on the floor.

 

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

 

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical, Aerospace, Mechanical, Manufacturing or Industrial Engineering, or a related technical discipline.

  • Personally owned the build flow for at least one vehicle-level or major-assembly integration line — sequence definition, station content, work instructions and travelers — and can walk through how you built it and what you changed after first article.
  • Hands-on depth in mechanical integration: precision fastening and torque control, bonded or shimmed joints, mechanism installation, harness routing and installation, and alignment to metrology-defined datums (laser tracker, CMM or photogrammetry).
  • Experience with weight and balance or mass properties verification and final close-out operations on flight or comparably high-consequence hardware.
  • Cleanroom manufacturing experience with contamination control and FOD prevention discipline (ISO 7 or cleaner).
  • Hands-on fluency with a manufacturing execution system and a PLM system as the system of record — build definition, work instruction or work order authoring, as-built records and production data. Teamcenter, Palantir Foundry, SAP, Manufacturo, Windchill or equivalent.
  • Currently possesses and is able to maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance
  • Willingness to travel up to 25%

 

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

 

  • Direct experience integrating satellites, spacecraft or space-based instruments (flight hardware), including support to environmental test campaigns (TVAC, vibration, shock, acoustics) and launch site integration.
  • Familiarity with space workmanship and process standards — NASA-STD-8739 series, IPC-620 for harness and cable, ECSS equivalents — and with mechanism and fastener standards for flight hardware.

The Maritime Division operates across multiple sites and business lines, producing advanced undersea systems for national defense. As the division scales from a single-product facility to a multi-site, multi-business-line operation, maintaining a unified and audit-ready quality management system is critical. This role sits within the Corporate Quality organization but is fully dedicated to the Maritime Division, serving as the connective tissue that keeps quality systems aligned across every site, product line, and certification boundary.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a Lead Quality Systems Engineer, Maritime to join our team and own the end-to-end AS9100 quality management system across the Maritime Division. In the near term, you will support ongoing AS9100 certification and surveillance activities. Looking ahead, your primary mission is solving a much harder problem: as new product lines and manufacturing sites come online, the AS9100 certification scope expands to cover multiple sites, multiple product lines, and multiple business lines operating under shared facilities. You will be responsible for designing and maintaining a QMS architecture that keeps all of these threads audit-ready, ensuring that growth in one area does not create certification risk in another. This role requires deep expertise in AS9100 and aerospace quality systems, experience managing multi-site certification scopes, and the ability to work across organizational boundaries. If you are someone who can see the big picture of a quality system while managing the granular documentation and process discipline required to pass rigorous third-party audits, this role is for you.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • AS9100 Certification Ownership: Own the Maritime Division's AS9100 QMS, including all documentation, internal audit programs, corrective action tracking, and management review processes. Ensure the system remains audit-ready at all times across all sites.
  • Multi-Site QMS Architecture: Design and implement a quality management system structure that accommodates multiple manufacturing sites operating under a single or coordinated AS9100 certification scope. Address the complexity that arises when product lines span multiple facilities and when multiple business lines share a single site.
  • Audit Preparation and Liaison: Serve as the primary point of contact for third-party certification body audits, customer audits, and regulatory reviews. Manage audit schedules, coordinate site readiness, and ensure findings are closed on time. Guide the organization through the evolution from a single-site audit scope to a multi-site, multi-product scope.
  • Cross-Site Process Harmonization: Establish standardized quality processes, procedures, and documentation practices that work across all division manufacturing sites. Ensure that shared processes meet AS9100 requirements regardless of which site or business line is being audited, while allowing for site-specific procedures where necessary.
  • Risk and Gap Analysis: Continuously assess QMS gaps and certification risks as new product lines and sites are brought online. Proactively identify where the expansion of audit scope creates exposure and develop mitigation plans before issues surface in formal audits.
  • Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA): Own the division-wide CAPA process. Track nonconformances, drive root cause analysis, and ensure corrective actions are implemented and verified across all sites. Monitor trends to identify systemic issues before they become repeat audit findings.
  • Training and Culture: Build quality awareness across the Maritime Division. Develop and deliver training programs that ensure personnel at all sites understand AS9100 requirements, their role in maintaining certification, and the implications of nonconformance in a multi-site environment.
  • Stakeholder Coordination: Work across Corporate Quality, site leadership, production teams, and business line leads to ensure QMS requirements are integrated into operational planning. Participate in site battle rhythm meetings and provide regular quality status updates to division leadership.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 5+ years of experience in quality management within aerospace, defense, or government-contract manufacturing
  • Direct experience managing or significantly contributing to AS9100 certification and surveillance audits
  • Demonstrated experience with multi-site or multi-scope quality management systems
  • Strong knowledge of CAPA processes, internal auditing, and management review requirements under AS9100
  • Effective communicator who can work across organizational boundaries and present to leadership
  • Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • AS9100 Lead Auditor certification (e.g., through Exemplar Global, RABQSA, or equivalent)
  • Experience in a scaling or startup manufacturing environment where QMS processes were being built or significantly expanded
  • Familiarity with other aerospace/defense quality standards (e.g., AS13100, NADCAP, ISO 9001, ITAR/EAR compliance as it relates to quality documentation)
  • Experience managing AS9100 scope expansions, including adding new sites or product lines to an existing certificate
  • Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Quality Management, or a related field
  • Experience with ERP/MES systems and their integration with quality management processes
  • Lean, Six Sigma, or continuous improvement certification or experience

Manager, Accounting (Intercompany)

We are looking for an exceptional Accounting Manager to build and lead the intercompany and intracompany accounting function. The Accounting team owns the month-end close and reporting infrastructure behind one of the fastest-scaling companies in defense. This is a build seat more than a maintain seat: we are preparing for a future potential IPO, expanding rapidly, and managing increasingly complex intercompany and intracompany relationships, so you will set the processes, systems, and controls this function runs on for years.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Intercompany & Intracompany Accounting: Own end-to-end intercompany and intracompany accounting — designing and maintaining the intercompany framework, processing intercompany and intracompany transactions, reconciling balances, and driving timely elimination entries across all entities and business units.
  • Passdown & Allocation: Own the methodology and execution of corporate cost passdowns, intracompany allocations, shared-service allocations, and management fee structures, ensuring they are defensible, well-documented, and compliant with government contracting requirements (e.g., CAS/FAR).
  • Entity Management: Maintain the legal entity structure in the ERP and ensure new entities are set up with proper charts of accounts, intercompany agreements, and elimination hierarchies.
  • Financial Close: Own the monthly, quarterly, and annual close for intercompany and intracompany accounts, delivering journal entries, accruals, and flux analysis on the close calendar.
  • Reporting & Disclosures: Prepare and review consolidation schedules, intercompany elimination entries, and related footnotes and disclosures for financial reporting.
  • Reconciliations: Review balance sheet reconciliations for intercompany and intracompany accounts on a timely basis, and research and resolve variances as needed.
  • Team Leadership: Lead, mentor, and develop a team of accountants, setting priorities, reviewing work, and building bench strength as the intercompany portfolio grows.
  • Systems & Process Improvement: Help implement new systems or improve efficiencies with current systems to support continued company and team growth — including intercompany billing platforms and consolidation tools.
  • SOX Readiness: Help build and maintain SOX-ready process documentation and key controls over intercompany transactions, intracompany allocations, and eliminations in support of public company readiness.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are seeking a highly experienced and dynamic Manager of Manufacturing Engineering to lead our manufacturing engineering efforts across multiple critical space programs. This pivotal role demands a visionary leader with deep technical expertise in advanced aerospace manufacturing, a proven track record of bringing complex space-qualified hardware from prototype to production, and an unwavering commitment to quality and mission success.
 
As a Manager of Manufacturing Engineering, you will be responsible for leading and managing a manufacturing engineering team over a subset of Anduril’s products to drive process improvements, ensure the highest quality of production, and support the development and implementation of new products. You will play a crucial role in optimizing manufacturing processes, reducing costs, and increasing efficiencies on existing technologies while also developing new products and scaling to full scale production. 

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

  • Lead the manufacturing engineering team, setting goals, providing direction, and evaluating performance over a certain product or set of products, from initial prototyping through large full-scale production.
  • Develop and execute strategic plans to enhance production capabilities, incorporating new technologies and methodologies.
  • Own documentation required for successfully manufacturing product group hardware at scale, such as work instructions, inspection plans & requirements, etc.
  • Collaborate with product development teams to ensure manufacturability of new designs and smooth transition from prototype to production.
  • Assist in the selection, installation, and commissioning of new manufacturing equipment, ensuring optimal integration into production lines.
  • Drive continuous improvement initiatives that result in cost reduction, quality enhancement, and throughput maximization.
  • Manage budgets and forecast future manufacturing needs, including personnel, equipment, and materials.
  • Establish and maintain robust training and documentation programs to enhance team skills and promote cross-functional knowledge sharing.
  • Foster a culture of innovation, teamwork, and accountability within the manufacturing engineering department.
  • Serve as the technical expert and point of contact for manufacturing engineering issues, providing guidance and support to resolve complex problems.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to ensure successful product launches, from initial design through to full-scale production.
  • Liaise with vendors and suppliers to ensure the timely delivery of equipment and materials and maintain quality standards.
  • Analyze production metrics and performance data to identify trends and opportunities for improvement.
  • Ensure compliance with all safety, quality, and regulatory requirements within the manufacturing process.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related field
  • Minimum of 5-7 years of experience in manufacturing engineering, with at least 3 years in a managerial or supervisory role.
  • Proven track record of leading teams, developing new products and processes, and cradle to grave ownership.
  • Experience driving process improvements in a manufacturing setting.
  • An attitude of world-class mission assurance, quality, attention to detail, and dedication.
  • A genuine interest in manufacturing and thirst for learning.
  • Excellent project management skills and experience leading cross-functional projects.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making capabilities.
  • Exceptional communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively at all levels of the organization.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced and dynamic environment.
  • Personal experience physically manufacturing hardware via any means (machining, fabrication, soldering, assembly, etc.). Work on personal or extracurricular projects is a plus.
  • Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Masters degree in engineering, business, or related field.
  • Strong knowledge of Lean Manufacturing, Six Sigma, and other process improvement methodologies.
  • Proficient in CAD software and familiar with modern manufacturing technologies and automation.
  • Software scripting experience in any language.

Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Tactical Effects (TFX), as part of Tactical Reconnaissance & Strike (TRS) team, is focused on positioning Anduril as a lead provider of specialized engineering and products for Man-packable portable systems to expeditionary multi-mission to mass counter UAS defense and strike. We work to clearly understand customer requirements, shape their concepts of operation, and deliver exquisite capability across their problem set. We aim to develop and deploy critically needed capabilities that address our customers' most pressing national security requirements.

ABOUT THE JOB
As the Manager of Product Quality Engineering for Anvil, you will lead a team of product quality engineers and quality specialists who will work inside and outside the organization to define, develop, and execute processes that deliver high quality and reliable products. Your leadership will impact how Anduril delivers production quality and sustaining support for Anvil across its lifecycle. You will build partnerships with heads of production, manufacturing engineering, program management, deployments, sourcing and multiple engineering teams. The right person for this role has knowledge of manufacturing, product development, sub-system performance criteria and metrology, and leadership experience to contribute to Anduril's mission.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Develop close collaboration with Product, Engineering, Test, and Supply Chain leadership teams and execute to Product Development Process (PDP) to meet all gate readiness review criteria (CDR, BRR, MRR/PRR) engaging from early prototype testing to full rate production.
  • Be the voice and leader for product development, production quality, supplier quality, and all the functions that contribute to an efficient and effective NPI/production process and delivery of Anvil to Anduril customers.
  • Lead and manage a team to champion continuous improvement and failure mode elimination in the development and production phases, driving part and system level quality readiness for production scaling, and supporting customer / deployment quality issues.
  • Own and utilize Supplier Quality Engineering resources to own and track supplier quality control and development program for Anvil as well as supplier part qualification and risk management programs.
  • Own and lead Quality Control process, framework, and execution starting from detailed engineering requirements and risks all the way to managing inspection methods and tooling by collaborating with systems design partners and providing leadership and prioritization to quality control teams.
  • Set daily and weekly priorities for the quality teams and establish culture of best-in-class product quality by driving the adoption and consistent use of quality tools and processes.
  • Drive production readiness by detailed design reviews, process development, verification/validation, and qualification of processes and parts, sub-assembly, and system deployments.
  • Drive clarity and resolution for performance ambiguities associated with product maturity, process stability, and field performance that impact Anvil meeting its quality and reliability goals for production.
  • Drive ongoing quality performance for incoming quality control, in-process quality control, and end of line quality.
  • Own the elimination of product risk by reducing process contribution to quality and reliability across the product lifecycle.
  • Lead Root Cause and Corrective Action (RCCA), Non-Conformance Reviews (NCRs), Corrective and Preventive Action (CAPA), and Material Review Board (MRB) activities. Review the effectiveness of actions and share lessons learned across the product team.
  • Own and lead cross functional alignment within Corrective Action Board (CAB) activities to drive ownership to investigations and resolutions of quality issues regarding design, integration, process, and supply chain.
  • Lead product health data analysis and improvement activities. Establish metrics for measuring quality and the factors that predict quality performance. Drive performance when out of goal/out of specification conditions occur.
  • Support the continuous improvement of the Quality Management System needed to support the process and product. Define and improve required documentation and activities.
  • Develop strategies and resource plans with heads of production, program management, deployments, sourcing and chief engineers and architects to meet customer and product requirements.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelors degree in a technical Engineering discipline
  • Minimum 5+ years of experience leading organizations including teams of direct report engineers to address NPI and production execution and quality issues that impact delivery or product quality at our customer
  • Minimum total of 10+ combined years of experience working in technical/engineering disciplines related to product quality/engineering as an individual contributor engineer or working engineering manager
  • Working knowledge of design review and quality management of PCBA, harnessing, mechanical structures, systems integration, power/battery systems, radar, vision system/optical image capture, networking/communication protocol, and remote management systems
  • Experience driving product quality and performance requirements to test and measurement system development and optimization. Leading the transition from engineering qualification to manufacturing variance testing for product quality coverage.
  • Working knowledge of product development methodologies such as Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (FMEA), Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP), Inspection and measurement systems, Production Part Approval Process (PPAP) elements such as Measurement Systems Analysis (MSA), Gauge Repeatability and Reproducibility (GR&R), Statistical Process Control (SPC), and Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T)
  • Working knowledge of precision mechanicals, composites, motors, and/or PCBA and Cable harnessing manufacturing processes
  • Ability to read and drive clarity for technical drawings, requirements, Quality Clauses, and SOWs used to describe quality requirements
  • Working knowledge of Manufacturing Execution systems, Configuration Management and Document Control/Data Management
  • An extreme ownership mindset with demonstrated capability to drive projects from start to completion
  • Analytical skills and experiences for data mining, data quality, metrics generation, issue management systems, and statistical analysis tools (MatLab, JMP, MiniTab, etc)
  • Eligible to obtain and/or maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Masters degree in a technical engineering discipline
  • Contractual knowledge in ITAR and EAR applications regarding product technicalities
  • Experience in design/integration/test of sensors/cameras/gimbals
  • Experience recruiting, hiring, and developing a team of engineers and specialists
  • 8+ years of experience with developing quality systems for high volume, high complexity manufacturing environments
  • Working knowledge of AS9100 / ISO 9001-based Quality Management System requirements
  • Experience with IPC standards, mastery of ESD and FOD prevention and mitigation programs
  • Experience with government contracts and military standard requirements
  • Experience with Teamcenter/PLM, Oracle, Warehouse management, Non-Conformance management systems, and Atlassian work stream tools

$147,000—$196,000 USD

    • Via Agency Partner: If contacted by a recruiting agency for an Anduril role, their email will clearly identify their agency. If you suspect any suspicious activity, please verify the agency's authenticity by reaching out to contact@anduril.com.

ABOUT THE JOB

As a Manager of Product Security Foundations, you will be responsible for leading and managing a security engineering team responsible for delivering reusable, foundational security components Anduril’s products.

The ideal candidate has a background in electrical or software engineering, with a focus on platform security. They will be able to conduct complex security architecture reviews, research and mitigate exploits against hardware and software, and implement critical features in collaboration with other engineering teams to build resiliency into our products.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Own the development and maturation of the security roadmap for Anduril’s products
  • Lead teams within the Product Security org to ensure Anduril products are resilient enough to survive against modern cyber threats
  • Collaborate and build solutions with engineering teams to meet and exceed industry-standard security goals
  • Build a strong partnership with Anduril’s engineering teams in order to develop and execute against a well aligned roadmap that covers Anduril’s portfolio globally
  • Engage with teams to remediate uncovered weakness in designs, implementations, integrations, and processes
  • Own processes that includes both pre-market and post-market processes engineering teams leverage throughout the product development lifecycl

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Possesses both strategic vision and technical depth, maintaining active involvement in security architecture and implementation
  • Proficient with one or more programming languages (e.g. C/C++, Golang, Rust, Python)
  • Regularly builds, tests, and delivers production-ready systems, especially for embedded and/or Linux systems
  • Experience assessing security of firmware, applications, network, IoT, or embedded systems
  • Experience developing features for and improving security of firmware, applications, network, or embedded systems
  • Familiarity with anti-tamper and reverse engineering mechanisms
  • Experience in platform security engineering and secure SDLC implementation
  • Strong and professional communication skills (written and verbal)
  • Demonstrated commitment to practical, mission-enabling security solutions
  • Must be eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. TS clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Familiarity with security architectures of embedded, aerospace, or cyber-physical systems
  • Experience building endpoint detection and response solutions
  • Experience building factory automation for secure key handling/provisioning
  • Experience building, testing, and delivering production-ready systems, especially for embedded and/or Linux systems
  • Experience with programmable logic devices and their development tools
  • Knowledge of cyber threat actors, their TTPs, and their implications for weapon and space system operations
  • Experience securing complex, AI-native systems
  • Experience conducting incident response in cloud systems and embedded systems

Job Description: Manufacturing Engineer, Turbine Engines

JOB DESCRIPTIONS:

By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. SUMMARY - ABOUT THE TEAM / JOB

Anduril Industries is seeking a skilled and innovative Turbomachinery Manufacturing Engineer to join our growing team. The ideal candidate will play a crucial role in developing and optimizing manufacturing processes for advanced turbine engines and their precision components used in our cutting-edge defense systems.

The right person for this role can demonstrate past holistic ownership on solving a technical challenge with a creative, physical, solution that they either personally manufacturing or oversaw manufacturing on, in a fast-paced, resource-limited environment. If you are someone who thrives in such an environment, then this role is for you.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Design, develop, and implement robust, efficient, and high-quality manufacturing processes for advanced turbine engines and their precision components, from concept to production.
  • Specify, design, procure, and validate necessary tooling, fixtures, and manufacturing equipment to support production goals and process requirements.
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to ensure manufacturability of turbomachinery designs, including DFx principles.
  • Optimize existing manufacturing processes to improve efficiency, quality, and cost-effectiveness.
  • Develop and maintain manufacturing documentation, including work instructions, process flow diagrams, and quality control plans
  • Conduct root cause analysis for manufacturing defects, non-conformances, or process inefficiencies, and implement effective corrective and preventive actions.
  • Evaluate and implement new manufacturing technologies and methodologies.
  • Ensure compliance with quality standards, safety regulations, and environmental requirements.
  • Manage projects related to turbomachinery manufacturing improvements and capacity expansion.
  • Provide technical support to production teams and train personnel on new processes and equipment.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or related field; Master's degree preferred.
  • 5+ years of progressive experience in turbomachinery component manufacturing, aerospace, defense, or high-performance industrial gas turbine industries.
  • Experience with CAD/CAM software, preferably NX or similar.
  • Familiarity with CNC machining, additive manufacturing, and other advanced manufacturing technologies.
  • Excellent problem-solving skills and ability to work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.
  • Strong communication and teamwork skills.
  • Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience integrating automation, robotics, or advanced metrology systems (e.g., CMM, optical scanning) into manufacturing workflows.
  • Owned end-to-end equipment development and implementation
  • Designing and fabricating tooling, such as mandrels and other fixture jigs

By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. SUMMARY - ABOUT THE TEAM / JOB
Anduril’s Manufacturing team is seeking a Manufacturing Engineer to join our team. The Propulsion Manufacturing Team is responsible for rapidly iterating and building cutting-edge defense hardware for the Core Technologies Platform. This responsibility includes everything in the manufacturing value-chain, including, but not limited to, Design for Manufacturability work, tool design & selection, process creation & optimization, vendor sourcing & interaction, quality planning, and work documentation associated with the hardware that the Manufacturing Engineer owns.

The right person for this role can demonstrate past holistic ownership on solving a technical challenge with a creative, physical, solution that they either personally manufacturing or oversaw manufacturing on, in a fast-paced, resource-limited environment. If you are someone who thrives in such an environment, then this role is for you.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Own the disposition and rework of engines that fail internal acceptance test or are returned by customers, addressing both hardware failures and upgrades to the latest configuration for the entire program.
  • Diagnose engine-level issues by analyzing test data, inspecting hardware, and driving each failure to its true root cause.
  • Author clear, complete rework instructions and partner closely with production to communicate tasks, priorities, and expectations.
  • Manage configuration across the EBOM and MBOM to keep every engine traceable to its correct build state.
  • Lead teardown and inspection of returned engines, documenting findings and determining whether components are serviceable, repairable, or scrap.
  • Define and manage upgrade paths that bring legacy-configuration engines to the current standard, including the required rework steps and parts.
  • Feed failure findings back to design, quality, and reliability engineering so recurring issues are corrected at the source.
  • Estimate rework scope, cost, and turnaround time, and coordinate with planning and supply chain to signal hardware demand.
  • Verify that every reworked engine meets requirements and passes acceptance testing before it ships to the customer.
  • Maintain accurate as-built records so each engine's final configuration is fully documented after rework.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, or related field; Master's degree preferred.
  • 5+ years of progressive experience in turbomachinery component manufacturing, aerospace, defense, or high-performance industrial gas turbine industries.
  • Experience with CAD/CAM software, preferably NX or similar.
  • Familiarity with CNC machining, additive manufacturing, and other advanced manufacturing technologies.
  • Excellent problem-solving skills and ability to work in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.
  • Strong communication and teamwork skills.
  • Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS (No minimum requirements, maximum ~5-6 bullet points)

  • Experience integrating automation, robotics, or advanced metrology systems (e.g., CMM, optical scanning) into manufacturing workflows.
  • Owned end-to-end equipment development and implementation

ABOUT THE JOB: 

This engineer is our first line of defense on the Imaging production floor. Embedded on the line, they keep hardware moving by rapidly troubleshooting in-line issues, driving down downtime, and resolving the technical and process problems that stand between us and shipping product. This is a hands-on, floor-dedicated sustaining role focused on the assembly, integration, and test of discrete electromechanical and optomechanical systems.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • First Line of Defense: Embed on the production floor to rapidly respond to, diagnose, and resolve in-line production issues across assembly, integration, and test — keeping downtime to an absolute minimum. 
  • Downtime & Ticket Management: Own the response process when the line goes down. Triage, drive, and close production downtime & non-conformance issues, coordinating engineering, maintenance, quality, and supply chain to restore flow quickly.
  • Digital Line Operations: Handle the essential digital administration of the line. Own the day-to-day updates and troubleshooting within our ERP and MES (Manufacturing Execution Systems) to ensure accurate production tracking, data integrity, and inventory flow. 
  • Root Cause & Debugging: Perform rapid debugging, testing, and root-cause analysis (RCA) on failing hardware and processes. Implement containment, drive corrective and preventive actions, and escalate systemic issues to the design and quality teams.
  • Floor Collaboration: Partner hands-on with technicians and assemblers every day, capturing assembly friction points and feeding improvements back into process and design.
  • Documentation & Training: Create, update, and maintain clear, accurate work instructions, SOPs, and rework procedures so the floor always runs to the current standard. Ensure ECO/ECN change implementations are managed and executed on the production floor correctly and on time.
  • Continuous Improvement: Analyze line data to surface recurring failures and bottlenecks, and drive incremental improvements to yield, throughput, and first-pass quality.


REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Degree in a technical field such as mechanical, electrical, systems, or industrial engineering, or a related hard science.
  • 5+ years of hands-on experience supporting an active production line — in manufacturing, production, process, sustainment, or industrial engineering.
  • Demonstrated, hands-on experience troubleshooting, testing, and assembling electromechanical hardware in a live production environment.
  • Demonstrated experience utilizing and managing data within MES (Manufacturing Execution Systems) and ERP platforms to track yields, routing, and inventory.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience in aerospace/defense or another regulated, high-reliability industry, including familiarity with defense terminology and processes.
  • Exposure to ISO 9001 / AS9100 quality systems.
  • Familiarity with optical / opto-mechanical system integration and test.
  • Experience in a high-growth or startup manufacturing environment combined with mature-production rigor (“knows what good looks like”).
  • Familiarity with PLM and WMS platforms.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Connected Warfare is the team at Anduril dedicated to the modernization of the command and control systems of U.S. and Allied forces. New technologies and new adversaries demand a new approach to battlefield intelligence, and our products are rapidly scaling in production to deliver the volumes that our customers need. You will have opportunities to work on products like Menace-I, Menace-X, Menace-T, and TITAN as well as a wide array of future upcoming products. You will be the owner of one of these products in production and you will have the opportunity to drive their production ramps. Your work will help to change the balance of defense capabilities on a global scale. Apply now and become part of our mission to secure a safer tomorrow.

As a Manufacturing Engineer in Connected Warfare, you will be able to be a part of the entire design and manufacturing process for brand new and state of the art command and controls systems. You will have chances to take on large projects and own them from cradle to grave. The right person for this role has a high level of ownership and drive to improve their skills as a Manufacturing Engineer. If you are someone who isn’t afraid of taking on large scale and complex projects or getting outside of your comfort zone and learning about new and challenging concepts, then this role is for you.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Execute the manufacturing of a certain product or set of products, from initial prototyping through large full-scale production.
  • Work with design engineers during the development process to drive design for manufacturing best practices into the design effort, and help facilitate the transition from design to prototype to rate production.
  • Act as a subject matter expert to technicians on the floor helping to solve complex build problems that arise such as, mechanical fitment issues, electrical and harnessing issues, as well as software and firmware issues.
  • Own documentation required for successfully manufacturing products at scale such as MBOM’s, work instructions, process flows, floor plans, time studies, capacity analysis, etc.
  • Collaborate with internal customers and manufacturing planning teams to define capacity planning actions to meet customer needs and expectations.
  • Work hand in hand with the broader production team to solve complex issues to ensure customer demand is met.
  • Analyze metrics for continuous improvement initiatives (cost reduction, QI reduction & capacity increase).
  • Instill a culture of innovation, teamwork, and accountability within the manufacturing engineering product team.
  • Travel to suppliers and partner sites to do initial sourcing work, solve ongoing production issues, and implement process procedures as required.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Degree in a technical field such as engineering, math, or a hard science
  • 5+ years in manufacturing or similar position
  • An attitude of world-class mission assurance, quality, attention to detail, and dedication
  • A genuine interest in manufacturing and thirst for learning
  • Demonstrated ability to creatively deliver hardware in a resource-constrained environment
  • Personal experience physically manufacturing hardware via any means (machining, fabrication, soldering, assembly, etc.). Work on personal or extracurricular projects is a plus
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Top Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience building successful production operations from scratch, often working with very little definition
  • Harness & PCBA fabrication experience or proven competency in mechanical system design and analysis
  • Ownership of a complex bill of materials for an electromechanical product
  • Knowledge of manufacturing processes including sheet metal, machining, and 3D printing
  • Experience in NX/Teamcenter

ABOUT THE TEAM 

Anduril is fielding the next generation of Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) to tackle the extremely challenging industry demands of seabed exploration. Founded in 2018 by a group of experts in the AUV industry, Anduril has brought to the market a unique, ultra-long-range, full-ocean-depth platform and a completely refreshed maritime vehicle and flexible manufacturing architecture that scales from “large” to “extra-large” vehicle sizes. Today, Anduril is executing on multi-million-dollar contracts for the US Navy and DARPA while simultaneously performing Robot-as-a-Service (RaaS) commercial surveys. Anduril is a well-funded, venture-backed team with over 100-years of combined AUV experience from organizations such as Liquid Robotics, Teledyne, Bluefin Robotics, Oceaneering, the US Navy, and more.

As our team continues to quickly grow, we are looking for motivated candidates that are inspired to work within an extremely energetic, creative, and innovative team that is passionate about subsea robotics and exploring the open ocean. We work in a highly dynamic environment where collaboration and idea sharing are a way of life.

ABOUT THE JOB 

We are seeking a Manufacturing Test Engineer to join Anduril, working in a cutting-edge start-up environment to advance the state-of-the-possible in subsea robotics. The Manufacturing Test Engineer will be charged with developing and implementing high-fidelity, acceptance test procedures for Anduril’s portfolio of AUV’s. Working closely with engineering staff and a team of skilled electro-mechanical technicians, this role is key to advancing our testing capabilities to ensure the highest levels quality are achieved as we continue drive scalability into our production operations.

WHAT YOU’LL DO 

  • Optimize test design and execution of offshore acceptance testing of AUV’s, including test plan generation, fixture development, and data analysis tools.
  • Collaborate with Systems/Test and Evaluation teams throughout product development cycles to perform risk assessments, transition test campaign to operationalized production testing, drive reductions in offshore acceptance test cycles, and mature in-factory acceptance testing within production line.
  • Develop automated post-mission analysis tools to evaluate vehicle performance through acceptance test.
  • Build a broad range of test capabilities across the manufacturing value stream - from system level checkouts and acceptance testing to key component level in process validation.
  • Develop, execute, and manage test eco-system to de-risk hardware and ensure product meets target reliability levels and ultimate design intent.
  • Perform hands-on and data-driven root cause analysis of electromechanical subsystems utilizing structured problem solving methodologies.
  • Design and implement semi-automated testing equipment/protocols for subsystem characterization and reliability/environmental testing.
  • Produce and maintain testing logs/data, develop library of error codes with troubleshooting logic/diagrams for fast issue resolution.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree in Mechanical, EE/Computer Engineering, Ocean Engineering or related field, or equivalent work experience
  • 5+ years of experience in a relevant field, preferably test design of electro-mechanical hardware in a manufacturing environment
  • Experience in analyzing or reviewing sonar and/or acoustic data from subsea sensors
  • Well versed with Autonomous Underwater Vehicles and/or offshore robotics testing and are passionate about understanding what it takes to make them work reliably
  • Proficiency in programming languages such as Python, Matlab, SHELL, or others
  • Have experience developing full system test plans and know how to execute them on fast-paced product development timelines
  • Have experience with programming/testing a wide range of sensors, actuators, and electrical components
  • Bias for action – if you see a problem, you want to solve and fix it
  • Can prototype and run your own tests, from experimental setup to hardware and software implementation
  • Must be eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 

  • Familiar with Product Life Cycle (PLM) systems, Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), and Test Execution Systems (TES)
  • Demonstrated ability to learn new skills or adapt to new situations. Un-phased by challenges that go beyond the traditional comfort zone or work experience. Multidisciplinary approach to problem solving
  • Comfortable with high project ownership under technical and schedule pressure, particularly where the scope and definition are limited
  • Experience testing and operating with or around hazardous systems (high voltage up to 400V)
  • Experience working on projects that involve the integration of electrical, mechanical, and software/firmware systems

  • Author and negotiate Launch Requirements Documents and Interface Control Documents (ICDs) that define the mechanical, electrical, and environmental interfaces between the spacecraft and launch vehicle
  • Coordinate delivery of analysis and data products to and from the launch provider – mass properties, coupled loads analysis (CLA) inputs and results, structural and thermal FEMs, separation and clearance analyses, range safety documentation, MSDS, and test reports
  • Define and verify spacecraft compatibility with launch environments (quasi-static, vibration, acoustic, shock, and thermal), reconciling launch provider levels against the spacecraft design and test program
  • Own the verification and compliance matrix against launch provider requirements for spacecraft and payloads
  • Plan and lead launch site operations – transport, fit-checks, propellant loading support, integrated testing, encapsulation, and day-of-launch activities
  • Support integration and readiness reviews (e.g., MRR, LRR, FRR) and present launch readiness status internally and to customers
  • Work with internal teams and government agencies to obtain the required licenses and approvals (FAA, FCC, NOAA, etc.) and comply with range safety and orbital debris mitigation regulations for launching spacecraft
  • Triage issues, conduct root cause investigations, and drive lessons learned from each launch campaign into simpler, more standardized processes across programs
  • Create excellent technical documentation – integration plans, interface control documents, procedures, test reports
  • Travel to launch sites, ranges, and vendors as needed, including extended and international campaign support and off-nominal launch operations

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • BS or higher degree in engineering or a hard science, ideally in Mechanical or Aerospace Engineering
  • Experience conducting launch integration operations with an emphasis on simplicity, safety, and reliability
  • Experience interfacing with launch vehicle providers and spacecraft development teams, including the products exchanged – ICDs, mass properties, coupled loads, environments, and separation systems
  • Ability to quickly understand and navigate detailed requirements
  • Highly motivated and capable of solving complex technical problems with little oversight
  • Clear communication and organizational skills including documentation and training material
  • Excellent attention to detail
  • Willing to establish scope and requirements for ill-defined problems
  • A desire to work on critical spacecraft systems in support of the U.S. government and her allies
  • Be able to obtain and hold a U.S. Top Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience writing code or automating functions to improve efficiency and delivery to customers and launch providers (Python, MATLAB, etc.)
  • Experience supporting spacecraft environmental test campaigns (structural, thermal-vacuum, EMI/EMC)
  • Experience designing and integrating mechanical and electrical ground support equipment for environmental test and launch integration campaigns
  • Familiarity with launch vehicle user’s guides and with ride-share and dedicated launch provider interface and environmental requirements
  • Direct experience running coupled loads, separation and clearance, or structural and thermal analyses
  • Experience working as a stack integrator and coordinating interfaces across multiple spacecraft providers
  • Familiarity with range safety, launch licensing, and orbital debris mitigation (e.g., FAA Part 450, ODMSP, NASA-STD-8719.14)

  • Develop and review prototype requirements, execute against build milestones, and lead sourcing activities

  • Lead risk assessments and investigations for packaging-related issues in transportation and storage
  • Utilize ERP & WMS software systems and tools to track packaging inventory, generate reports, and provide data-driven insights to support decision-making and optimization measures
  • Ensure compliance with regulatory requirements, safety standards, and quality control protocols in all material management activities

  • Bachelor’s degree in engineering
  • 5+ years of experience in packaging engineering in a high-rate supply chain or manufacturing environment, where complex mechanical and/or electrical assemblies are built
  • Ability to travel up to 25% of the time
  • Ability to relocate, if not already local to be onsite in Costa Mesa, CA
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering or materials engineering
  • Experience with packaging solutions in the automotive, defense, semiconductor, or other relevant industries
  • Experience or familiarity with relevant defense packaging and transportation standards
  • Strong knowledge of supply chain principles, inventory management techniques, and material planning strategies
  • Detail-oriented, highly organized, and capable of managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment
  • Proficiency in using software systems and tools, such as AutoCAD, SolidWorks, PackAssistant
  • Prior knowledge of NetSuite, Oracle or a similar Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) system
  • Familiarity with MIL specs
  • Knowledge of hazardous material packaging and compliance

ABOUT THE JOB

Anduril Industries is seeking a highly technical and strategic Senior Color, Material, and Finish (CMF) Designer to join the Industrial Design team in our Bellevue, WA office. In this role, you will define and implement CMF standards across a diverse hardware portfolio supporting the Warfighter Systems team. You will translate the industrial design vision into scalable, production-ready solutions by establishing design quality standards and partnering with global manufacturing teams to execute them on the factory floor. 

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Define, develop, and scale a holistic CMF strategy across Anduril’s Warfighter Systems hardware portfolio.
  • Identify and evaluate advanced materials, innovative coatings, and sustainable manufacturing processes that support product performance, durability, and design intent.
  • Lead on-site color-matching sessions and evaluate physical parts under standardized lighting conditions.
  • Factory execution and quality standards: Serve as the subject-matter expert for visual and cosmetic quality at supplier and manufacturing sites.
  • Establish, document, and implement Cosmetic Quality Specification(CQS) with global manufacturing partners.
  • CMF documentation: Create and maintain comprehensive CMF specifications, approved boundary and limit samples, and step-and-gap requirements to ensure assembly precision and surface consistency.

Anduril's Space team is dedicated to expanding our AI-powered capabilities into the final frontier, enhancing Space Domain Awareness, Space Control, and Command and Control for U.S. military and allied partners. We're developing fully integrated hardware and software systems, including Lattice for Space Missions and modular payloads, to address growing threats in space and ensure our Guardians maintain a decisive advantage in this contested warfighting domain.

ABOUT THE JOB

You'll own the production readiness of space hardware — take maturing and flight-proven designs and drive them to repeatable, higher-rate manufacturing. Intelligently pace design changes with a holistic view of the program and its build schedule.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Use first principles as a basis for decisions and continuously look for opportunities to simplify designs, reduce part count, and design for manufacturing, assembly, and test (DFM/DFA/DFT) — improving producibility, repeatability, and reliability at higher production quantities
  • Modify and mature existing designs to resolve problems realized in production – fit, tolerance, assembly, and yield issues
  • Update designs to reduce build and test cycle times, improve first-pass yield, and remove bottlenecks from assembly, integration, and test (AI&T) operations
  • Own bills of material (BOMs) and engineering drawings – release and maintain part and assembly drawings, GD&T, and BOM structure; process engineering changes (ECO/ECN) and manage revisions and effectivity
  • Propagate engineering changes through assembly hierarchies — revise parent assembly models, drawings, and BOMs when subcomponent designs change, ensuring next-higher-level documentation stays current and consistent
  • Act as the Responsible Engineer for your hardware in production: disposition nonconformances, author red-lines and rework/retrofit instructions
  • Partner with manufacturing, supply chain, and test engineering to transition designs from low-rate to higher-rate production and to stand up repeatable work instructions, tooling, and fixtures
  • Build and validate prototypes and production trial builds, analyze failures, and feed lessons learned back into the design and the build process
  • Travel to test sites, production facilities, and vendors as needed
  • Create excellent technical documentation – assembly and work instructions, procedures, test plans and reports, vendor specifications and statements of work, etc.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • BS or higher degree in engineering or a hard science
  • CAD skills (any platform) and ability to make high quality engineering drawings that meet common industry standards, including GD&T
  • Experience taking hardware designs into manufacturing and production – design for manufacturing/assembly and drawing release. Experience transitioning hardware from prototype or low-rate to higher-rate production
  • Working knowledge of BOM structures, revision control, and engineering change orders (ECO/ECN), ideally within a PLM/PDM system
  • Demonstrated hands-on fabrication and assembly skills. Experience working with hand tools, mill, lathe, etc.
  • Strong understanding of engineering fundamentals: heat transfer, statics, solid mechanics, materials
  • Familiarity with tolerance analysis and inspection methods
  • Excellent attention to detail
  • Highly motivated, self-starting, and able to perform duties autonomously without supervision
  • Very organized and willing to establish scope and requirements for ill-defined problems
  • Passion for defending the United States and her allies
  • Be able to obtain and hold a U.S. Top Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 4+ years of mechanical design or production/sustaining engineering experience in a professional setting with space hardware
  • Experience in NX/Teamcenter or equivalent CAD/PLM
  • Experience with nonconformance disposition and Material Review Board, root cause and corrective action (RCCA), and first article inspection (FAI)
  • Experience designing tooling, fixtures, and ground support equipment to improve build and test throughput
  • Ability to integrate electronic components (PCBAs, motors, sensors, etc.) into mechanical designs
  • Experience developing code in higher-level languages (e.g. Python, MATLAB, C++) for analytical models, data acquisition, and automation
  • Experience with statistical process control, tolerance stack-ups, or design of experiments (DOE) to improve yield

About the Role

Anduril Industries is building next-generation defense technology to protect the United States and its allies. We are looking for Production Technicians to join our Rocket Motor Systems manufacturing team. In this role, you will perform hands-on final assembly operations on solid rocket motors and their subassemblies, working in a fast-paced production environment where precision, safety, and teamwork are paramount.

You do not need prior experience with solid rocket motors or energetic materials to be successful here — we will train you. What matters most is that you bring a strong safety mindset, a willingness to learn, the technical aptitude to master detailed procedures, and the ability to work collaboratively with your team.

Core Responsibilities

  • Perform solid rocket motor final assembly operations including mandrel extraction, nozzle installation, and igniter assembly integration per detailed work instructions
  • Execute igniter subassembly build-up, including component preparation, epoxy application, and curing processes
  • Conduct motor marking, labeling, and serialization in accordance with configuration control requirements
  • Perform leak check and pressure testing of completed motor assemblies using calibrated test equipment
  • Complete pack-out and preparation of finished motors for storage or shipment, ensuring compliance with packaging and handling specifications
  • Maintain accurate and thorough records of all assembly operations, inspections, and test results in the production tracking system
  • Participate in daily production stand-ups, communicate status and blockers, and coordinate handoffs between shifts or stations

Safety & Compliance

  • Solid propellant and other energetic materials are exceptionally dangerous if mishandled — adhere strictly to all safety protocols, standard operating procedures, and explosive safety requirements at all times with zero tolerance for deviation
  • Maintain housekeeping and Foreign Object Debris (FOD) control standards in all work areas
  • Identify and escalate safety concerns, near-misses, and hazards immediately through established reporting channels
  • Use required Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) correctly and consistently
  • Support and participate in safety audits, process hazard analyses, and continuous improvement initiatives

What We're Looking For

We hire for mindset and aptitude. If you've built things with your hands — whether in a factory, a shop, the military, or your own garage — and you take pride in doing precise, careful work, we want to hear from you.

Required

  • High school diploma or equivalent
  • Demonstrated safety-first mindset — you stop the line when something doesn't look right
  • Ability to follow detailed written and visual work instructions with precision and consistency
  • Moderate to high mechanical aptitude: comfortable working with hand tools, torque wrenches, fixtures, and small components
  • Strong attention to detail and quality — you catch your own mistakes before they move downstream
  • Team-oriented attitude with clear, direct communication skills
  • Coachable and self-aware — you seek feedback, absorb it, and apply it
  • Ability to lift up to 35 lbs and stand for extended periods
  • Willingness to work in environments with energetic materials after completing required training and certification
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. security clearance (U.S. citizenship required)
  • Ability to obtain and maintain an ATF Explosives "Employee Possessor" license

Preferred

  • Experience in aerospace, defense, automotive, or other precision manufacturing environments
  • Familiarity with AS9100, ISO 9001, or equivalent aerospace quality management systems
  • Experience working with adhesives, sealants, epoxies, or potting compounds
  • Military service or experience in an environment with strict procedural discipline
  • Experience with calibrated measurement tools (micrometers, calipers, pin gauges, etc.)
  • Lean manufacturing, 5S, or continuous improvement experience

Why Anduril

  • Mission-driven work — what you build matters for national security
  • A team culture that values safety, ownership, and getting better every day
  • Competitive compensation, equity, and benefits
  • Hands-on training and career growth pathways into senior technician, lead, and supervisory roles
  • The opportunity to build a production operation from the ground up alongside a tight-knit team

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Follow detailed blueprints, schematics, instructions, and CAD models to assemble products or systems
  • Use various hand tools and power tools to put components together

  • Follow safety protocols and procedures in the workplace
  • Possibility for overtime and weekend shifts as needed
