ABOUT THE TEAM

The Robotics Data Foundation (RDF) team builds Anduril's vehicle telemetry backbone, from onboard systems to cloud. This includes onboard data recording and backhaul, ingestion into our cloud data platform, normalizing data across flight controllers and vehicle management systems, mission systems, and sensor payloads, and making it available to a range of downstream 1st and 3rd-party analysis tools. Our vehicle telemetry platform powers software and hardware development, T&E workflows, production incident response, and contractual customer reporting today, and underpins new product development, fleet-wide analysis, simulation, and machine learning workflows. Anduril sits on the world's largest defense robotics data asset, and the RDF team is working to operationalize that across the board.

ABOUT THE JOB

As an engineer on the Robotics Data Foundation team, you will design and build the Anduril-wide cloud systems that host our ingestion pipelines, storage systems, and tooling that carry vehicle telemetry from onboard systems to the cloud and make it discoverable, searchable, and analyzable across the fleet. You'll normalize data across flight controllers, vehicle management systems, mission systems, and sensor payloads, and expose it to downstream 1st- and 3rd-party analysis tools, and build infrastructure that supports large-scale batch ingestion of recorded telemetry, as well as low-latency streaming.

  • Build reliable and performant cloud data systems: Our software ingests high volumes of telemetry across Anduril, so the systems we ship must be high-availability and stable when processing high-scale vehicle telemetry.
  • Design extensible telemetry and data architectures: Robotics teams have diverse data sources that are often unique to a platform or sensor. Our architecture must enable easy integration of bespoke data sources into our standardized ingestion framework.
  • Enable data-driven engineering in real-time: We own the software that delivers live telemetry streams and recorded data to cloud destinations and analysis tools so engineers, operators, and test teams across locations can understand their systems in real-time.
  • Build and develop cloud-native systems that are also edge-compatible: While we are responsible for delivering an excellent cloud data platform experience for all teams across Anduril, we also deliver a subset of capabilities to edge nodes to facilitate telemetry capture in offline / air-gapped settings. You will also be responsible for fielding data systems to classified environments.
  • Eagerly engage with our customers: We partner closely with business line engineering teams to understand their specific data requirements and iteratively deliver solutions that meet their particular needs and constraints.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience with modern lakehouse architectures (Iceberg, Delta Lake), ETL systems (Flyte, Dagster, Airflow, Argo Workflows), and distributed data processing engines (Spark, Trino, etc.).
  • Experience developing and operating high-throughput streaming data pipelines (leveraging systems like Spark Streaming, Flink, Kafka).
  • Strong proficiency in Python, Java, Rust, and/or Go (the team predominantly uses Python & Rust for core backend services and pipelines).
  • Experience building and operating cloud systems, including common containerization and deployability technologies (Docker, Kubernetes, GitOps systems like FluxCD / ArgoCD).
  • U.S. Person status is required as this position needs to access export controlled data. Eligibility to obtain/maintain a US Top Secret clearance is also desirable.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Special Projects team within Finance helps lead Anduril's financing strategy, complex strategic transactions, and cross-functional initiatives that don't sit neatly within any one org. We structure and lead negotiations on some of Anduril's largest and most complex deals – financing transactions with banks and investors, and major commercial engagements with customers – owning those processes from internal framing through execution. The work requires getting close to the business: we partner directly with operations, contracts, supply chain, and division finance teams to understand the economics and operating constraints, develop a point of view, and drive decisions. Beyond transactions, we take on high-priority problems that span functions or lack a clear owner, working with the relevant teams from initial analysis through implementation.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a Special Projects, Finance team member to join our growing team in Costa Mesa, CA. You will have real ownership early, taking on a mix of live transactions and high-priority projects and driving them from initial analysis through execution. The role combines the financial rigor of investing with far closer proximity to the business: you will build the analysis, form a view, work directly with the teams closest to the problem, and turn decisions into action. You should be comfortable working through incomplete information, going deep when the details matter, and moving between financial models, operating discussions, and recommendations to senior leadership. This is a role for someone with a strong foundation in investment banking and buyout private equity who wants broader scope and more direct ownership than either seat typically offers.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Own the financial models behind Anduril's financings, strategic transactions, and major investment decisions end-to-end – sizing, structural alternatives, and downside scenarios.
  • Drive the analytical workstream on live transactions from first framing through close – pressure-testing terms, building diligence materials, and tracking where each negotiating position actually lands.
  • Build operating models that connect the underlying business to financial outcomes. Get deep into how a factory ramps, what a program costs to execute, and where the business is exposed, then translate that analysis for banks, investors, and other external counterparties.
  • Build durable frameworks for capital allocation and investment decisions across new facilities, capacity expansion, vertical integration, and other non-routine commitments.
  • Go get the data yourself. Work directly with supply chain, manufacturing, contracts, and program teams, pull from our corporate systems, and reconcile messy inputs into numbers you would defend line by line.
  • Own ambiguous initiatives that have no natural owner. Frame the problem, build the analysis, land on a recommendation, and drive it through implementation.
  • Present directly to senior leadership and work across functions, from Legal and Accounting to Supply Chain and Manufacturing. You will be expected to defend your analysis, navigate competing priorities, and bring a group that does not report to you to a decision.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 3-5 years of experience, including time at a top-tier investment bank and at a buyout private equity firm – ideally with both LevFin or Restructuring experience and industrials coverage.
  • Exceptional financial modeling ability. You can build detailed, structurally sound models from the ground up, but also know when a quick analysis is enough to make the decision at hand.
  • Strong command of debt financing structures, capital structure, and credit. You understand how financing decisions affect the operating decisions that follow.
  • Real business judgment and an operational tilt. You can see what actually drives a program's economics and which assumptions are critical, even from messy and incomplete information. You are excited to be in the program reviews and on the factory floor where those answers come from.
  • A first-principles thinker with strong institutional grounding. You know the standard playbook well enough to know when to use it – and when the problem calls for something else.
  • Extremely high agency. You are comfortable working through genuinely hard problems, don't wait to be told to move, and can sprint when the situation demands it.
  • Comfortable presenting to large, extremely senior audiences and company leadership.
  • Demonstrated interest in industrial and defense technology.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Direct operating experience inside a company, ideally in a high-growth environment. Candidates combining investment banking, buyout private equity, and operating experience are particularly compelling.
  • Direct project finance, structured finance, or dedicated financing transaction experience.
  • Deep exposure to industrials, aerospace and defense, or manufacturing businesses, whether through coverage, deal work, or time at a portfolio company.
  • Former founder or early-stage operator – you have built something without a playbook.
  • Undergraduate degree in a STEM, engineering, or quantitative major.

Anduril's Air Dominance & Strike (AD&S) Manufacturing Engineering team is seeking a Staff DFx Engineer to serve as the technical authority on design for manufacturability, assembly, and cost across our mechanical, structural, thermal management, and fluid systems (fuel, hydraulics, pneumatics) subsystems. This role spans our full portfolio of autonomous aircraft, cruise missiles, and loitering munitions — ensuring that every design decision accounts for how hardware will be built, by whom, and at what cost.
You will bring deep specialty expertise in at least one — and ideally two — of the following domains: mechanical structures and assemblies, thermal/heat transfer systems, or fluid systems including fuel, hydraulic, and pneumatic architectures. Your primary focus areas are manufacturability, assembly, and cost — the three lenses that determine whether a design can be produced at rate, by a qualified supplier, at an affordable price point. You are not reviewing designs in the abstract; you are shaping them to be buildable.
A critical part of this role is working directly with subject matter expert (SME) manufacturing engineers and design engineers to evaluate producibility and drive design improvements. You will also play a key role in the selection and qualification of contract manufacturers — assessing supplier capabilities against DFx requirements and ensuring that external production partners can deliver to the quality, rate, and cost targets our programs demand. This is an inherently cross-functional role: you will work daily with supply chain, quality, operations, and program teams in addition to ME and DE.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Own and drive DFx analysis across mechanical, structural, thermal, and fluid systems subsystems for AD&S programs, with a primary focus on manufacturability, assembly, and cost.
  • Lead structured DFM/DFA/DFC reviews at key design milestones, applying rigorous scoring to identify producibility and cost risks and drive design changes before they reach production.
  • Lead/facilitate DFMEAs with cross-functional teams. Use FMEA outputs to drive design changes, inspection strategies, and control plans.
  • Work directly with SME manufacturing engineers and design engineers to evaluate designs, translate manufacturing constraints into actionable feedback, and negotiate design trades that balance performance, producibility, and cost.
  • Assist in the selection and qualification of contract manufacturers for machined components, fabrications, composite structures, thermal management hardware, and fluid system assemblies — assessing supplier manufacturing capability, process maturity, and cost competitiveness against DFx requirements.
  • Conduct supplier manufacturing assessments including facility reviews, process audits, and capability evaluations to determine readiness for production qualification.
  • Develop and maintain should-cost models and cost-driver analyses for mechanical and fluid system assemblies, identifying design changes that reduce unit cost without compromising quality or performance.
  • Develop and maintain DFx standards, guidelines, and scorecards specific to mechanical manufacturing processes including CNC machining, sheet metal fabrication, welding, brazing, composite layup and bonding, tube bending and swaging, casting, forging, and mechanical assembly.
  • Analyze designs across key lenses — manufacturability/assembly, cost structure, adherence to specification, process capability, and technology maturity — to produce quantified risk assessments that inform engineering and program decisions.
  • Evaluate thermal management designs (heat exchangers, cold plates, thermal interface materials, cooling loops) for manufacturability and cost-effective production at rate.
  • Assess fuel, hydraulic, and pneumatic system designs for producibility — including tube routing, fitting selection, seal and joint design, leak test strategies, and cleanliness requirements.
  • Partner with supply chain to align DFx requirements with sourcing strategy, ensuring that designs are producible by the suppliers we intend to use.
  • Collaborate with quality engineering to ensure DFx findings flow into inspection plans, acceptance criteria, and supplier quality requirements.
  • Close the loop between production floor feedback, supplier performance data, and upstream design improvements.
  • Build and evolve the DFx toolkit — templates, scoring rubrics, cost models, lessons-learned databases, and training materials — so that DFx knowledge scales across the organization.
  • Mentor and develop junior and mid-level engineers on DFx principles, cost analysis techniques, and supplier assessment methods.
  • Travel to production sites, contract manufacturers, and supplier facilities (~20%, depending on business needs).

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related field.
  • 12+ years of experience in manufacturing engineering, producibility engineering, or DFx with a significant focus on mechanical systems, thermal management, or fluid systems — with deep specialty expertise in at least one of these domains.
  • Strong technical depth in mechanical manufacturing processes: CNC machining, sheet metal fabrication, welding (TIG, MIG, electron beam, friction stir), brazing, composite layup and cure, bonding, casting, forging, and complex mechanical assembly.
  • Demonstrated experience leading DFM/DFA reviews and translating findings into measurable design improvements that reduce cost and improve producibility.
  • Experience evaluating and qualifying contract manufacturers — including facility assessments, process capability reviews, and production readiness evaluations.
  • Strong understanding of cost drivers in mechanical and fluid system production, with experience building or contributing to should-cost models.
  • Ability to read and critically evaluate mechanical drawings, GD&T, 3D models, and assembly documentation for producibility and cost impact.
  • Working knowledge of relevant standards and specifications for aerospace mechanical and fluid systems (AS9100, NAS, AN/MS fittings, SAE AS specifications for fluid components).
  • Proven ability to work cross-functionally across design engineering, manufacturing engineering, supply chain, quality, and operations — and to influence decisions through technical credibility.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present DFx and cost findings to engineering leadership and drive alignment on design changes.
  • Experience with Full Size Determinant Assembly (FSDA).
  • Comfortable working across multiple programs simultaneously in a fast-paced, high-growth environment.
  • Personal experience in a machine shop, fabrication shop, or on a production floor working with mechanical hardware. Hands-on credibility matters.
  • Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export controlled information or facilities.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Master's degree in engineering or a related field.
  • Deep specialty expertise in two or more of: mechanical structures, thermal/heat transfer systems, fuel systems, hydraulic systems.
  • Experience in aerospace or defense mechanical production, particularly with qualified or flight-critical hardware.
  • Familiarity with AS9100/AS9102 quality management systems and First Article Inspection processes.
  • Experience with composite manufacturing (autoclave cure, out-of-autoclave, RTM) and associated DFM considerations.
  • Proficiency in CAD software (NX, CATIA, SolidWorks, or similar) sufficient to review designs independently.
  • Background in Design of Experiments (DOE), statistical process control, or Six Sigma applied to mechanical manufacturing.
  • Experience with value engineering or formal cost reduction programs in a production environment.
  • Knowledge of fluid system cleanliness, proof/burst testing, and qualification requirements for aerospace applications.
  • Currently possesses and is able to maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance with Full-Scope Polygraph.

Anduril's Air Dominance & Strike (AD&S) Manufacturing Engineering team is seeking a Propulsion Manufacturing Engineer to provide subject matter expertise on propulsion system manufacturing across our portfolio of autonomous aircraft, cruise missiles, and loitering munitions. This position may be filled at either the Senior or Staff level depending on experience and qualifications. This role covers the full spectrum of propulsion technologies relevant to AD&S — air-breathing jet turbines, ramjets, and solid rocket motors — and is responsible for ensuring that propulsion hardware can be manufactured, assembled, tested, and integrated at production rate with the quality and reliability our programs demand.
You will bring deep expertise in the manufacturing processes, materials, and quality requirements specific to propulsion systems. Your knowledge of how these systems are built — from turbine blade casting and combustor fabrication to solid propellant processing and nozzle manufacturing — is what makes you valuable. You are the person who knows what can go wrong in propulsion production and how to prevent it through design influence, process control, and supplier qualification.
A critical part of this role is working directly with design engineers and program-level manufacturing engineers to evaluate propulsion designs for producibility, drive DFM improvements, and support the selection and qualification of propulsion suppliers and contract manufacturers. You will also support propulsion system test campaigns from a manufacturing engineering perspective, including integration, acceptance testing, and anomaly resolution. This is an inherently cross-functional role: you will work daily with supply chain, quality, operations, test engineering, and program teams.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Serve as a propulsion manufacturing engineering subject matter expert across AD&S programs, covering air-breathing turbines, ramjets, and solid rocket motors.
  • Evaluate propulsion system designs for manufacturability, assembly, and cost — leading or supporting DFM/DFA reviews and driving design changes that improve producibility without compromising performance.
  • Work directly with design engineers and program manufacturing engineers to translate propulsion manufacturing constraints into actionable design feedback.
  • Assist in the selection and qualification of propulsion suppliers and contract manufacturers — assessing manufacturing capability, process maturity, quality systems, and cost competitiveness for propulsion-specific production.
  • Conduct or participate in supplier manufacturing assessments for propulsion hardware, including facility reviews, process audits, special process qualification (casting, brazing, propellant processing, thermal spray), and production readiness evaluations.
  • Develop and maintain manufacturing process requirements and standards for propulsion-specific processes including turbine component manufacturing, combustor and hot section fabrication, solid propellant mixing and casting, nozzle manufacturing, and propulsion system assembly and integration.
  • Support propulsion system test campaigns from a manufacturing engineering perspective — including hardware preparation, instrumentation integration, acceptance test criteria, and post-test hardware disposition and anomaly investigation.
  • Develop or contribute to should-cost models and cost-driver analyses for propulsion assemblies and components, identifying design and process changes that reduce unit cost at rate production.
  • Partner with quality engineering to define or support inspection plans, acceptance criteria, and process controls specific to propulsion hardware — including non-destructive testing (NDT), dimensional inspection, and material certification requirements.
  • Collaborate with supply chain to align propulsion manufacturing requirements with sourcing strategy, including long-lead material planning and sole/single source risk mitigation.
  • Close the loop between production and test feedback, supplier performance data, and upstream design and process improvements.
  • Build and maintain propulsion manufacturing knowledge within the ME organization — developing training materials, lessons-learned databases, and technical reference documents.
  • Mentor and develop junior and mid-level engineers on propulsion manufacturing principles and supplier assessment methods (Staff level).
  • Travel to production sites, propulsion suppliers, and test facilities (~20%, depending on business needs).

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, or a related field.
  • 12+ years of experience in propulsion manufacturing, propulsion engineering, or a closely related manufacturing discipline — with expertise in at least one propulsion type: air-breathing turbines, ramjets, or solid rocket motors.
  • Strong technical knowledge of propulsion-specific manufacturing processes relevant to your area of expertise. Depending on specialty, this may include: investment casting and single-crystal blade production, combustor and hot section fabrication (welding, brazing, thermal barrier coatings), solid propellant formulation, mixing, casting and curing, nozzle and throat insert manufacturing (ablatives, refractory metals, carbon-carbon composites), ramjet combustor and inlet manufacturing, or propulsion system assembly, integration, and acceptance testing.
  • Experience evaluating propulsion designs for manufacturability and translating findings into measurable improvements.
  • Experience evaluating or qualifying propulsion suppliers — including special process qualification and production readiness assessments.
  • Understanding of cost drivers in propulsion production, with experience building or contributing to should-cost models.
  • Ability to read and critically evaluate propulsion system drawings, specifications, and test requirements for manufacturing implications.
  • Working knowledge of relevant propulsion standards and specifications (MIL-STD, SAE AMS, JANNAF, AIAA standards as applicable).
  • Proven ability to work cross-functionally across design engineering, manufacturing engineering, test engineering, supply chain, quality, and operations.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present technical findings to engineering leadership and drive alignment on design and process changes.

ABOUT THE JOB:

This Staff SRE role sets the reliability architecture for the systems that run Anduril’s business and manufacturing operations. You are not responding to tickets. You are the person who decides how production works: how services are observed, how deployments are safe, how incidents are managed, and how reliability scales as the platform grows. You own the infrastructure and mechanisms that make reliability a property of the platform rather than a function of individual heroics.

The role carries broad organizational reach. You will influence how software engineering teams across CorpTech Platform build and operate their systems, set the standards that govern production readiness, and make infrastructure decisions that affect every service in the portfolio. You bring both deep systems expertise and the judgment to know which reliability investments matter most at each stage of the platform’s growth.

WHAT YOU"LL DO:

  • Set the reliability architecture for CorpTech Platform’s production environment, including observability infrastructure, deployment systems, incident management, capacity planning, and failure-domain isolation.
  • Design and operate the observability platform, including metrics, distributed tracing, structured logging, alerting, and dashboarding infrastructure that gives engineering teams real production visibility at scale.
  • Own deployment infrastructure and release-safety mechanisms, including progressive rollout systems, canary analysis, automated rollback, and deployment gates that let the organization ship fast without gambling on production stability.
  • Define and govern SLO frameworks that make reliability measurable and actionable, creating shared language between SRE, product engineering, and leadership for making trade-off decisions.
  • Identify systemic reliability risks across the platform and drive infrastructure or automation investments that eliminate entire failure classes rather than patching individual symptoms.
  • Establish production-readiness standards and review processes that engineering teams adopt during design and pre-launch, embedding reliability into the development lifecycle rather than bolting it on after release.
  • Lead incident response for complex, multi-system failures and drive post-incident processes that produce durable systemic improvements rather than shallow fixes.
  • Develop reliability patterns for AI-enabled systems, including monitoring for model behavior drift, non-deterministic output degradation, and graceful fallback under novel failure modes.
  • Provide technical direction to SRE and infrastructure engineers, facilitate cross-team architecture decisions, and represent reliability concerns in platform-level planning and prioritization.
  • Drive capacity planning, cost optimization, and performance engineering for the platform’s critical paths and shared infrastructure.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 10+ years of experience in site reliability engineering, production engineering, infrastructure engineering, or a closely related discipline, including experience operating at architecture or platform-wide scope.
  • Demonstrated experience designing and owning reliability infrastructure that multiple engineering teams depend on, including observability platforms, deployment systems, or incident management tooling at meaningful scale.
  • Deep technical fluency across distributed systems, container orchestration (Kubernetes), cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, or Azure), networking, storage, and the failure modes specific to each layer.
  • Proficiency in systems programming languages (Go, Python, Rust, or equivalent) used for building production infrastructure, tooling, and automation.
  • Demonstrated experience defining SRE standards, production-readiness frameworks, or operational maturity models and influencing adoption across engineering teams without formal authority.
  • Track record of leading incident response for complex, multi-system failures and converting post-incident findings into infrastructure investments that prevent recurrence.
  • Proven ability to work independently through ambiguity, define reliability strategy without top-down direction, and sequence investments against competing organizational demands.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence senior engineers, engineering leadership, and cross-functional partners on infrastructure and reliability decisions.
  • Degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Engineering, or related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
  • U.S. Person status is required as this position needs to access export controlled data.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Experience designing or operating observability platforms (Datadog, Grafana, Prometheus, OpenTelemetry) at organizational scale, including decisions about instrumentation standards, data pipelines, retention, and cost management.
  • Experience building deployment and release-safety infrastructure, including canary systems, progressive delivery, feature flagging, and automated rollback mechanisms.
  • Experience with reliability engineering for AI-enabled or ML-serving systems, including monitoring non-deterministic behavior, building evaluation-driven alerts, and designing graceful degradation for model failures.
  • Familiarity with frontier AI tooling, AI coding assistants, and AI-enabled software development workflows.
  • Experience in hyper growth startup-like environments, with demonstrated success scaling reliability practices alongside rapid engineering growth.
  • Familiarity with enterprise systems and business process domains such as ERP, MES, WMS, CRM, finance systems, or manufacturing systems.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret security clearance.

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Anduril Imaging team develops state-of-the-art imaging systems across both hardware and software, deployed to tackle the most significant security challenges of America and its allies. The team is heavily involved in utilizing computer vision, perception, electro-optical, infrared, and sensor data to give the US and its allies an advantage. We are extending that capability into orbit — building space-based EO/IR and sensing payloads under a New Space philosophy: aggressive schedules, commercial-cadence engineering, and a relentless bias toward flying hardware. Our standard is to take a payload from architecture to orbit in a year or less, not the multi-year timelines that have traditionally defined space programs.

ABOUT THE JOB

As a System Architect on the Anduril Imaging team, you will own the electronics architecture for space-bound imaging payloads and drive their design from concept through flight. This is a system-level role for an engineer who can hold the whole payload in their head — defining the electrical architecture, making the build-versus-buy and COTS-versus-rad-hard tradeoffs that keep schedule and cost in check, and then going hands-on to lay out, bring up, and qualify the hardware. You will set the technical direction for power, sensor, and interface electronics, and remain hands-on to see your individual designs take flight. You will work in rapid design cycles where the goal is to get capable, robust hardware into space in twelve months or less. You will make well-informed engineering judgments about which requirements are load-bearing and which aren't, iterate on real hardware, and demonstrate the discipline to design for manufacturability, test, and EMI/EMC compliance from day one. You will operate with a high degree of autonomy and be a technical anchor for less experienced engineers on the team.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Own the electrical architecture for imaging payloads, partitioning the system, defining power, sensor, data, and interface electronics, and driving the architectural tradeoffs (COTS vs. rad-hard, performance vs. schedule vs. cost) that enable a rapid path to orbit.
  • Lead the design, layout, bring-up, and qualification of PCBAs spanning analog, mixed-signal, FPGAs, and power electronics for EO/IR sensor systems.
  • Translate sensor and system performance models into electrical requirements, and push back on requirements that don't earn their place on the critical path.
  • Drive rapid design-build-test cycles: prototype quickly, characterize on the bench, iterate on real hardware, and converge on flight-ready designs without unnecessary cycles.
  • Design for the space environment (radiation, thermal extremes, vacuum, vibration, and launch loads) and own the analysis and testing (TVAC, vibe, EMI/EMC) that proves it.
  • Bake in design for manufacturability and assembly (DFM/DFA) from the first schematic so designs scale cleanly toward low-rate production as programs mature.
  • Lead board bring-up, integration, and troubleshooting in the lab and during environmental and integration testing, using standard bench equipment (oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, power supplies, DMMs, etc.).
  • Partner closely with firmware, optics, mechanical, systems, and program teams to drive integration and close out anomalies fast.
  • Mentor and provide technical guidance to other electrical engineers, and serve as a design-review and decision-making anchor for the electronics scope.
  • Document architectures, designs, analyses, and test results to a standard that supports flight readiness and program reviews.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 8+ years of experience in electrical engineering spanning system-level architecture, electronics design, and hands-on test, with a track record of owning designs end to end.
  • A degree in Electrical Engineering or equivalent.
  • Demonstrated ownership of electronics architecture for a complex electromechanical or sensor system, including the tradeoff decisions that shaped it.
  • Strong analog, digital, mixed-signal, and power electronics design experience, with deep schematic capture and PCB layout proficiency.
  • Proven ability to take hardware from architecture through bring-up, integration, and qualification — including hands-on debug in the lab.
  • Experience delivering hardware on aggressive timelines and working in rapid, iterative design cycles.
  • Excellent engineering judgment, problem-solving, and the ability to make sound decisions with incomplete information under schedule pressure.
  • Ability to collaborate effectively across a multidisciplinary engineering team.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 8+ years of experience in electrical engineering spanning system-level architecture, electronics design, and hands-on test, with a track record of owning designs end to end.
  • Direct experience designing electronics for space, especially New Space / commercial-cadence programs that flew hardware in a year or less.
  • Familiarity with the space environment and qualification: radiation effects (TID/SEE), rad-hard and rad-tolerant part selection, COTS-for-space approaches, TVAC, vibration, and EMI/EMC.
  • Experience with EO/IR, RF, optical, or other sensor and communication systems.
  • Experience designing for manufacturability and assembly, and transitioning proven designs toward low-rate production to make them more robust and lower cost.
  • Familiarity with analytical tools and programming languages such as MATLAB, Python, or C++.
  • Understanding of system integration processes and workflows in aerospace or defense environments.
  • Experience mentoring engineers and leading design reviews.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril’s Space Manufacturing team is seeking a System Integration and Test Engineer to join our team. The Space Manufacturing team is responsible for assembly, integration, and test of ground support equipment, PCBA, unit-level, and integrated systems that are vital for our aerospace and defense operations. Your expertise will help ensure that our products meet the highest standards of quality and reliability at Anduril. The right person for this role can demonstrate past holistic ownership in solving a technical challenge with a creative, physical solution that they either personally manufactured or oversaw the manufacturing of, in a fast-paced, resource-limited environment. If you are someone who thrives in such an environment, then this role is for you.


WHAT YOU’LL DO 

  • Lead and participate in system integration and test campaigns, developing test plans, test procedures, and schedules, coordinating resource needs, test equipment, and test facility needs.
  • Lead test readiness reviews (TRRs) for flight hardware.
  • Participate in manufacturing readiness reviews (MRRs) for flight hardware.
  • Develop, document, and continuously improve processes for the manufacturing, assembly, and integration of PCBAs and box-level assemblies, and space vehicles, ensuring compliance with space-grade standards.
  • Perform hands-on hardware and software testing at unit-level and system level.
  • Perform detailed root cause analyses (RCA) and drive corrective actions for non-conformances/anomalies identified during integration and test.
  • Specify, procure, and maintain assembly tools, fixtures, and equipment required for integration and test.
  • Communicate with supply chain, hardware teams, program management, and test teams to manage priorities and resolve technical challenges.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS 

  • 5+ years of experience in aerospace, aviation, military, or other high-reliability industries, including 2+ years in hands-on integration and test of flight or comparably high-reliability hardware.
  • Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or another technical discipline.
  • A working, cross-disciplinary understanding of both mechanical and electrical engineering — comfortable interpreting mechanical drawings and GD&T as well as electrical schematics, troubleshooting across both mechanical hardware and electrical/electronic systems, and interfacing with design engineers to address DFM/DFA challenges.
  • 3+ years of hands-on experience in unit-level, space-vehicle, or system integration, assembly, and environmental testing, with direct involvement in at least 2 of: vibration, thermal vacuum, acoustic, shock, or EMI/EMC.
  • Hands-on integration or test experience with electro-optical/infrared (EO/IR) or comparable sensor and payload systems — at least 1 such area, and preferably more than one (e.g., EO/IR, RF/communications, or optical instruments).
  • 3+ years of practical, hands-on experience using test equipment such as oscilloscopes, network analyzers, power supplies, electronic loads, and DAQs.
  • 2+ years working with Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP), and/or Material Resource Planning (MRP), including hands-on use of at least 1 as a system of record in production.
  • 2+ years applying manufacturing process controls, quality assurance, and continuous-improvement methodologies.
  • Willing to work on-site full-time in Costa Mesa, CA  in cleanrooms and around sensitive flight hardware, with travel up to 15% to test and supplier sites.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Strong communication and collaboration skills, with a track record of working across 3+ cross-functional teams (e.g., supply chain, hardware/design, program management, and test), and proven attention to detail in a fast-paced, dynamic environment.
  • Support of at least 1 full spacecraft integration-and-test campaign, including subsystem-level tests (e.g., power, RF communication, software simulations, optical instruments) and full system-level tests.
  • 2+ years working on satellite systems, spacecraft, launch vehicles, or related technologies.
  • Proficiency with CAD or 3D-modeling software for tooling design.
  • Experience working in an ISO 7 or cleaner cleanroom, or other contamination-controlled environment.
  • Experience assembling electro-optical instruments.
  • Familiarity with tools such as JIRA, NX design, and Python.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Top Secret security clearance.

The team is responsible for taking products like Ghost, Anvil, Bolt and Altius from concepts to operational systems. We work in close coordination with specialist teams to solve some of the hardest problems facing our customers. We are looking for software engineers, hardware engineers, roboticists, and front-end mobile developers who are excited about creating a powerful robotics platform that can be tasked and viewed in real-time through a variety of interfaces.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Work within a team of multidisciplinary engineers and specialists throughout the life of UAV design and integration efforts
  • Conceptualize system architecture for upgrades and enhancements to existing vehicle systems
  • Conceptual designs of small drones including sizing, system performance and initial prototyping
  • Layout system design plans and interfaces for new UAV products and platforms
  • Manage tactical engineering efforts, interfacing between different engineering and test disciplines
  • Draft and develop test plans for critical subsystems, and support vehicle level acceptance testing
  • Develop interface controls for partners and customers to use for hardware, software, and electrical integration of complex and unique payloads with the Anduril UAVs
  • Achieve maximum uptime by leading vehicle data analysis efforts to identify performance trends and develop predictive failure models
  • Support build and benchtop testing of new vehicle systems
  • Conduct hands-on UAV testing with occasional travel

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • A passion for systems development, integration, and testing
  • 7-10 years of industry experience including but not limited to systems engineering
  • Familiarity with concepts of systems engineering, mechanical engineering, electrical engineering, software development, and control theory
  • Hands-on build and prototyping of complex robotic or aircraft systems
  • Knowledge of electronics troubleshooting and ability to use basic test equipment
  • Extremely organized and detail-oriented
  • Excellent verbal & written communication skills
  • A sincere commitment to a positive, inclusive, and collaborative culture
  • Ability to travel as required for test planning and execution
  • Must be able to obtain and hold a U.S. Top Secret security clearance

  • Experience developing electromechanical system models to inform design, operation, and troubleshooting of complex subsystems
  • Hands on manufacturing or flight testing experience
  • Experience in design engineering
  • Experience in software engineering
  • Understanding of aerodynamics, avionics and flight systems

Anduril's Space team is dedicated to expanding our AI-powered capabilities into the final frontier, enhancing Space Domain Awareness, Space Control, and Command and Control for U.S. military and allied partners. We're developing fully integrated hardware and software systems, including Lattice for Space Missions and modular payloads, to address growing threats in space and ensure our Guardians maintain a decisive advantage in this contested war-fighting domain.

ABOUT THE JOB

As an Electro Optical System Engineer for our Space team, you will facilitate the integration of EO Payloads on our spacecraft platforms from initial concept development through on-orbit execution. A successful candidate will have experience during all phases of payload system engineering including architecture and requirement derivation, performance modeling, design reviews, laboratory testing, spacecraft assembly integration and test, on-orbit initialization, and mission operations. A proven history of interfacing with all disciplines of the engineering, specialty, and program management team to shepherd a payload design to maturity is required. 

You’ll be expected to clearly communicate risk, issues, and progress with customer representatives and external vendors in a collaborative environment. We are especially seeking candidates with hands-on experience in optical laboratories characterizing and calibrating optical payloads. You will be expected to know how to configure and operate test equipment such as collimators, integrating spheres, interferometers, and other tools. You will work closely with other AI&T professionals and be expected to train others how to also use this equipment. Payloads you will be interacting with include photon detecting imagers from visible through long wave infrared wavebands including CMOS and CCD focal planes, thermal sensors including microbolometers, as well as LiDAR and laser range finders. Experience with state-of-the-art sensing technology such as event based cameras, quantum detectors, and metamaterials is also highly desired.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Perform concept designs of active and passive EO payloads
  • Derive system and unit level requirements
  • Analyze performance with an in-depth understanding of payload technology and related physics
  • Identify payload key performance parameters and create test plans and procedures to measure these parameters in a laboratory environment
  • Perform hands-on characterization and calibration of the radiometric and geometric performance of flight hardware using collimators, integrating spheres, theodolites, laser trackers, interferometers, and other optical test equipment
  • Train and educate other AI&T professionals to conduct successful payload testing
  • Work with the external and internal engineering team to author Interface Control Documents (ICD) covering all aspects of payload integration including electrical, data, algorithmic, mechanical, thermal, and optical interfaces
  • Facilitate communication between mechanical, thermal, electrical, and software teams to resolve complex integration trades and manage technical risk
  • Define and develop payload data calibration algorithms and data products and work with computer vision and flight software engineers to integrate these algorithms into the processing pipeline
  • Define on-orbit calibration sequences, initialization procedures, and provide real-time engineering support during nominal operations
  • Clearly communicate with customers at design reviews and during the entire payload development lifecycle
  • Assist assembly and integration campaigns for space systems flight hardware
  • Integrate across numerous teams to collaboratively identify testing requirements to include verification and validation plans
  • Develop test plans and procedures for prototype, qualification, and acceptance of space systems flight hardware

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Strong engineering background from industry and school, ideally in areas/fields such as Systems Engineering, Physics, Mechanical Engineering, or Electrical Engineering
  • Experience conducting assembly, integration and test of space payload flight hardware with a focus on performance characterization and requirement verification
  • Deep understanding of professional optical test equipment, tools and methodologies with a tie back to the underlying physics
  • Experience with advanced payload analyses and laboratory measurements including photon transfer, dark current, radiometry, responsivity, distortion mapping, boresight alignments, non-uniformity corrections, point spread function, modulation transfer function, and more
  • Ability to quickly understand and navigate complex systems and detailed requirements
  • Capable of solving complex technical problems with little oversight
  • Clear communication and organizational skills including documentation and training material
  • Experience writing technical documentation, procedures, and reports
  • Experience working in cleanroom and ESD-safe environments
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience with ImageJ, Python, MATLAB
  • Experience with optical test equipment from Labsphere, 4D Technologies, Leica, SORL, and other industry leaders
  • Experience with stray light, depth of focus, and supplementary payload analyses
  • Experience with optical modeling in tools such as Zemax or Code V
  • Experience with RF payload design and testing

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Prepare technical reports to present findings to internal teams, management, and external customers
  • Stay current with advancements in thermal analysis techniques, materials technology, and industry standards

  • Familiarity with Matlab or Python (or equivalent) for developing analytical models and performing data acquisition & post-processing
  • Experience with performing test-model correlation and test based characterization of critical modelling input parameters
  • Good at working independently and with various teams and key stakeholders
  • Highly motivated, self-starting, results oriented, and capable of working in a dynamic environment
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance 

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

About the Team

Our Robotics team is focused on unlocking general-purpose robotics and advancing toward AGI-level intelligence in dynamic, real-world environments. Working across the full model and systems stack, we integrate cutting-edge hardware and software to explore a broad range of robotic form factors. We strive to seamlessly blend high-level AI capabilities with the physical constraints of real-world systems to improve people’s lives.


About the Role

We’re looking for an Electrical Engineer to develop the AI inference compute systems that power OpenAI’s humanoid robots. This role combines compute architecture, high-speed digital design, onboard power electronics, and compact HDI PCB development.

We’re looking for a self-driven engineer who takes ownership from concept through deployment. Above all, you should enjoy hands-on engineering: bringing up boards, characterizing interfaces, and tracking challenging failures to their root cause.


In this role, you will:

  • Own compute hardware architecture and development, from component selection and schematic design through PCB layout, validation, and deployment.

  • Design and integrate high-speed interfaces—including PCIe, DDR, Ethernet, MIPI, USB, and DisplayPort—balancing bandwidth, connectivity, power, and signal integrity.

  • Develop onboard DC-to-DC conversion and power distribution to meet efficiency, transient-response, sequencing, and power-integrity requirements.

  • Define HDI PCB stackups, dielectric materials, via structures, and routing strategies that balance electrical performance, manufacturability, reliability, and cost.

  • Lead bench bring-up and validation, including test planning, high-speed interface characterization, power measurements, and debugging through verified resolution.

  • Partner with thermal, mechanical, EMC, and software teams to integrate compute hardware into tightly constrained robotic systems.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have 5+ years of experience developing compute hardware or similarly complex high-speed electronics, with demonstrated ownership of complete designs.

  • Bring strong hands-on measurement and debugging skills, including practical experience with oscilloscopes, probing techniques, and interface validation.

  • Understand high-speed digital interfaces deeply enough to make architectural tradeoffs and diagnose issues across hardware and software boundaries.

  • Have strong signal-integrity and power-integrity fundamentals, a solid foundation in power electronics, and practical experience designing complex HDI PCBs.

  • Can use a Linux shell, write simple shell scripts, connect over SSH, and perform basic Ethernet and network troubleshooting.

  • Take initiative, turn ambiguous requirements into concrete engineering plans, and follow through to deliver working systems.

Additional, preferred qualifications:

  • Experience designing around AI inference SoCs or accelerators, including their power, memory, and communication architectures.

  • Familiarity with how AI inference workloads map to silicon capabilities, including compute throughput (TOPS), DRAM bandwidth and capacity, and how workload requirements and DRAM technology choices affect achievable performance and performance per watt.

  • Experience bringing compute hardware into production and resolving fabrication, assembly, or test issues with manufacturing partners.

About the Team

The Product Policy research team studies how people use and experience AI, generating evidence to inform product, policy, and safety decisions. We partner with researchers, data scientists, engineers, and cross-functional teams to understand AI’s effects on people’s lives, including well-being, youth experiences, and social and emotional use.

About the Role

We’re looking for an Applied Scientist to help design, execute, and analyze large-scale longitudinal research on AI use and well-being. You’ll work closely with research leads to translate scientific questions into rigorous studies, combining survey responses with behavioral data to understand how people’s experiences with AI evolve over time.

This is a hands-on role spanning applied analysis, research methods, and study execution. You’ll build reproducible analytical workflows, assess data quality and representativeness, and help establish reliable infrastructure for ongoing panel research. Your work will support research involving teens and adults, including studies of AI companionship, and help turn findings into useful evidence for product, policy, and safety partners.

In this role, you will:

  • Partner with research leads to develop study designs, survey measures, and analysis plans for longitudinal research on AI use and well-being.

  • Conduct statistical analyses of survey and behavioral data, including evaluating selection and response bias, account-linkage patterns, and sample representativeness.

  • Prepare and validate analysis-ready datasets, implement analysis plans, and produce clear summaries and visualizations using reproducible workflows.

  • Develop quality checks across survey programming, fieldwork, data delivery, and repeated study waves to identify inconsistencies and improve research reliability.

  • Own day-to-day study execution, coordinating timelines, vendors, and cross-functional dependencies to deliver high-quality research on schedule.

  • Collaborate with data engineering and privacy partners on responsible account linkage, data flows, logging, and retention.

  • Support human-subjects research review, including Institutional Review Board (IRB) documentation, protocol amendments, and consent and assent processes.

  • Maintain clear documentation of methods, measures, assumptions, and protocol changes, and contribute analysis and methodological materials for research readouts, publications, and peer review.

  • Communicate findings, limitations, and practical recommendations to technical and nontechnical partners, and build reusable tools and processes that improve future studies.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have experience conducting applied quantitative research in social science, behavioral science, human-computer interaction, statistics, or a related field.

  • Bring strong foundations in survey research and statistical analysis, with experience working on panel studies, longitudinal datasets, or human-subjects research.

  • Are comfortable using SQL and Python or R to prepare data, implement analyses, validate results, and create visualizations.

  • Understand how recruitment, missing data, participant attrition, and measurement choices can affect the interpretation and generalizability of findings.

  • Can move between analytical work and practical execution, managing multiple timelines and collaborators while maintaining scientific rigor.

  • Communicate clearly, lead with the key takeaway, and connect methodological choices and findings to the decisions they inform.

  • Exercise sound judgment when working with sensitive data and research involving minors.

  • Enjoy building structure in ambiguous environments and collaborating across disciplines.

Nice to Have

  • Experience combining survey responses with behavioral or product data.

  • Familiarity with preregistration, measure validation, reproducible research, and academic publication or peer-review processes.

  • Experience working with research vendors, survey platforms, or IRB and ethics-review partners.

  • Research experience related to AI-human interaction, digital well-being, youth development, or social and emotional uses of technology.

About the Team

The Foundations Research team works on high-risk, high-reward ideas that could shape the next decade of AI. Our goal is to advance the science and data that enable our training and scaling efforts, with a particular focus on future frontier models. We push the boundaries of data, scaling laws, optimization techniques, model architectures, model + search co-design and efficiency improvements to propel our science.

The Search team sits within Foundations, building agentic search by co-designing model-system interfaces with the core search stack: serving, indexing, and retrieval. We research and develop large-scale systems that transform and index vast corpora, enabling models to most effectively find and reason over information.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Researcher to work on semi-structured knowledge graphs within Search. You’ll research and develop methods for mining structured information from heterogeneous, unstructured and semi-structured web content, making that information more accessible and useful to AI models.

The core questions are: What structure helps models find and use information? How can we extract it reliably at web scale? And how do we measure whether it improves the model’s ability to reason and answer questions? How do we design the system to be optimizable end-to-end?

You’ll work across research, data, and systems, exploring how advances in AI and compute can improve the way knowledge is extracted, organized, and retrieved. This work will support retrieval across OpenAI products and internal research efforts, with opportunities for scientific publication.

Responsibilities

  • Develop methods to extract and connect structured information across diverse web sources, including entities, attributes, and relationships.

  • Build scalable approaches for transforming noisy, inconsistent content into useful knowledge representations.

  • Explore how models and compute can improve extraction quality and reduce the manual work involved in building knowledge systems.

  • Design evaluations that measure both the quality of extracted knowledge and its usefulness for retrieval and model reasoning.

  • Partner with researchers and engineers to integrate structured knowledge into Search and use model performance to guide improvements.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You Have

  • Deep experience in knowledge extraction, knowledge graphs, entity resolution, or related work that derives structure from large, heterogeneous datasets.

  • Strong machine learning and research skills, with experience developing and evaluating methods for real-world data.

  • A track record of building or scaling data and ML systems, particularly for web-scale extraction, indexing, or retrieval.

  • Experience independently driving open-ended technical problems from an initial idea through experimentation and implementation.

  • A first-principles approach to using AI and compute, with a willingness to rethink established methods as model capabilities improve.

  • A strong interest in how the representation of information shapes what models can find, understand, and use.

The Search team sits within Foundations, building agentic search by co-designing model-system interfaces with the core search stack: serving, indexing, and retrieval. We research and develop large-scale systems that transform and index vast corpora, enabling models to most effectively find and reason over information. In close partnership with researchers, we bring modeling advances into production and improve how AI systems discover, retrieve, and use knowledge.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Researcher to lead Search Integrity: the systems that distinguish useful web content from spam, manipulation, and other adversarial or low-quality material.

The challenge extends beyond evaluating individual pages. A page may appear credible in isolation, while its links, metadata, or relationships with other sites reveal coordinated manipulation. As AI makes convincing content easier to produce at scale, detection systems must adapt to increasingly sophisticated adversaries.

You’ll define the technical approach, build classifiers and evaluations, and shape how integrity signals influence what Search indexes and retrieves. Working closely with Search and broader Safety and Integrity teams, you’ll use frontier models to advance detection methods and bring them into production.

Responsibilities

  • Define the technical direction for Search Integrity, identifying gaps and determining which problems and interventions to prioritize.

  • Develop AI and ML systems to detect spam, scams, phishing, malicious domains, prompt injections, and other adversarial or low-quality web content.

  • Discover useful signals across page content, links, domains, metadata, and relationships between websites, including patterns that reveal coordinated manipulation.

  • Build evaluations that measure detection quality and how integrity interventions affect the information Search surfaces.

  • Translate detection signals into indexing, ranking, and filtering decisions, improving what models can retrieve and rely on.

  • Serve as the technical owner for integrity within Search, partnering with researchers, engineers, and broader Safety and Integrity teams to build and deploy these systems.

You Might Thrive in This Role If You Have

  • Deep experience in web spam, search quality, adversarial content detection, or related integrity problems at scale.

  • Strong applied ML and research skills, with experience developing classifiers, detection methods, and evaluations for real-world systems.

  • An understanding of how adversaries manipulate content and links, coordinate across sites, and adapt to detection systems.

  • A track record of independently defining ambiguous technical problems and driving solutions from experimentation through production.

  • Experience working across research, engineering, and integrity teams while remaining hands-on with technical work.

  • A first-principles approach to using frontier models and compute, and a strong interest in keeping detection systems effective as adversaries evolve.

AI and ML power innovation in all areas of the business, including helping members choose the right title for them through personalization, better understanding our audience and our content slate, creating high-quality subtitles, dubbings, images, trailers, and other assets, optimizing our payment processing, and much more. AI Platform (AIP) organization builds highly scalable, differentiated AI infrastructure to maximize the business impact of all AI/ML practitioners at Netflix, which is key to accelerating this innovation.

The Opportunity

The AI Observability team makes AI, ML, and Agentic systems transparent, reliable, and production-ready at scale. We build end-to-end observability for ML and GenAI workloads, capturing model inputs, features, predictions, outcomes, and behavior across online and batch systems. Our platform enables teams to monitor model performance, data quality, drift, latency, and failures, turning the ML system from a black box into an explainable, debuggable system. We provide developer-friendly libraries, dashboards, and alerts so teams can debug issues, respond to incidents, and ship AI-powered products with confidence.

We're looking for a hands-on senior engineer to build the frameworks behind Netflix's AI Observability platform, model performance, evaluation, and vendor integration surfaces. You will design reusable infrastructure that enables ML/AI practitioners across domains to monitor model quality in production, evaluate LLM and agentic systems, and adopt vendor tooling through a consistent, self-serve platform. AIP owns the generic, reusable infrastructure; domain teams own their domain-specific evals and remediation. You will partner closely with engineering, product, machine learning, and data teams to turn their needs into reusable platform capabilities. To succeed, you will bring a strong background in AI or ML infrastructure and a passion for building scalable, robust systems.  

In this role, you will:

  • Build the observability framework and platform capabilities that give ML and GenAI systems metrics, logs, and distributed traces across online inference, batch scoring, feature pipelines, and agent orchestration, so teams can instrument their systems consistently.

  • Build the primitives that let teams monitor model performance (accuracy, calibration, error rates), data quality, drift, and degradation on their own systems, rather than monitoring individual models yourself.

  • Build and extend evaluation frameworks for LLM and agentic systems that support response quality, grounding and hallucination, task success, tool-use and trajectory correctness, and LLM-as-a-judge and human-in-the-loop scoring, giving teams reusable building blocks to define and run their own evals.

  • Lead build-vs-buy evaluations for observability and eval tooling, and own the SDKs, connectors, and APIs that integrate vendor platforms into a consistent, well-supported interface, so ML and product teams can onboard models and agents with minimal friction.

  • Build reusable libraries, SDKs, and templates that make observability and evaluation the default for new systems ("observability-by-default"), lowering the barrier for teams to instrument and evaluate their work.

Overview

Can you turn cloud strategy into clear, practical plans for a market? Do you enjoy working with sales, marketing, partner and engineering teams to deliver results for customers? Are you motivated by plans that drive revenue, growth and long-term market impact? 

Microsoft's Cloud & AI Field Sales & Operations organization is hiring a Senior Manager, Cloud Capacity Go-to-Market based in Tokyo. Microsoft is rapidly expanding its cloud and AI datacenter regions worldwide. In this role, you will make sure the services and capacity we bring to Japan match what our customers need, both now and in the years ahead. 

This is a new function at Microsoft, and few similar roles exist elsewhere in the industry. You'll join a growing team across Asia, with counterpart teams in the Americas and EMEA. You'll work with Microsoft's sales leadership in Japan and Asia, with Azure engineering and capacity planning teams, and with our datacenter expansion teams. Together you'll shape how Microsoft's cloud grows in Japan. 

We don't expect anyone to arrive with every skill listed here. If you have a strong go-to-market background and solid cloud experience, we want to hear from you, and we'll support you as you build the rest on the job. 

Microsoft's mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond. In alignment with our Microsoft values, we are committed to cultivating an inclusive work environment for all employees to positively impact our culture every day. 



Responsibilities

  • Build a multi-year growth plan for Microsoft's cloud presence in Japan, with a clear strategy and measurable goals. 

  • Coordinate datacenter expansion activities with local and regional sales leadership, solution architects, marketing and global teams. This covers site planning, launch readiness, pipeline and reporting. 

  • Build demand ahead of launch. Work with sales, sales operations, partner and finance teams to develop and track customer pipeline for new cloud capacity, especially from large anchor customers. 

  • Represent customer demand to engineering. Identify the cloud services and features customers in Japan need, and work with engineering and capacity planning teams so they are available in time. 

  • Develop business cases for datacenter expansion and help secure investment and support from global teams. 

  • Respond to urgent capacity needs. Work with stakeholders to find options that support business continuity for customers' mission-critical workloads. 

  • Build relationships across internal teams and with external partners, and help grow the local technical ecosystem. 

  • Partner with corporate communications on announcements of new or expanded datacenter regions. 

  • Track execution of the plan and support Asia leadership with strategic decisions and course corrections. 



Qualifications

Required qualifications 

  • 5+ years of experience in go-to-market strategy, sales enablement, business development, business planning, technical pre-sales or a related area. 

  • Experience with at least one major public cloud platform, such as Microsoft Azure, AWS or Google Cloud. You should understand cloud services and how customers adopt them. 

  • Fluency in Japanese and business-level English. 

Preferred qualifications 

  • Experience with Microsoft Azure specifically. 

  • Experience driving demand generation and pipeline growth in a complex multinational or matrixed organization. 

  • Knowledge of datacenter infrastructure, such as capacity planning, power, network or hyperscale datacenter operations. 

  • Strong executive communication and storytelling skills, including turning complex ideas into simple messages. 

  • Strong business analysis skills, including financials, sales processes, scorecards and KPIs. 

  • A track record of working across teams and influencing senior stakeholders. 


This position will be open for a minimum of 5 days, with applications accepted on an ongoing basis until the position is filled.

Overview

The Cloud Hardware and System Engineering (CHSE) team is looking for a Senior Hardware Engineer to serve as the Compute System Technical Lead (STL) in Taipei, Taiwan, providing end-to-end technical leadership for the development and validation of next-generation Azure compute hardware platforms. The STL bridges architecture and execution, maintains technical continuity across program development and validation lifecycle phases, and ensures that hardware, firmware, software, validation, manufacturing, and operational workstreams converge into a complete, high-quality system solution. The STL owns end-to-end technical execution, cross-functional integration, design quality, technical readiness, and program-level technical decisions within the approved baseline. The STL also provides technical input and impact assessment for program decisions while preserving the ownership of functional engineering and program-management teams. 

As Azure grows to support increasingly demanding cloud, AI, and data-intensive workloads, compute infrastructure deliver greater performance, efficiency, reliability, serviceability, security, and cost effectiveness at global scale. The CHSE team defines and delivers the systems engineering required to bring new cloud hardware platforms from concept through qualification, deployment, and fleet operations. This role will provide system-level technical leadership for Azure compute hardware, including conventional cloud servers and, where relevant, large-memory, multi-processor platforms with up to eight sockets and CXL-attached memory, as well as AI and high-performance computing (HPC) workloads. Experience with complex server platforms is central; prior ownership of a specific large-memory, multi-processor or HPC platform is not required. 

CHSE sits within the broader Microsoft Silicon, Cloud Hardware, and Infrastructure Engineering (SCHIE) organization that designs and delivers the silicon, hardware systems, firmware, software, and other foundational technologies that power Microsoft Azure. Our teams work across silicon, servers, storage, networking, accelerators, datacenters, security, and operations to build infrastructure that is reliable, efficient, secure, and scalable for Microsoft's global cloud services. We are looking for engineers who want to shape the next generation of cloud infrastructure and deliver trusted experiences for customers worldwide.

The Fitness team is shaping the future of personal health and activity across watchOS and iOS. Behind the features our users count on every day is the Fitness Quality team, a force multiplier for every engineer testing them. We build the automation frameworks and test infrastructure that let us test ambitious new fitness experiences quickly and with confidence. As a Tools and Automation Engineer on our team, you will be at the heart of this process.

Description

In this role, you'll design and build automation frameworks, tools, and services that power Fitness quality engineering on watchOS and iOS. You'll work across the entire lifecycle, from on-device test automation to scalable backend systems and reporting. Your work will directly speed up innovation and help ensure the quality of fitness features used by millions of people worldwide.

Responsibilities

Design, develop, and deploy automated tests and frameworks that check Fitness and Activity features end to end across watchOS and iOS, including scenarios that need a paired Apple Watch and iPhone.
Build tools that simulate real-world activity so fitness features can be tested repeatably and at scale.
Add automated test suites to CI/CD pipelines that run on every build, so regressions are caught early and engineering teams get fast, reliable feedback.
Keep the automation healthy: find and fix flaky tests, update coverage as features change, and retire tests that no longer add value.
Triage automated test failures daily. Separate product regressions from test or infrastructure problems, and file clear, reproducible bug reports with the diagnostics engineers need to act.
Investigate complex failures across devices, OS builds, and lab infrastructure, and find the root cause so problems don't come back.

Description

Operations Reliability Engineers are responsible for guiding development and operations teams toward generating reliable designs for Apple's new technology components, modules, and overall products. Analyze test correlation between different assembly nodes, align test pass/fail criteria and metrology systems, cosmetics requirements, etc.
Summarize Reliability results and share findings with cross-functional partners and senior management Manage alignment and transition of reliability testing from NPI to MP.
Develop capable suppliers that can be both technology and volume scaling partners.
Willingness and ability to travel internally up to 20% to China or within US.
