  • Vet Suppliers' production capabilities, factory lay out, facilities, workforce for supplier inclusion in Approved Supplier List
  • Support Supply Chain Product Sourcing Engineers (PSE), Supply Chain Global Strategic Sourcing Management (GSS) and Supplier Quality Engineers (SQE) in ensuring Suppliers' understanding and adherence to the criteria for part quality set by SQE
  • Own bringing up new production tooling & lines, development at Supplier as needed, at Supplier sites to ensure materials, processes & tools are capable of meeting product performance, quality (criteria set by SQE) and demand requirements
  • Own capacity expansion readiness and production ramp-up at Supplier
  • Establish and drive process performance and controls (SPC) reviews at Supplier
  • Identify and drive product and process improvements, factory layout optimization at Supplier sites to lower part cost, reduce supply risk, eliminate potential defects, and improve cycle time ​over the product lifecycle
  • Support SQE with root cause task force at Anduril by working in tandem with the Supply Chain team, Suppliers​, and be responsible for closing the loop of root cause corrective/preventative actions at Supplier

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree in supply chain, engineering, or related technical field
  • 6+ years of experience in supplier quality and industrialization within a manufacturing environment
  • Experience with specific category technical expertise, as applicable, electronics manufacturing, SMT processing, GD&T
  • Ability to travel at least 30% of the time
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

  • Bachelor’s degree in electrical engineering, or related technical field
  • Previous experience in defense, aerospace, automotive, high tech, or another related industry
  • Strong understanding of quality systems, standards, and certifications
  • Familiarity with developing high-tech products in a high-mix, low-volume environment
  • Exposure to working in a fast-pace, start-up environment
  • Excellent communication, negotiation, and problem-solving skills

The Anduril Rocket Motor Systems (ARMS) team is on a mission to build next generation solid rocket motors for a safer, more connected world. To achieve our vision of becoming a large-volume provider of tactical rocket motors, we will develop differentiated products and services that maximize our customers' capabilities, and we will establish and maintain a reputation of Quality and Reliability.

ABOUT THE JOB
Anduril's Planning team is seeking a Supply Planner to support high-volume production on a dedicated program. This role is execution-focused: you will be responsible for generating the purchase requisitions and manufacturing work orders that keep material flowing from raw stock through finished goods. You will run Clear-To-Build (CTB) analyses, flag shortages quickly, and escalate material constraints so the production schedule stays on track. While the schedule itself is set by senior planners, you will own the day-to-day supply signals that ensure Purchasing and Manufacturing have what they need, when they need it.

WHAT YOU'LL DO
Clear-To-Build & Shortage Management
  • Execute CTB reviews against Engineering and Manufacturing Bills of Material (BOMs) for scheduled production runs. Identify where the build is not clear — which parts need to be expedited and which are at risk of shortage.
  • Escalate shortages promptly through established channels (e.g., posting to the designated Slack channel, flagging to the program lead) so constraints are visible and action is taken before production is impacted.
  • Track purchase order commitments and inbound material status to assess manufacturing readiness against the published production schedule.
Purchase Requisitions & Work Orders
  • Create and manage a high volume of purchase requisitions to ensure material is on order and aligned with production demand.
  • Generate, schedule, and manage manufacturing work orders across the work order lifecycle. Monitor aging work orders and coordinate with the Production Scheduler when priorities shift due to material availability or capacity changes.
  • Maintain accuracy and completeness in all transactional ERP entries to support downstream traceability and reporting.
Material Coordination & Compliance
  • Coordinate with the Production Scheduler and Warehouse on product prestaging, picking, and kitting requirements to support on-time production starts.
  • Maintain serialized parts and material traceability within the ERP system to meet Quality Management System (QMS), defense, and HazMat standards.
  • Support inventory accuracy by flagging discrepancies and participating in cycle count and reconciliation processes.
ERP System Support
  • Ensure item master data, lead times, and reorder points relevant to your program are accurate and up to date within the ERP/MRP system.
  • Troubleshoot day-to-day MRP-related issues and partner with senior planners on system improvements and workflow refinements.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS
  • Experience & Education: 3+ years of experience in Supply Planning, Material Planning, or Production Planning. Academic coursework or a degree in Supply Chain Management, Operations, Engineering, or a related field.
  • ERP/MRP Proficiency: Hands-on experience creating purchase requisitions, work orders, and running CTB or similar material readiness analyses in an ERP/MRP system.
  • High-Volume Execution: Demonstrated ability to manage a large volume of transactional planning activities accurately and on time in a fast-paced production environment.
  • Shortage Escalation: Experience identifying material constraints and driving timely escalation and resolution with cross-functional partners.
  • Regulatory Standards: Familiarity with government-furnished material management and Federal Acquisition Regulation (FAR) guidelines is a plus.
  • Quality Systems: Exposure to AS9100 or similar quality management systems and an understanding of Lean Manufacturing principles.

$77,000—$100,000 USD

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a Systems Engineer to support the US Army's Next Generation Command and Control (NGC2) program.

You will lead the technical engagements that bring new partners onto the platform: conducting technical exchanges with their engineering teams, establishing the integration design, decomposing the resulting requirements into engineering work, and authoring the reference material other teams build from. Most of this work is conducted across an organizational boundary, without shared reporting lines or a shared backlog.
 
WHAT YOU'LL DO
  • Lead partner engagements end to end; Conduct the technical exchange, own the integration design, and drive open items to written resolution across both organizations.

  • Establish reusable patterns; Convert what recurs across engagements into reference architectures, decision guidance, and integration documentation, and define the standard other teams document to.

About the Team

The Identity Infrastructure Engineering team builds the identity and access systems that OpenAI’s researchers, engineers, and internal teams rely on to protect critical systems and data.

We partner with Research, Applied Engineering, Infrastructure, IT, and Security to make secure access practical across cloud and internal environments.

About the Role

We’re looking for a hands-on software engineer to design and build high-scale, high-throughput secure access proxies and the distributed systems behind them. These are tier-zero services: researchers, engineers, and agents depend on them to reach critical infrastructure safely and reliably.

You’ll work at the intersection of networking, distributed systems, and infrastructure security, building the serving paths and control-plane integrations that connect identities to resources. Teleport is a core part of the current platform; the role also includes credential brokers, policy enforcement, and developer-facing integrations.

You’ll own the services you build from design and implementation through production. That means understanding human, agent, and workload traffic, improving throughput and tail latency, making authorization decisions auditable, and designing for safe multi-region rollout and recovery. We’re looking for someone who can turn a demanding security requirement into software that works well at scale and is straightforward for other engineers to use.

In this role, you will:

  • Design and implement secure access proxies, gateways, and credential brokers that provide narrowly scoped, auditable access to infrastructure and internal services while reducing standing privileges..

  • Integrate identity and access policy across clients, proxies, and target systems so approved permissions take effect promptly and access expires or is revoked when required. Ensure correct behavior when policy is stale or sessions remain active.

  • Build observability that explains the end-to-end access path: latency, errors, saturation, authorization decisions, and identity attribution, without leaking credentials.

  • Engineer safe multi-region rollouts, canaries, rollback, failover, and recovery. Validate changes with realistic test environments, load tests, and failure testing.

  • Keep core access services reliable, performant, and maintainable. Own production support, maintenance, upgrades, and incident recovery; ship durable fixes that reduce recurring failures, alert noise, and manual work.

  • Make secure access easy to adopt through reusable APIs, client tooling, diagnostics, and self-service workflows. Lead migrations that preserve critical workflows, with tested rollback and recovery paths and clear ownership across Infrastructure, Security, and SRE.

You might thrive in this role if you: 

  • Have built and operated production backend, proxy, networking, or infrastructure services with demanding scale or availability requirements.

  • Have practical networking depth and can reason about HTTP, TCP, TLS, DNS, routing, and load balancing across real request paths.

  • Can explain how you handled performance bottlenecks, partial failures, multi-region deployment, or a difficult production change in a system you personally built.

  • Understand authentication, authorization, least privilege, trust boundaries, credential handling, and the consequences of an access-control failure.

  • Have strong software engineering fundamentals and experience with Go, Rust, Python, or similar languages.

  • Use tests, profiling, telemetry, and reproducible experiments to debug across system boundaries and verify correctness, performance, and recovery.

  • Make practical scope decisions, communicate tradeoffs clearly, and follow through from code to production. Teleport or comparable access-platform experience is helpful; strong engineering and production ownership matter more than knowing every tool.

About the Team

OpenAI didn’t begin as a traditional company. It began as an idea: that artificial intelligence could be developed in a way that benefits everyone. As a creative team, our role is to help make sure the work behind that idea is understood as it leaves the lab and meets the world.

This company works at the frontier of intelligence. Like any frontier, it’s unfinished, constantly shifting, and still being explored. Our job is to stay close to that uncertainty and help shape how this story gets told in a way that feels grounded and human. We do this through campaigns, launches, films, brand systems, and work that doesn’t fit neatly into any of those categories yet. This team is for people who want to help shape something from the beginning.

About the Role

We’re looking for an experienced Creative Director, Copy to join our growing in-house creative team focused on OpenAI’s business audiences. In this role, you’ll help define how we communicate the value of OpenAI to organizations - from growing businesses and startups to global enterprises and developers building with our technology.

You’ll concept and write across integrated campaigns, product launches, customer stories, events, and other brand moments. You’ll translate complex products, technical capabilities, and business outcomes into clear, compelling ideas that resonate with decision-makers, builders, and teams adopting AI.

About the Role

We are looking for an experienced and technically skilled accounting professional to manage the accounting and financial reporting for OpenAI’s compute and infrastructure lease-related activities. In this role, you will own complex lease accounting matters across data centers, servers, equipment, and other infrastructure arrangements, while helping operationalize new programs as the organization continues to scale.

You will evaluate unique and highly structured transactions, assess their accounting implications, and translate technical conclusions into clear recommendations for leadership. You will also work cross-functionally to design the processes, systems, controls, and data solutions required to support accurate and scalable accounting operations.

This role requires a strong command of US GAAP, particularly lease accounting and consolidation, as well as the ability to operate effectively and fluidly in an evolving environment where new infrastructure programs may not yet have established processes or system solutions. The ideal candidate is both a technical accounting expert and a hands-on builder who can turn complex arrangements into sustainable operating models.

You will partner closely with Finance, Technical Accounting, Legal, Tax, Procurement, Engineering, Infrastructure, and other key stakeholders. You will also work with external counterparties and service providers to ensure the accounting treatment, operational processes, and reporting outputs are accurate, well-documented, and scalable.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

 

In this role, you will:

  • Own the end-to-end accounting for compute and infrastructure lease-related activities, including data centers, servers, equipment, colocation arrangements, and other infrastructure deployments.

  • Evaluate new and evolving infrastructure arrangements to determine the appropriate accounting treatment under US GAAP, including lease identification, classification, measurement, commencement, modification, impairment, and presentation considerations.

  • Partner with Technical Accounting and other cross-functional stakeholders to assess complex or non-standard transactions, document accounting conclusions, and present the financial reporting implications to senior leadership.

  • Lead the accounting operationalization of new compute and infrastructure programs by developing scalable processes, controls, systems, data requirements, and reporting solutions from the ground up.

  • Design and implement system solutions to support lease accounting, fixed asset tracking, subledger requirements, data integration, and management reporting.

  • Own month-end and quarter-end close activities for the lease portfolio, including journal entries, reconciliations, flux analysis, rollforwards, balance sheet substantiation, and reporting packages.

  • Ensure the completeness and accuracy of lease-related accounting records by developing robust contract intake, asset tracking, and reconciliation processes.

  • Manage the accounting and reporting requirements for unique legal entities and special-purpose structures associated with infrastructure investments, including consolidation assessments, intercompany activity, and entity-level reporting.

  • Monitor changes in contractual arrangements and operational facts to identify lease modifications, reassessments, impairments, consolidation changes, and other accounting impacts.

  • Build and maintain strong internal controls over lease accounting, infrastructure data, entity reporting, journal entries, reconciliations, and management review processes.

  • Support internal and external audit requests, including preparation of accounting documentation, control evidence, reconciliation support, and responses to technical questions.

You might thrive in this role if you have:

  • 10+ years of progressive experience in accounting, audit, advisory, or a related finance function, with meaningful experience managing complex transactions from initial assessment through operational execution.

  • Strong technical knowledge of US GAAP, particularly ASC 842, ASC 810, ASC 360, fixed asset accounting, construction-in-progress accounting, and related financial reporting requirements.

  • Experience assessing complex lease arrangements, embedded leases, equipment financing, data center arrangements, build-to-suit structures, or other infrastructure-related transactions.

  • Experience with consolidation accounting, including variable interest entity assessments, special-purpose entities, intercompany accounting, and noncontrolling interests.

  • Demonstrated ability to translate complex contractual terms and accounting conclusions into scalable operational processes, system requirements, and control frameworks.

  • Experience working with large-scale lease accounting systems, fixed asset systems, and ERP tools such as NetSuite, SAP, Oracle, or similar platforms.

  • Strong systems-thinking capabilities and a track record of partnering with data, engineering, or IT teams to design automated accounting solutions.

  • A builder mindset and a willingness to operate hands-on in ambiguous environments, creating structure where processes, systems, or ownership models are still evolving.

  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to present complex accounting matters clearly and concisely to senior leadership and cross-functional partners.

  • Exemplary interpersonal skills and the ability to partner effectively with stakeholders across Finance, Legal, Tax, Procurement, Engineering, Infrastructure, and external organizations.

  • Genuine passion for technology and artificial intelligence, aligned with OpenAI’s mission.

  • CPA or CA required.

The goal of a Machine Learning Engineer at Scale is to leverage techniques in the fields of generative AI, computer vision, reinforcement learning, and agentic AI to improve Scale's products and customer experience in production environments. Our machine learning engineers take advantage of robust internal infrastructure and  unique access to massive datasets to deliver improvements to our customers.

Our Public Sector Machine Learning team is focused on deploying cutting-edge models to mission-critical government systems through products like  Donovan and Thunderforge. Our work spans multiple modalities, with a strong focus on both large language models and computer vision. On the LLM side, we are developing agentic systems that help solve complex operational and planning challenges for government partners. We're also advancing research in areas like reinforcement learning for agentic LLMs, with successful deployment into real-world operational environments. On the computer vision front, we're training advanced models to increase labeling throughput and automate perception tasks. Our efforts include building large-scale fine-tuning pipelines, training models across multiple modalities, and developing generalizable vision foundation models to support a wide range of defense applications.

You will:

  • Take state of the art models developed internally and from the community, use them in production to solve problems for our customers and taskers
  • Improve and maintain production models through retraining, hyperparameter tuning, and architectural updates, while preserving core performance characteristics
  • Collaborate with product and research teams to identify and prototype ML-driven product enhancements, including for upcoming product lines
  • Work with massive datasets to develop both generic models as well as fine tune models for specific products
  • Build scalable machine learning infrastructure to automate and optimize our ML services
  • Serve as a cross-functional representative and advocate for machine learning techniques across engineering and product organizations
  • Be comfortable learning new technologies quickly and managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment
  • Comfortable with light travel (approximately 10%) for customer interaction and team needs

  • 2+ years of experience building and deploying applied ML systems in production environments
  • Extensive experience with GenAI, Agentic AI, natural language processing, deep learning and deep reinforcement learning, or computer vision in a production environment
  • Solid background in algorithms, data structures, and object-oriented programming
  • Strong programming skills in Python, experience in Tensorflow or PyTorch

Nice to Haves:

  • Experience deploying software into environments you can't reach from your laptop - on-prem, edge, air-gapped, or otherwise restricted networks. Regulated industries count; the constraint is the point, not the sector.

  • Hands-on fine-tuning of open-weight models - LoRA/PEFT, instruction tuning, or training embedding models, at work or on your own.
  • Having written evaluations for a system whose output isn't deterministic: benchmarks, LLM judges, or a regression suite that caught something real.
  • Experience with geospatial data or maps - GIS tooling, spatial reference systems, or imagery.
  • A shipped project with real users behind it, where you owned it after launch rather than handing it off at merge.

The goal of a Senior Machine Learning Engineer at Scale is to own how we apply generative AI, agentic AI, computer vision, and reinforcement learning to mission-critical problems in production. Our senior machine learning engineers are handed problems that don't yet have an established approach, they propose the architecture, build it with support from other engineers, and are accountable for whether it holds up in the environments our customers depend on.

Our Public Sector Machine Learning team is focused on deploying cutting-edge models to mission-critical government systems through products like Donovan and Thunderforge. Our work spans multiple modalities, with our primary focus on agentic systems built on large language models. We are developing agents that solve complex operational and planning challenges for government partners: agent frameworks that integrate custom retrieval pipelines and production APIs, memory and context-management systems that hold state across long-running tasks, geospatial reasoning over maps and spatial data, and the evaluation tooling that benchmarks and refines agent behavior. We also apply reinforcement learning in targeted places where it earns its keep, and our computer vision work advances evaluation, labeling efficiency, and multimodal model training in support of defense applications.

As a Senior MLE, you'll have design authority over a capability area - the final say on the patterns used within your team, and the responsibility to make those patterns work under real constraints: classified environments, limited compute, and correctness requirements that don't bend.

You will:

  • Own the design and delivery of agent capabilities end to end - architecture, implementation, and the evaluation that proves they work
  • Define net-new patterns in problem spaces with no established approach, propose them to the wider team, and lead the work to build them
  • Take state of the art models developed internally and from the community and put them into production to solve problems for our customers and taskers
  • Improve and maintain production models and agents through retraining, hyperparameter tuning, and architectural updates, while preserving core performance characteristics
  • Build agent-level evaluation benchmarks, LLM judges, and verifiers - and use it to hillclimb performance rather than just report on it
  • Partner with product and research teams to scope and shape high-impact initiatives, including for upcoming product lines
  • Build scalable machine learning infrastructure to automate and optimize our ML services
  • Work directly with government users and subject-matter experts, and translate what you learn into technical direction
  • Act as a force multiplier and a primary reviewer for your team, mentoring at least one engineer, and your manager's go-to on feasibility questions
  • Communicate technical tradeoffs clearly to non-technical stakeholders
  • Treat security and compliance as design constraints to engineer around rather than blockers to route past
  • Serve as a cross-functional representative and advocate for machine learning techniques across engineering and product organizations
  • Be comfortable learning new technologies quickly and managing multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment
  • Comfortable with light travel (approximately 10%) for customer interaction and team needs

This role will require an active TS security clearance

Ideally You'd Have:

  • 5+ years of experience building and deploying applied ML systems in production environments
  • Extensive experience with GenAI, Agentic AI, natural language processing, deep learning and deep reinforcement learning, or computer vision in a production environment
  • A track record of owning architectural decisions and defending the tradeoffs behind them - not just implementing a design handed to you
  • Experience shipping agentic systems with real production traffic and evaluation rigor, rather than prototypes or demos
  • Solid background in algorithms, data structures, and object-oriented programming
  • Strong programming skills in Python, experience in PyTorch or Tensorflow
  • Experience mentoring or reviewing the work of other engineers

  • Experience deploying ML in classified, air-gapped, or IL5+ environments
  • Geospatial or GEOINT experience

Job Summary:

Job Summary


We are seeking a Character Effects Supervisor to support our upcoming feature film. The Character Effects Supervisor works inside of NAS to lead the CFX team on a specific film, overseeing hair, fur, cloth, garments, and other character-related simulations. This role ensures that character effects enhance performance and storytelling, align with the Director’s vision, and are technically robust for downstream departments, working within the direction and standards set by the Head of Character Effects and show leadership.

  • Provide input to Production Management and department leadership on CFX complexity and progress to support realistic planning and prioritization.
  • Mentor and support CFX artists, helping to identify training needs and contributing to performance feedback and career development.
  • Help foster a respectful, inclusive, and collaborative team culture where artists can do their best work.


What You’ll Need


  • Extensive experience in Character Effects/CFX within feature animation, VFX, or high‑end series, including time in a Lead or Supervisory role.
  • A strong reel demonstrating advanced hair, fur, cloth, and garment simulations and how they support character performance.
  • Proficiency with simulation tools such as Houdini and/or Maya, and solid understanding of CFX pipelines and caching strategies.

It is a global platform relied on by millions of people every day, from students and scientists to business leaders and innovators. The Excel Agent team’s mission is to make expert-level Excel capabilities available to everyone. People describe what they need in plain language, and the agent works in their workbook to help accomplish the task. It understands workbook context and user intent, plans and completes multi-step tasks using Excel capabilities, and checks its results before reporting back. We are building an agent people can trust with real work, one that brings in the right context, supports repeatable processes, and delivers results that remain editable and easy to verify.

You will own feature implementation, testing, and production support with minimal guidance while contributing to technical designs with support from more experienced engineers. You will work across client and service components and gain experience building reliable AI-powered experiences at scale.

We use AI throughout our engineering processes while maintaining accountability for the quality and reliability of our work. We use prototypes and experiments to test ideas and use data and customer feedback to inform our decisions. Overview

Build the foundation. Shape the team that follows. We are seeking a Principal Software Engineer to serve as a founding technical leader for the next generation of our commerce platform. You will define the engineering direction for a modern, extensible commerce ecosystem, translate customer and business needs into durable system designs, and make consequential cross-system technical decisions. This is an opportunity to establish the foundation, engineering standards, and reusable patterns that a future commerce engineering team can build on and extend.  

This is a hands-on individual contributor role with broad organizational influence. You will work through technical credibility, code and design reviews, prototypes, operational evidence, and clear engineering guardrails rather than direct reporting authority. You will partner across engineering, product, operations, security, privacy, systems integrators, and platform vendors to resolve ambiguity and raise the quality bar. Success means both delivering a dependable modern commerce platform and creating the technical foundation, practices, and culture needed for a future team to thrive. 

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees, we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day, we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond. 



Responsibilities

  • Own the end-to-end technical strategy and system design for the commerce ecosystem and its evolution roadmap.  

  • Define system boundaries, data ownership, interfaces, end-to-end flows, APIs, performance benchmarks, security, events, and integration patterns across product and SKU lifecycle, product information, pricing and promotions, storefront and content, search, cart and checkout, and the order lifecycle.  

  • Connect commerce capabilities to payments, tax, fraud prevention, fulfillment, returns, identity and consent, and telemetry and analytics.  

  • Establish clear engineering contracts with retained enterprise services so new and existing platforms can coexist without fragmented responsibilities or incompatible designs.  

  • Set technical direction and drive material cross-system design decisions within the commerce scope.  

  • Evaluate platform and build-versus-buy choices, configuration versus customization, interoperability, and vendor exit options.  

  • Make tradeoffs explicit, review partner and vendor designs, and use prototypes, code review, benchmarks, and operational evidence to validate high-risk assumptions.  

  • Define measurable engineering requirements for resilience, scalability, performance, observability, security, accessibility, and operating cost.  

  • Design for transaction integrity, idempotency, reconciliation, failure recovery, and traceability across distributed APIs and event-driven workflows.  

  • Guide modernization through implementation, migration, coexistence, release, cutover, and rollback.  

  • Partner with delivery teams to verify that implementation and production behavior conform to the intended system design and remain accountable for technical integrity and platform evolution after launch.  

  • Establish the engineering standards, reusable patterns, development practices, and decision mechanisms that will form the foundation of a future commerce engineering team.  

  • Lead technical and code reviews, resolve conflicting approaches, and document important decisions, alternatives, rationale, owners, and implications.  

  • Influence and mentor engineers and technical leads across partner teams without relying on direct reporting authority.  

  • Create clear guardrails that enable teams to move independently while maintaining system coherence, production quality, and shared engineering standards.  

  • Design and build the platform for AI-assisted and agentic commerce through well-defined interfaces and controlled access.  

  • Enable agentic capabilities to evolve safely over time, with appropriate permissions, consent, auditability, and controls for customer-impacting actions. 

Embody Microsoft’s culture and values.



Qualifications

Required Qualifications  

  • Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science or related technical field AND 6+ years technical engineering experience with coding in languages including, but not limited to, C, C++, C#, Java, JavaScript, or Python 

    • OR equivalent experience. 

Preferred Qualifications 

  • Architecture leadership experience: Lead complex, cross-team system design, resolve ambiguity, and influence technical decisions. 

  • Engineering experience: Design reliable distributed systems and modernize critical platforms while managing migration risk. 

  • Preferred experience: Commerce platforms, SaaS integrations, vendor evaluation, and governed AI capabilities.

FSO sits within Global Vendor Delivery & Solutions (GVDS) and is part of the Operations Service Center (OSC). The team brings together a portfolio of operational workstreams, including Intake & Demand, Bowler Management, MBO Vendor Spend, Audit & Controls and a set of transformation programs, which together underpin how sales operations are planned, governed and delivered.  

Role Purpose 

The Program Manager will provide the execution backbone for Frontier Sales Operations, integrating plans and dependencies across Intake & Demand, Bowler Management, MBO Vendor Spend, Audit & Controls and the broader program portfolio. The role translates portfolio decisions into disciplined execution, proactively manages risks and dependencies, drives accountability for commitments and provides a single, integrated view of program health. In doing so, it enables the Frontier Sales Ops leader to focus on strategic portfolio leadership, prioritization, investment and governance, while maintaining the execution rigor required to deliver FSO outcomes.



Responsibilities

Integrated Program Execution 

  • Own and maintain the integrated FSO program plan as the single source of truth for portfolio delivery. 

  • Translate priorities and leadership decisions into clear milestones, deliverables, owners and actions. 

  • Drive the day-to-day operating cadence across the portfolio, including planning, review and reporting forums. 

  • Ensure commitments progress to plan, and intervene early when execution moves off track. 

Cross-Workstream Management 

  • Coordinate execution across Intake & Demand, Bowler, Vendor Spend, Audit & Controls and individual transformation programs. 

  • Identify and actively manage cross-program dependencies, ensuring hand-offs and interlocks are understood and owned. 

  • Connect individual program managers' plans into a single, integrated portfolio view. 

  • Drive alignment and closure where delivery requires multiple teams or stakeholders. 

RAID & Dependency Management 

  • Own the portfolio-level process for risks, actions, issues, decisions and dependencies (RAID). 

  • Ensure material risks are identified early, with clear owners and mitigation plans. 

  • Escalate issues that require leadership intervention, with clear options and recommendations. 

  • Track leadership decisions through to execution and closure. 

Performance & Bowler Execution 

  • Manage the inputs and execution rhythm that support the FSO Bowler. 

  • Ensure milestones, KPIs and commitments have clear ownership and up-to-date status. 

  • Surface performance gaps and drive corrective actions to closure. 

  • Maintain traceability between portfolio commitments, actions and delivered outcomes.

  • Experience managing KPIs and scorecards (bowlers), including the operating rhythm that keeps them current.

  • Drives for results, holding self and others accountable for commitments and following through to closure.

This is a highly cross-functional role at the intersection of product marketing, engineering, product management, research, data, customer feedback, sales, and more.   • Bachelor’s Degree AND 8+ years experience, OR Master’s Degree AND 6+ years experience
  • Experience with AI products, evaluations, benchmarking, experimentation, or data-driven product development.

Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment.

 

Gray Systems Lab (GSL) is an applied research lab within Azure Data. We conduct research and development in databases, big data, and cloud systems, working closely with product teams to design innovative solutions to real-world problems. Our team is friendly and inclusive. We focus on a variety of exciting areas, including: machine learning for systems, reinforcement learning, fine-tuning and post-training techniques, agentic workflows and systems, resource management, query optimization and execution. We also work on workload optimization, graph analytics, data storage formats and governance, modern and emerging hardware (e.g., graphics processing units (GPUs), Non-Volatile Memory express (NVMe), and field-programmable gate arrays (FPGAs)), program analysis, data provenance, and ontologies. Our work spans both Microsoft internal and open-source systems, including Fabric, Spark, Structured Query Language (SQL) Server, MySQL, Apache Iceberg, and others. We provide opportunities to pursue ideas arising from internal collaborations and external partnerships with universities, while remaining active scholars in the research community.

 

 

We are looking for graduate students interested in cutting-edge research conducted in close collaboration with advanced industry product groups. Past Research Internships have resulted in both production-system impact and publications at top conferences. Applicants should demonstrate a track record in one or more areas of systems, databases, or data science, as well as an aptitude for hands-on system building and rigorous experimental design, including running and analyzing experiments at scale.

Research Interns put inquiry and theory into practice. Alongside fellow doctoral candidates and some of the world’s best researchers, Research Interns learn, collaborate, and network for life. Research Interns not only advance their own careers, but they also contribute to exciting research and development strides. During the 12-week internship, Research Interns are paired with mentors and expected to collaborate with other Research Interns and researchers, present findings, and contribute to the vibrant life of the community. Overview

Security represents the most critical priorities for our customers in a world awash in digital threats, regulatory scrutiny, and estate complexity. Microsoft Security aspires to make the world a safer place for all. We want to reshape security and empower every user, customer, and developer with a security cloud that protects them with end to end, simplified solutions. The Microsoft Security organization accelerates Microsoft’s mission and bold ambitions to ensure that our company and industry is securing digital technology platforms, devices, and clouds in our customers’ heterogeneous environments, as well as ensuring the security of our own internal estate.

 

The MDASH team is reimagining how organizations identify and remediate vulnerabilities in source code. Using AI agents and models, MDASH analyzes code to determine whether potential vulnerabilities are real and reachable, provides developers with actionable fixes, and helps verify that vulnerabilities have been successfully addressed.

 

We’re looking for a Senior Software Engineer to help build and evolve the MDASH scanning engine as we work to advance agentic code scanning. In this role, you’ll design and build systems that coordinate AI agents and models to analyze complex codebases, scale across programming languages and frameworks, validate security findings, generate high-quality fixes, and deliver reliable, efficient performance in production environments.

 

You’ll work closely with security researchers, applied scientists, model teams, and product managers to turn new techniques and evaluation insights into product capabilities. We’re looking for an engineer with experience building complex, large-scale systems, foundational knowledge of application security, and excitement about using AI to solve challenging problems in software security.

 

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond. 



Responsibilities
  • Design, build, and evolve the MDASH scanning engine, including agent orchestration, multi-model routing, code understanding, vulnerability detection, reachability validation, and fix generation and verification.
  • Extend the engine's coverage across vulnerability classes, programming languages, frameworks, build systems, and codebase sizes, from single services to large monorepos.
  • Integrate program analysis techniques into agent workflows to make detections more precise and grounded. These include static and dynamic analysis, taint tracking, call-graph and data-flow analysis, fuzzing, and sandboxed execution.
  • Improve the engine's precision, recall, consistency, and fix quality, working from evaluation results, research findings, and production feedback.
  • Optimize scan performance, scalability, cost, and latency so MDASH works well on enterprise-scale codebases and in CI/CD workflows.
  • Build a secure, reliable, observable engine, with strong isolation for running untrusted code and clear telemetry for diagnosing agent behavior.
  • Work with security research, applied science, model, and product teams to bring new techniques and models into the engine quickly and safely.
  • Track the agentic security and code-scanning landscape, and bring forward ideas that make MDASH stand out against competitors.
  • Write high-quality, well-tested code. Lead design reviews, take part in code reviews and on-call rotations, and help raise the engineering bar for the team.
  • Mentor other engineers and model Microsoft values to help build an inclusive environment where everyone can do their best work.


Qualifications

Required Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science or related technical field AND 4+ years technical engineering experience with coding in languages including, but not limited to, C, C++, C#, Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, or Python 
    • OR equivalent experience.

 

Other Requirements: Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings:

  • Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.

 

Preferred Qualifications: 

  • Master's Degree in Computer Science or related technical field AND 6+ years technical engineering experience with coding in languages including, but not limited to, C, C++, C#, Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, or Python 
    • OR Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science or related technical field AND 8+ years technical engineering experience with coding in languages including, but not limited to, C, C++, C#, Java, JavaScript, TypeScript, or Python 
    • OR equivalent experience. 
  • Experience building production systems with large language models, such as AI agents, multi-agent orchestration, tool calling, planning, context management, or code-understanding systems.
  • Experience building or working on security scanners, static analysis (SAST), dynamic analysis (DAST), software composition analysis (SCA), compilers, or other program analysis tools.
  • Working knowledge of vulnerability classes such as memory safety, injection, authentication and authorization, deserialization, path traversal, SSRF, and business-logic flaws.
  • Experience with program analysis techniques such as taint analysis, data-flow and control-flow analysis, code property graphs, fuzzing, or symbolic execution.
  • Experience building distributed, high-scale cloud services on Azure, including containerized or sandboxed execution.
  • Familiarity with multiple software ecosystems and build systems across C/C++, C#, Java, JavaScript/TypeScript, Python, and cloud-native applications.
  • A passion for developer experience, and for building tools that engineers trust and act on.

Microsoft's Detection and Response Team (DART) is seeking a skilled and experienced Cybersecurity Resilience Lead to join the team in the United States. You will lead proactive resilience engagements, establish delivery priorities and act as a trusted advisor for customers, including executive stakeholders. Working with incident responders, threat hunters, infrastructure engineers, reverse engineers and operations teams, you will help customers improve readiness before an incident and strengthen durable response capability after lessons learned.

Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I Critical Environment Program Manager - Metrology, you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development of all employees and offers trainings and opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion trainings and events, and professional certifications.

Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 datacenters in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.

With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our datacenter design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.



Responsibilities

Data Center Operations/Service Delivery:

  • Establish strong working relationships with customers.
  • Own the delivery and continuous improvement of the data center metrology program, including calibration and verification governance for critical mechanical, electrical, environmental, and life safety instrumentation.
    • Manage preventive maintenance, calibration, verification, and out-of-tolerance remediation for electrical and mechanical equipment instrumentation.
    • Use enterprise software to register instruments, maintain calibration histories and due dates, issue and assign calibration, verification, and corrective work orders.
    • Monitor execution, review certificates and as-found/as-left results, and verify that completed work meets approved procedures, tolerances, traceability, and documentation standards.
  • Ensure electrical, mechanical, environmental, and fire/life safety equipment and associated instrumentation provide accurate, reliable, and traceable measurement results.
  • Establish and maintain standardized metrology program governance, procedures, calibration methods, documentation, traceability, and measurement uncertainty expectations across supported data center locations.
  • Act as escalation point for metrology issues, including overdue calibration, out-of-tolerance conditions, emergency support, technician coaching, and recommendations on instrument selection for electrical/mechanical design parameters; escalating significant operational risk as needed.
  • Lead metrology projects from conception through completion, including instrument onboarding, calibration capability deployment, procedure development, laboratory or vendor readiness, and digitization of calibration records and workflows.
  • Provide reporting on critical infrastructure and metrology performance, including calibration compliance, overdue work, out-of-tolerance events, vendor performance, operational and maintenance KPIs, objectives, and adherence to organizational policies, procedures, and standards.

The next breakthrough in artificial intelligence (AI) needs more than powerful accelerators: it needs a network that makes them work as a supercomputer. On Azure Networking’s infrastructure team, you build networking for Microsoft-developed AI accelerators and GPUs from NVIDIA, AMD and other suppliers. You turn advances in connectivity into regional network designs that deliver reliable, high-performance training and inference at Microsoft scale.

As a Senior Technical Program Manager in Azure Networking, you will own the introduction of the next-generation Ethernet platform for regional networking at Microsoft scale, from requirements and regional network design through interoperability validation, workload testing, operational readiness and staged production deployments. You will independently drive this charter, creating clarity from ambiguity and aligning engineering and operations on priorities, tradeoffs and delivery. You will draw on Microsoft’s networking innovation, including Software for Open Networking in the Cloud (SONiC), high-bandwidth networks for Fairwater-class datacenters, and advances in Remote Direct Memory Access (RDMA) and Multipath Reliable Connection (MRC).

This opportunity will allow you to expand your influence on regional network architecture at Microsoft scale; deepen your expertise in workload-driven platform decisions; and extend your technical leadership across engineering, operations and industry partners.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. Finance Managers in our team help us transform the way we measure business performance, manage resources, and lead financial activities using business intelligence, modeling, and analytics. In the Excel Product Group, we’re building an intelligence layer that does just that, and we’re just getting started. We’re looking for a Senior Product Manager, Excel Copilot to join us as we reinvent what it means to work with data, bringing the power of the world’s best AI models together with Excel to give every person new superpowers for getting their work done. 

Excel is one of the world’s most widely used tools for working with data. From a student building their first budget, to an analyst forecasting a business, to experts building extraordinarily sophisticated financial and operational models, people turn to Excel to understand information, explore possibilities, and make decisions. 

Our team builds the core Excel experience across Windows and Mac. We are a diverse, worldwide, passionate, customer-obsessed team with a highly collaborative environment. We believe world-class products come from world-class teams, and we work as deliberately on our culture as we do on our product. 望ましい経験/スキル:

You will partner directly with leaders across Apple’s software and hardware organizations to propose, develop, and evaluate features for new silicon generations, representing Apple’s compute and ML roadmap while the hardware is still taking shape.

Contribute to the bring-up of new chips and products built on our new GPUs

This role owns delivery across Meta's EMEA co-location estate, while partnering with an APAC-based counterpart to support projects in that region and provide coverage across the combined portfolio.   • Share accountability with the other International Payroll Manager for the accuracy, timeliness and local compliance of payroll across 39 countries and multiple legal entities, owning delivery end to end for your organization

  • Drive standardization and touchless processing by reducing country-level variation, eliminating manual touchpoints and improving system integration, and reinvest the capacity created in business partnership and continuous improvement

  • Sustain delivery, controls and team health through operating model changes, system implementations, new entity launches and regulatory change

Meta is seeking a graduate mechanical engineering student with a strong background in finite element analysis (FEA) to join our Accelerator Reference Design (ARD) team.   • shadow moiré, strain gauge) and refine models to improve accuracy.

  • Experience correlating simulation with physical test data
  • Experience bringing ECAD/MCAD data into FEA models
  • Familiarity with 3D CAD (Creo preferred
  • SolidWorks acceptable) for geometry cleanup and simplification
  • Scripting or automation experience (e.g. Python, APDL) for parametric studies or post-processing
  • Strong analytical, technical writing and communication skills

Meta is seeking Security Engineers with Privacy and Data protection expertise to join our Applied Artificial Intelligence (AAI) organization. You will apply deep privacy engineering expertise to hard, real-world problems in how systems collect, use, retain, expose, and delete data. Your work is AI-augmented from day one: you leverage AI tools and agents to accelerate your impact, and where the models fall short, your expertise directly drives their improvement. The problems that matter here are the ones a capable engineer cannot solve by reading the code in front of them: which jurisdiction's deadline applies to a deletion request, whether a derived dataset clears an anonymity threshold, where a deletion has to cascade. Models already handle the privacy obligations that are stated as ordinary good engineering practice, so the work is the obligation they cannot derive. This role is for privacy engineers who want to operate at the intersection of deep privacy expertise and frontier AI, not just applying AI to privacy work but shaping what it is capable of.

Responsibilities

  • Apply deep privacy and data protection expertise to identify, scope, and solve complex problems that require multi-step reasoning, novel approaches, and expert judgment
  • Build privacy capabilities, tools, and evaluation environments, prototyping AI-driven solutions to real-world privacy problems at Meta's scale
  • Design and execute privacy obligation analysis, de-identification assessment, data lifecycle review, or data access reasoning augmented by AI tools and agents
  • Identify where AI models lack privacy reasoning capability and directly contribute to improving them through expert-generated signals, evaluation, and feedback
  • Collaborate with model researchers to translate privacy expertise into training signals, decomposing hard problems into structured challenges that teach models to reason like privacy engineers
  • Partner with legal, policy, product, and infrastructure teams to translate obligations into engineering requirements
  • Own complex privacy initiatives end to end, from problem definition through delivery, and contribute to technical direction within the team
  • Disseminate findings through internal publications, knowledge sharing, and contributions to the broader privacy and security community

  • B.S. or M.S. in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or related field, or equivalent experience
  • 5+ years of hands-on engineering experience in technical privacy, data protection, or privacy-adjacent security engineering
  • Deep expertise in at least one privacy subdomain with demonstrated ability to advance the state of the art: purpose limitation, retention and deletion, data access control, jurisdictional obligations, de-identification, consent, or ML and model privacy
  • Experience implementing privacy obligations in production systems, in addition to reviewing or advising on them
  • Software engineering proficiency, including code review and maintenance, with experience coding in Python, PHP, Java, C/C++, or an equivalent language
  • Track record of architecting privacy systems, controls or programs that operate at scale and influence how others build
  • Demonstrated ability to define and drive complex, ambiguous problem spaces with group-level impact

Preferred Qualifications

  • Demonstrated ongoing AI skill development (e.g., prompt/context engineering, agent orchestration) and staying current with emerging AI technologies
  • Experience applying differential privacy, k-anonymity, or other formal de-identification techniques in production rather than in research only
  • Experience with pseudonymization lifecycle, including deletion of the user-to-pseudonym mapping
  • Experience adhering to and implementing responsible, ethical AI practices (e.g., risk assessment, bias mitigation, quality and accuracy reviews)
  • Experience implementing obligations conditioned on jurisdiction, age band, or cohort: regional carve-outs, regulatory deadlines, minor and parent-initiated request handling
  • Experience improving AI model performance through expert feedback, red teaming, or evaluation design
  • Background in ML and model privacy: memorization, membership inference, training-data extractability, disclosure through model outputs
  • Demonstrated ability to integrate AI tools to optimize/redesign workflows and drive measurable impact (e.g., efficiency gains, quality improvements)
  • Contributions to the privacy or security community (original research, tools, conference presentations, publications)
  • Experience with privacy review or privacy incident response at scale

Meta is seeking Security Engineers with Trust & Safety expertise to join our Applied Artificial Intelligence (AAI) organization. You will apply deep domain expertise in online abuse and adversarial behavior, across areas such as child safety, human exploitation, fraud and scams, violent extremism, and coordinated inauthentic behavior, to advance what AI systems can do in Trust & Safety. Your work is AI-augmented from day one: you leverage AI tools and agents to accelerate your impact, and where the models fall short, your expertise directly drives their improvement. The problems here are the ones where abuse comes from behavior, context, and scale rather than a software defect: a model that overtrusts an asserted authorization, an agent pressured into a policy exception, a campaign in which every artifact looks benign on its own. Models recognize public benchmarks far more readily than internal ones, so building evaluations that hold up is part of the engineering process. This role is for Trust & Safety practitioners who want to operate at the intersection of deep domain expertise and frontier AI, not just applying AI to protect from and prevent adversarial behavior, but shaping what it is capable of.

Responsibilities

  • Identify and solve ambiguous problems within a Trust & Safety domain where the solution and requirements are initially unknown, driving solutions that affect multiple teams
  • Architect Trust & Safety capabilities and evaluation infrastructure that set the standard across teams; drive platform-level decisions for AI-driven solutions at Meta's scale
  • Lead the strategy and methodology for the abuse problems AI cannot yet reason about: age-aware policy boundaries, adversaries who adapt to enforcement, abuse at campaign scale, and policy interpretation under pressure
  • Shape how Trust & Safety expertise translates into AI capability: define the methodologies that make model improvement systematic and scalable
  • Drive cross-organizational partnerships that define how Trust & Safety and AI intersect: influence technical direction beyond the immediate team
  • Break down problems into smaller scoped workstreams, owning the most technically complex pieces while enabling others to execute against the overall solution
  • Mentor other engineers across the organization, build community, and act as a role model for Trust & Safety engineering practices and Meta values
  • Disseminate findings through internal publications, knowledge sharing, and contributions to the broader community

Minimum Qualifications

  • B.S. or M.S. in Computer Science, Cybersecurity, or related field, or equivalent experience. OR PhD + 2 years of hands-on engineering experience
  • 5+ years of hands-on engineering experience in Trust & Safety, integrity, fraud and abuse, or security investigations
  • Demonstrated depth in at least one abuse domain: child safety and youth protection, dangerous organizations and violent extremism, fraud and scams, coordinated inauthentic behavior and information operations, or content policy enforcement
  • Experience building detection, enforcement or evaluation systems in an abuse domain, in addition to operating or investigating within one
  • Experience analyzing and interpreting large-scale data, including relational databases and SQL, to identify patterns of adversarial behavior and quantify trends
  • Experience investigating and acting on high-impact threats and online threat actors
  • Experience coding in at least one of the following or similar languages: PHP, Python, or Java

Preferred Qualifications

  • Demonstrated ongoing AI skill development (e.g., prompt/context engineering, agent orchestration) and staying current with emerging AI technologies
  • Experience with campaign-level investigation and attribution of coordinated adversary networks
  • Experience adhering to and implementing responsible, ethical AI practices (e.g., risk assessment, bias mitigation, quality and accuracy reviews)
  • Experience adversarially testing conversational or agentic systems: jailbreaks, social engineering, prompt injection, policy-exception pressure
  • Experience authoring or interpreting enforcement guidelines at scale, including coded terminology and evolving slang
  • Experience with age assurance and age-signal inference, including calibrated confidence and mode switching
  • Contributions to the Trust & Safety or security community (original research, tools, conference presentations, publications)
  • Experience developing and evaluating classifiers for abuse, fraud, or policy enforcement
  • Demonstrated ability to integrate AI tools to optimize/redesign workflows and drive measurable impact (e.g., efficiency gains, quality improvements)
  • Experience improving AI model performance through expert feedback, red-teaming, or evaluation design

Your work is AI-augmented from day one: you leverage AI tools and agents to accelerate your impact, and where the models fall short, your expertise directly drives their improvement. The problems that matter here are the ones a capable engineer cannot solve by reading the code in front of them: which jurisdiction's deadline applies to a deletion request, whether a derived dataset clears an anonymity threshold, where a deletion has to cascade. About the role

As a Communications Manager at Anthropic, you will bring The Anthropic Institute's research to the world. The Institute works to advance the public conversation around AI, publishing findings so that policymakers, researchers, journalists, and the public can reckon with what's here and prepare for what's ahead. 

You will provide dedicated communications coverage for the Institute's two largest and fastest growing research engines: 1) Economic Research, which tracks AI's effect on jobs, wages, and the broader economy through the Anthropic Economic Index and labor market analysis, and 2) Societal Impacts, which studies how Claude is actually used, from workplace impacts and personal guidance to Claude's values and frontier agent use. You’ll also support TAI’s other teams, including Special Projects and the Frontier Red Team. 

In this role, you'll drive research tracking, publication strategy, and reactive press across both portfolios, including launches like quarterly Economic Index releases and the rollout of the new Economic Research Fund. You'll partner closely with the Economic Research and Societal Impacts research teams day to day, work alongside the Deputy Communications Lead, and coordinate with Anthropic's broader communications, policy, and editorial teams to keep messaging aligned while maintaining the Institute's distinct voice.

Responsibilities

  • Drive day-to-day communications for the Economic Research and Societal Impacts teams, including research tracking, publication planning, and reactive press
  • Lead communications planning and launch execution for the Anthropic Economic Index, recurring labor market analyses, and new research initiatives like the Economic Research Fund
  • Develop narratives that translate technical and quantitative research for audiences well beyond specialist communities
  • Build and maintain relationships with reporters across economics, labor, technology, research, and general interest outlets, along with academic economists and think tank researchers
  • Draft communications plans, briefing documents, talking points, press materials, and social content
  • Manage reactive press on sensitive findings in partnership with the Communications Lead, Deputy Communications Lead, and policy team
  • Partner with policy and editorial teams on publishing strategy, ensuring research reaches the largest appropriate audience through the Anthropic blog, the Institute's site, microsites, interactive experiences, video, and audio
  • Present researchers for media interviews, podcast appearances, and speaking engagements, and prepare them to succeed in those moments
  • Partner with Institute communications leadership on major announcements and milestone engagements
  • Build repeatable rollout playbooks and processes that allow a lean team to cover a growing research portfolio
  • Track both teams' research agendas to shape findings early and plan publications months in advance

  • Have deep communications experience, with significant depth in research, science, economics, or policy communications
  • Have a track record of translating complex, technical, or academic research into public narratives that reach audiences well beyond specialist communities
  • Are comfortable reading and interrogating quantitative research, and can engage substantively and credibly with the researchers who produce it
  • Have strong, active media relationships
  • Can move between long-lead strategic messaging and fast-turnaround tactical execution without losing quality, from planning a launch months out to handling an inbound press inquiry the same day
  • Have led multi-channel rollouts spanning strategy, digital, press, and cross-functional approvals

  • Thrive in fast-moving environments where priorities shift and ambiguity is common
  • Are excited about Anthropic's mission to develop AI that is safe and beneficial

About the role

Anthropic's Beneficial Deployments team brings Claude to organizations doing some of the world's most important work across the nonprofit and education sectors. These organizations share a problem: mission-critical work, thin budgets, and little slack to figure out new technology on their own. Our Customer Success team helps them go from first login to Claude being part of how their teams work, but we cannot do that one organization at a time, nor should we. The sector already has trusted intermediaries these organizations turn to first: networks, capacity builders, funder technical assistance providers, community colleges, and fellowship programs. This role exists to make those intermediaries as effective at activating and training organizations on Claude as our own Customer Success team is.

As the Scaled Enablement Lead, you'll build the Claude for Nonprofits train-the-trainer program that qualifies intermediaries to onboard organizations and deliver Anthropic-designed workshops on our behalf. You'll own the kits, credentials, and quality gates that let them run the show without an Anthropic CSM in the room. You'll also own the enablement thinking behind scaling impact through Claude Corps: how what fellows learn and build serves every organization we support, not only the ones that host them.

The people you enable are not selling Claude. They are trainers, implementers, and program staff whose job is to help mission-driven organizations meaningfully adopt AI. Your job is to make sure these intermediaries can do that with Claude, to the same bar we hold ourselves to, and to help them evolve their offerings as we learn what these organizations need. The measure of success for this role is organizations activated and trained well without Anthropic delivering it.

You'll be half program builder, half facilitator. You'll design and deliver the first cohorts yourself, then make the system repeatable: kits, qualification paths, credentials, teach-back gates, and a refresh rhythm that keeps content current as our products change. You'll build on the operating model and certification infrastructure of Anthropic's Education team and own everything specific to this audience, working closely with Beneficial Deployments Customer Success, Partnerships, Claude Corps program leadership, and our Education teams.

This is not a partner account management or alliances role, and it carries no quota. It is not a book-of-business Customer Success role either, though you'll spend time with organizations to stay grounded in what these nonprofits truly need. The role reports to the Customer Success Lead for Beneficial Deployments, has no direct reports today, and may grow into people management as the program scales. Expect periodic travel for in-person cohorts and sessions.

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril's Air & Missile Defense Radar team develops cutting-edge tracking algorithms and software systems that detect, track, and characterize airborne threats in real-time. Working in small, focused teams, our software engineers design and implement sophisticated tracking solutions that protect lives and critical assets. Our work spans the full spectrum—from developing novel multi-target tracking algorithms to building high-performance distributed systems that process massive amounts of sensor data in milliseconds

We don't just publish papers; we deploy production-grade systems that our government and industry customers depend on for mission-critical operations. If you're passionate about applying mathematics, software engineering, and signal processing to solve complex real-world problems, we want to hear from you.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Design and implement advanced tracking algorithms for novel air and missile threats, including multi-target tracking, track fusion, and discrimination techniques
  • Develop high-performance, real-time software systems that process radar sensor data and maintain tracks on dozens to hundreds of simultaneous targets
  • Build and leverage modeling & simulation environments to validate tracking performance, quantify system capabilities, and identify areas for improvement
  • Collaborate directly with radar engineers and system architects to integrate tracking solutions into end-to-end defense systems
  • Optimize tracking software for performance-critical environments where milliseconds matter
  • Communicate technical concepts and trade-offs to cross-functional teams, program leadership, and customers to drive informed decisions
  • Participate in customer demonstrations and field tests to ensure successful deployment and operational effectiveness

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 2 years of relevant experience & Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Physics, or related technical field (or equivalent experience)
  • Strong programming skills in C++ and Python
  • Solid foundation in mathematics: linear algebra, probability, statistics, and/or differential equations
  • Understanding of software engineering fundamentals: design patterns, testing, version control, and debugging
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Top Secret SCI security clearance

DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience with tracking, estimation, or filtering algorithms (Kalman filters, particle filters, multiple hypothesis tracking, etc.)
  • Background in controls, estimation theory, or digital signal processing
  • Familiarity with radar systems or sensor fusion
  • Experience with high-performance computing (multithreading, GPU acceleration, distributed systems)
  • Knowledge of machine learning techniques for classification, clustering, or data association
  • Proficiency with database technologies (SQL, NoSQL, time-series databases)
  • Experience with web development technologies (JavaScript, React, Node.js) for building visualization and analysis tools
  • Familiarity with modeling and simulation tools (MATLAB, Simulink, or custom frameworks)
  • Experience working in agile development environments
  • Active U.S. Top Secret SCI clearance

Protecting Yourself from Recruitment Scams

Anduril is committed to maintaining the integrity of our Talent acquisition process and the security of our candidates. These scammers often attempt to extract payment or sensitive personal information.

To ensure your safety and help you navigate your job search with confidence, please keep the following critical points in mind:

  • No Financial Requests: Anduril will never solicit payment or demand personal financial details (such as banking information, credit card numbers, or social security numbers) at any stage of our hiring process. Our legitimate recruitment is entirely free for candidates.

  • Please always verify communications:

ABOUT THE TEAM 

In the Space Special Programs team, we build spacecraft and space systems which serve a wide variety of functions in the space architecture. At a time when space superiority can no longer be taken for granted and with space systems proliferating at an incredible rate, the Space Special Programs team provides advanced, mission critical capabilities to our customer base to be able to more effectively operate and survive within this expanding environment with limited personnel. Working across product, engineering, sales, logistics, operations, and mission success, the Space Special Programs team develops, tests, deploys, and operates new, unique, space capabilities to drive mission success in challenging operational environments. 

ABOUT THE JOB 

We are looking for Circuit Designers to join our rapidly growing team in Chantilly, VA. In this role, you will be responsible for Full Cycle PCB design for spacecraft and associated systems including deriving requirements, schematic design, component selection, supervision or completion of layout, bring-up, test, debug and integration with the system. The engineering team as a whole must span the capabilities of digita-to-analog circuit design, analog circuit design, RF circuit design, digital circuit design (including FPGA, SOC, and MCU implementations), motor control, small power system design, and ultra-low power circuitry, as well as computer engineering basics such as basic embedded software and PC-based tools, and FPGA development in VHDL.  

WHAT YOU’LL DO 

  • Work with a cross-functional team to design market leading space flight hardware and associated ground equipment products 
  • Implement product components through rapid prototyping, design verification, and space qualification activities 
  • Learn and apply modern space-flight hardware design standards and guidelines to create high-reliability, highly manufacturable assemblies 
  • Implement combinations of high-speed digital, precision analog, RF, and ultra low-power designs 
  • Participate in peer-level and cross-discipline design reviews and collaborate with other EEs on your team to improve everyone’s capabilities 
  • Low level firmware development for bring-up and test 
  • Root cause investigation data collection and analysis in support of production operations 
  • Work in a fast-paced environment, having to juggle multiple concurrent projects and changing delivery timelines 

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS 

  • B.S. in electrical / computer engineering or similar engineering or technical field  
  • 2-8 years of professional experience, in hardware product development 
  • Basic understanding of PCB Layout techniques to meet space flight mechanical, electrical, and manufacturing requirements 
  • Ability to read and interpret schematics and apply best practices appropriate for each design 
  • Familiarity with standard interfaces such as Ethernet, CAN, I2C, SPI, PCIe, MIPI CSI-2, etc 
  • Familiarity with common MCU, CPU, FPGA devices and technologies 
  • Knowledge of modern analog and digital electronics and electronic circuits 
  • Ability to determine manage work assignments based on prioritized direction from management, near-term goals, and day-to-day levels of progress 
  • Experience using Altium Designer or equivalent E-CAD tools 
  • Excellent communication skills and ability to work effectively with others 
  • Ability to work within our company and team culture and take ownership of the tasks assigned to you 
  • Willing to listen and learn from experts but still speak up when you have ideas 
  • Must be a U.S. Citizen and able to obtain and maintain a U.S. Top Secret security clearance 

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 

  • Experience designing, integrating, and flying Cubesat spacecraft meant to operate in LEO through GEO environments is a significant plus 
  • 1+ years of experience working in a classified environment is a plus
