ABOUT THE TEAM

Core Technology is the engineering backbone of Anduril's hardware platforms — the shared systems, components, and infrastructure that power products across every division. The team develops and sustains the critical electromechanical systems, drive systems, propulsion, actuation, and embedded electronics that make Anduril's autonomous systems work.  The Quality team works with our customers, internal teams, and suppliers to ensure the deployment of reliable products that meet all mission requirements. We develop cutting-edge Quality processes and methods to secure scalable, long-term business success. As a Senior Product Quality Engineer, you will work inside and outside the organization to define and execute processes that deliver reliable products. The right person for this role has knowledge of manufacturing, product development, and continuous improvement as well as some experience with electromagnetic warfare systems such as RF countermeasures, electromagnetic energy, electronic masking, probing, reconnaissance, and intelligence along with electronic security, emission control, spectrum management. If you are someone who loves to build world-class Quality processes, work hands-on, and be accountable for results, then this role is for you.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Own the elimination of product risk to improve reliability across the product lifecycle with a key focus on PCBA product quality. Lead Quality activities from concept through development and manufacturing to field use.
  • Define, execute, and continuously improve product and process requirements. Partner with production to establish and refine incoming material inspection, process control plans, and end of line test to capture the essential quality requirements for successful customer shipments.
  • Drive cross-functional alignment to define and execute product quality requirements. Serve as the quality authority for your product line, influencing engineering, manufacturing, supply chain, and program stakeholders.
  • Lead Root Cause and Corrective Action (RCCA) and Material Review Board (MRB) activities for critical PCBA and system level interactions. Coach junior engineers on investigation methodology. Review the effectiveness of actions and drive lessons learned across the product team and broader quality organization.
  • Lead containment actions to segregate nonconforming parts on the production line. Establish containment protocols and ensure rapid response across shifts and work centers.
  • Lead product health data analysis and improvement activities. Define quality metrics, dashboards, and reporting cadences. Support customer quality issues and refurbishment testing and quality control.
  • Support change control board by identifying quality risks related to engineering changes of production parts. Provide data-driven risk assessments to inform disposition decisions.
  • Drive the continuous improvement of the Quality Management System. Define and improve required documentation, processes, and activities. Identify systemic gaps and lead initiatives to close them.
  • Mentor and develop junior quality engineers and inspectors. Set technical standards and best practices for the product quality team.
  • Support investigations, initiatives, and projects as needed, at the team or organization level.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering or similar technical field
  • 5+ years of experience in product quality, manufacturing quality, or reliability engineering for electronic systems or PCBA products
  • Strong working knowledge of AS9100 based Quality Management System requirements
  • Experience with the design and development of safety-critical circuitry of Ignition Safety Devices (ISD) and Electronic Safe and Arm Devices (ESAD)
  • Develop and execute quality management strategies of Printed Circuit Board Assemblies (PCBA)
  • Demonstrated experience working with RF and/or electronic systems with particular experience in PCBA design, development, and sustainment
  • Understanding of Gerber Files and reading schematics
  • Usage of electrical instrumentation to assess RC in PCBA's such as, multimeter, Oscilloscope, Logic Probes, Thermal Cameras.
  • IPC 610/620 and J-STD-001 knowledge - certification
  • Strong working knowledge of product development methodologies such as Failure Modes and Effects Analysis (FMEA), Advanced Product Quality Planning (APQP), and Geometric Dimensioning and Tolerancing (GD&T)
  • Experience leading RCCA and MRB activities with demonstrated results in defect reduction or yield improvement
  • Strong working knowledge of mechanical and/or electrical manufacturing processes
  • Proven track record in Engineering, Manufacturing, or Quality in aerospace/defense, automotive, medical device, or similar complex hardware
  • A strong ownership mindset with demonstrated capability to drive cross-functional projects from start to completion
  • Ability to obtain and hold a US Security Clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Master’s degree in Electrical Engineering or similar
  • Experience with RF test systems, data collection, analysis, and optimization for production control
  • Defense, national security or RF communication systems familiarity through industry or education
  • Delivered electronics warfare, RF or electronics products into production
  • Active TS/SCI clearance
  • Experience with low volume, high complexity manufacturing

About The Team
Anduril's Space team is at the forefront of advancing national security capabilities in the space domain. Our mission is twofold: 1) develop autonomous satellite systems and space-based platforms, and 2) deliver critical ground and orbital software infrastructure at scale. We transform products and capabilities across space command and control (C2), mission management, and space operations from early concepts into fully operational systems by partnering closely with specialist engineering, operations, and production teams. Through our integrated approach, we design and deploy space software systems using advanced algorithms, distributed architectures, and resilient infrastructure—delivering reliable, mission-critical capabilities that support operators across orbital and ground-based assets. Space Systems hires software engineers and systems engineers who are excited to build across a diverse and powerful portfolio—from satellite operations software to space domain awareness platforms. Our teams contribute to highly capable autonomous space systems and ground software products that operate reliably in the most demanding mission environments, supporting the DOD and IC in defending our national interests in space.

About The Job
Anduril is hiring Senior Radar Engineers to architect and deliver next-generation space-based radar systems that will redefine orbital ISR and tactical sensing. We're building software-defined RF payloads designed to break free from traditional satellite development timelines, and we need engineers who can operate at the intersection of advanced electromagnetics, real-time signal processing, and autonomous space operations. Depending on your level and fit, you'll lead a high-performing radar engineering team, direct cross-functional groups spanning payload development and mission software, or own a broader technical portfolio integrating space-based sensors with Anduril's C2 infrastructure. These roles combine hands-on technical leadership with people management and customer engagement, driving complex space programs from concept through launch to on-orbit operations. More senior candidates will additionally own multi-team strategy, executive-level customer relationships, and portfolio-scale outcomes.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Architect and implement RF sensing technologies for space-based radar payloads and multi-domain platforms
  • Collaborate with cross-functional teams to define system architectures and concepts of operations for complex space missions
  • Conduct rigorous system-of-systems analysis to decompose mission requirements into radar subsystem specifications, link budgets, and performance trades
  • Develop and validate advanced radar techniques, waveforms, signal processing algorithms, and detection/tracking technologies
  • Create and drive consensus on internal technical roadmaps for space radar capabilities
  • Engage directly with DoD and IC customers to translate operational needs into technical requirements
  • Provide technical leadership to program management and business development teams to support strategic decision-making
  • Mentor and grow team members in radar theory, space systems engineering, and best practices

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • BS or MS degree in Electrical Engineering, Physics, Mathematics, or related technical field (advanced degree preferred)
  • 5+ years of hands-on experience in radar systems engineering, including hardware, algorithms, or software development
  • Proven track record in a technical leadership role developing high-performance defense radar systems
  • Strong expertise in radar architecture, waveform design, radar modes, and system-level modeling
  • Proficiency in MATLAB and Python for radar simulation and analysis
  • Prior experience supporting DoD or IC programs
  • Active U.S. Top Secret or TS/SCI clearance


PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Hands-on experience developing space-based RF sensing systems, including satellite payload design, orbital mechanics considerations, and space environmental effects (radiation, thermal, plasma) on radar performance
  • Proficiency in C++ for real-time embedded systems or signal processing pipelines
  • Experience with SAR (Synthetic Aperture Radar), GMTI (Ground Moving Target Indicator), or space-based SIGINT modes
  • Understanding of radar antenna development, technology, and integration
  • Familiarity with spacecraft operations, space mission design tools, or hardware-in-the-loop integration with ground stations
  • Understanding of space software standards (e.g., cFS, SpaceVPX) and modular payload architectures

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril’s Manufacturing team is seeking a Senior Radio Frequency Manufacturing Test Engineer to join our Electromagnetic Warfare team. The EW Manufacturing Team is responsible for rapidly iterating and building cutting-edge defense hardware for Electromagnetic Warfare. This responsibility includes everything in the manufacturing value-chain, including, but not limited to, Design for Manufacturability work, tool design & selection, process creation & optimization, vendor sourcing & interaction, quality planning, and work documentation associated with the hardware that the Manufacturing Engineer owns.

ABOUT THE JOB 

As a Senior RF Manufacturing Test Engineer within EW, you will you will be responsible for ensuring that we are testing our systems to stringent standards ensuring that we are consistently shipping the highest quality products to our customers. Additionally you will ensure that we are able to meet the required throughput requirements of production. In this role you’ll need to think creatively and come up with solutions to solve difficult testing problems and push to continuously improve our methods of automation, throughput, user interfaces, and data analytics.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Maintain ownership of test activities in production and ensuring production test flow. Provide hands-on troubleshooting efforts and resolve complex electrical issues found during testing.
  • Maintain test capabilities across the manufacturing value stream - from system level checkouts and acceptance testing to key component level in process validation.
  • Improve and sustain existing test systems to improve automation, consistency, total cycle time, and test coverage (DfM).
  • Generate test work instructions that can be easily followed by technician team in MES. Train technicians on equipment use as required.
  • Develop library of common failure modes with troubleshooting guide/diagrams for fast issue resolution.
  • Determine root cause of product failures and recommend appropriate corrective actions (RCCA).
  • Work with Design, Quality and Manufacturing Engineering teams to support customer returns and failure analysis.
  • Contribute feedback to early-stage test design for test processes supporting early-stage products (NPI).
  • Analyze test data, document results, and provide detailed reports to identify defects and areas for improvement.
  • Collaborate with design engineers to provide feedback and recommendations for product enhancements based on test outcomes.
  • Optimize test strategies for efficiency and effectiveness, reducing test time without compromising quality.
  • Maintain and calibrate test equipment to ensure precision and reliability.
  • Support continuous improvement initiatives by identifying opportunities to enhance testing processes and methodologies.
  • Execute testing as required.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS 

  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical/Electronics, Computer, Mechanical Engineering, or related fields
  • 8+ years of relevant industry experience with emphasis on manufacturing test and product sustainment.
  • Familiarity with Linux, Ubuntu, LabVIEW, and NixOS.
  • Experience with contract manufacturers in the testing of PCBA/electronic assemblies. Thorough knowledge of PCBA testing standards and methods.
  • Familiarity with electronics test equipment such as power supplies, electronic loads, oscilloscope, function generators, spectrum analyzers, data acquisition and measurement sensors.
  • Strong root cause analysis skills of non-conforming hardware.
  • Excellent written, verbal, interpersonal and communication skills.
  • Familiar with Product Life Cycle (PLM) systems, Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), and Test Execution Systems (TES)
  • Experience working on projects that involve the integration of electrical, mechanical, and software/firmware systems.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain US DoD clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Master’s of Science in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science or related field.
  • Familiarity with Python, LabVIEW and/or MATLAB for data parsing and data visualization.
  • Experience with test automation, PCBA design, and mechanical design.
  • Experience with computer hardware communication protocols: USB, Ethernet, RS232, RS485, PCIe, HDMI, CAN, etc.
  • Experience with ESS-related testing (Thermal, Vibration, etc.)
  • Active Security Clearance or ability to obtain one.

ABOUT THE JOB
 
The Technical Program Manager, Mathematical Software and Algorithms is responsible for overseeing the development, execution, and delivery of the Battlespace Awareness software for critical programs - ensuring it meets all technical, functional, and business requirements. Battlespace Awareness software services comprise advanced algorithms for sense-making and decision-making at tactical timelines.  This role requires an individual with a strong technical background in software development, particularly in the domain of optimization and estimation, and experience managing complex projects with multiple sub-teams and many stakeholders. The Sr Technical Program Manager will be the linchpin in ensuring that the software is developed in line with the objectives defined and is released according to the planned schedule.
 
WHAT YOU'LL DO
  • Project Leadership and Strategy:
    • Develop and maintain a detailed project and execution plan - including feature development, testing and validation, deployment, and monitoring. 
    • Establish clear objectives and deliverables for the software that align with program needs.
  • Technical Expertise:
    • Maintain a deep understanding of underlying algorithms and software interfaces for battle management, threat prediction, tracking, and classification to ensure that the relevant services integrate effectively with the larger C2 system.
    • Stay updated on the latest techniques to work with subject matter experts in incorporating relevant innovations into the project plan.
  • Documentation and Process Improvement:
    • Ensure comprehensive documentation is maintained for the project, including technical specifications, user manuals, and project reports.
    • Continuously evaluate and improve project management processes to increase efficiency and effectiveness.
  • Release Management:
    • Oversee the planning and execution of the software release process, ensuring that deployment is carried out smoothly and efficiently.
    • Ensure that all software releases meet the defined quality standards before deployment.
  • Stakeholder Communication:
    • Serve as the primary point of contact for all project-related communications, internally across teams and externally with stakeholders.
    • Regularly update stakeholders on project status, risks, and milestones through reports and presentations.
  • Resource Allocation:
    • Assess and allocate necessary resources, including personnel, software, and hardware, to ensure the project is adequately supported.
    • Monitor resource utilization and make adjustments as needed to avoid bottlenecks or resource constraints.
  • Risk Management:
    • Identify potential risks and develop mitigation strategies with the subject matter experts to minimize impact on the project timeline and deliverables.
    • Regularly review and update the risk management plan to reflect changes in the project landscape.
  • Cross-Functional Collaboration:
    • Work with other divisions and departments to ensure software supports the program priorities and meets all integration requirements.
    • Facilitate effective communication and collaboration between the Battlespace Awareness business line and other stakeholders to promote a unified approach to program execution.
REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS
  • Bachelor's or Master's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field.
  • Extensive project management experience, preferably in software development.
  • Demonstrable understanding of optimization, applied probability, and AI/ML technology.
  • Strong analytical, problem-solving, and decision-making capabilities.
  • Experience with tools like JIRA, Confluence, and GitHub
  • Exceptional verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to manage high-pressure situations and tight deadlines.
  • Must be able to obtain and hold a U.S. security clearance.

PREFERRED QAULIFICATIONS:

  • Familiarity and experience working with materiel leadership or mission partners within Army Air & Missile Defense, USMC Ground Based Air Defense, SOCOM, DHS CBP, or allied defense organizations and working knowledge of the counter-UAS and air surveillance competitive landscape.
  • Experience working on or alongside a team developing mathematical software, such as optimization solvers, estimation engines, simulation frameworks, or applied probability models.

As a key member of Anduril's Talent Acquisition team, you will be responsible for the company's talent management as we continue to rapidly scale and grow. Your work will be hands-on and involve collaborating with Manufacturing leaders to define the hiring needs, influence process improvements and efficiencies, and set a high bar of talent and performance. To achieve this, you will be given the autonomy and tools to execute, build, and develop Anduril's world class team. We are looking for someone who can handle every aspect of recruiting and talent mapping, excited to be part of lean and nimble team on one mission together, where no task is too big or too small.

The Technical Program Manager, Mathematical Software and Algorithms is responsible for overseeing the development, execution, and delivery of the Battlespace Awareness software for critical programs - ensuring it meets all technical, functional, and business requirements.   • Project Leadership and Strategy:

  • Experience with tools like JIRA, Confluence, and GitHub
  • Exceptional verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to manage high-pressure situations and tight deadlines.
  • Must be able to obtain and hold a U.S. security clearance.

  • Familiarity and experience working with materiel leadership or mission partners within Army Air & Missile Defense, USMC Ground Based Air Defense, SOCOM, DHS CBP, or allied defense organizations and working knowledge of the counter-UAS and air surveillance competitive landscape.

ABOUT THE TEAM 

In the Space Special Programs team, we build spacecraft and space systems which serve a wide variety of functions in the space architecture. At a time when space superiority can no longer be taken for granted and with space systems proliferating at an incredible rate, the Space Special Programs team provides advanced, mission critical capabilities to our customer base to be able to more effectively operate and survive within this expanding environment with limited personnel. Working across product, engineering, sales, logistics, operations, and mission success, the Space Special Programs team develops, tests, deploys, and operates new, unique, space capabilities to drive mission success in challenging operational environments. 

ABOUT THE JOB 

We are looking for Software Engineers to join our rapidly growing team in Chantilly, VA. In this role, you will be responsible for implementation of flight software, ground test software, ground station software – at both embedded and application levels. The engineering team as a whole must span the capabilities of deeply embedded software design, implementation, and debugging, including data protocols, RF communication, machine learning, computer vision, and implementing control algorithms in a computationally-restricted environment; host side software for user interfaces, equipment interfaces, machine-to-machine communication, data analysis, display, compression and extraction to human-useable forms; and interfacing with existing Command and Control software and databases to integrate the spacecraft systems in a simple fashion. The embedded tasking will also include writing code to operate at the intersection of hardware, FPGA, and software. 

WHAT YOU’LL DO 

  • Work with a cross-functional team to design market leading space flight hardware and associated ground equipment products 
  • Implement software components through rapid prototyping, design verification, and space qualification activities 
  • Learn and apply modern space-flight software design standards and guidelines (e.g. fault detection and recovery, error checking, data redundancy, etc.) to create high-reliability, highly manufacturable assemblies which can be debugged and safely upgraded on orbit 
  • Implement low- and high-level mission functionality on combinations of high-speed digital, precision analog, RF, and ultra low-power designs 
  • Participate in peer-level and cross-discipline design reviews and collaborate with other SWEs on your team to improve everyone’s capabilities 
  • Understand when to use low level firmware development for bring-up and test and when/how to migrate that code to full-fledged flight code 
  • Root cause investigation data collection and analysis in support of production operations 
  • Work in a fast-paced environment, having to juggle multiple concurrent projects and changing delivery timelines 

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS 

  • Bachelor’s degree in computer science, electrical / computer engineering, or similar engineering or technical field  
  • 2-8 years of professional experience, in software product development (mix of needs for embedded and host side focuses, with versatility in both desired) 
  • For embedded roles: Ability to read and interpret VHDL, and write code in C 
  • For host-side roles: Ability to work with GUI, databases, and a variety of high-level languages 
  • Ability to read and interpret schematics  
  • Familiarity with standard interfaces such as Ethernet, CAN, I2C, SPI, PCIe, MIPI CSI-2, etc 
  • Familiarity with common MCU, CPU, FPGA devices and technologies 
  • Knowledge of modern analog and digital electronics and electronic circuits 
  • Ability to determine manage work assignments based on prioritized direction from management, near-term goals, and day-to-day levels of progress 
  • Experience using cross-platform compilers and toolchains 
  • Excellent communication skills and ability to work effectively with others 
  • Ability to work within our company and team culture and take ownership of the tasks assigned to you 
  • Willing to listen and learn from experts but still speak up when you have ideas 
  • Must be a U.S. Citizen and able to obtain and maintain a U.S. Top Secret security clearance

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril's Air & Missile Defense Radar team develops cutting-edge tracking algorithms and software systems that detect, track, and characterize airborne threats in real-time. Working in small, focused teams, our software engineers design and implement sophisticated tracking solutions that protect lives and critical assets. Our work spans the full spectrum—from developing novel multi-target tracking algorithms to building high-performance distributed systems that process massive amounts of sensor data in milliseconds

We don't just publish papers; we deploy production-grade systems that our government and industry customers depend on for mission-critical operations. If you're passionate about applying mathematics, software engineering, and signal processing to solve complex real-world problems, we want to hear from you.

WHAT YOU WILL DO

  • Design and implement advanced tracking algorithms for novel air and missile threats, including multi-target tracking, track fusion, and discrimination techniques
  • Develop high-performance, real-time software systems that process radar sensor data and maintain tracks on dozens to hundreds of simultaneous targets
  • Build and leverage modeling & simulation environments to validate tracking performance, quantify system capabilities, and identify areas for improvement
  • Collaborate directly with radar engineers and system architects to integrate tracking solutions into end-to-end defense systems
  • Optimize tracking software for performance-critical environments where milliseconds matter
  • Communicate technical concepts and trade-offs to cross-functional teams, program leadership, and customers to drive informed decisions
  • Participate in customer demonstrations and field tests to ensure successful deployment and operational effectiveness

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 0-2 years of relevant experience & Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, Physics, or related technical field (or equivalent experience)
  • Strong programming skills in C++ and Python
  • Solid foundation in mathematics: linear algebra, probability, statistics, and/or differential equations
  • Understanding of software engineering fundamentals: design patterns, testing, version control, and debugging
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Top Secret SCI security clearance

DESIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience with tracking, estimation, or filtering algorithms (Kalman filters, particle filters, multiple hypothesis tracking, etc.)
  • Background in controls, estimation theory, or digital signal processing
  • Familiarity with radar systems or sensor fusion
  • Experience with high-performance computing (multithreading, GPU acceleration, distributed systems)
  • Knowledge of machine learning techniques for classification, clustering, or data association
  • Proficiency with database technologies (SQL, NoSQL, time-series databases)
  • Experience with web development technologies (JavaScript, React, Node.js) for building visualization and analysis tools
  • Familiarity with modeling and simulation tools (MATLAB, Simulink, or custom frameworks)

ABOUT THE ROLE

Anduril’s Space Manufacturing team is seeking a Staff Manufacturing Engineer to join our team. The Space Manufacturing team is responsible for assembly, integration, and test of ground support equipment, PCBA, unit-level, and integrated systems that are vital for our aerospace and defense operations. Your expertise will help ensure that our products meet the highest standards of quality and reliability at Anduril.

As a Staff Manufacturing Engineer on our Space team, you will be a technical leader responsible for owning the manufacturing strategy and execution for complex spacecraft hardware. Your responsibilities the entire manufacturing value-chain, including Design for Manufacturability, advanced manufacturing process development, tooling design & selection, supplier technical management, quality system implementation, and comprehensive work documentation. You will lead a cross-functional initiatives, mentor junior engineers, and drive manufacturing excellence across PCBA, box-level electronics, electro-optical instruments, and integrated spacecraft systems. 

The ideal candidate demonstrates proven leadership in solving complex technical challenges with innovative, practical solutions in fast-paced, resource-constrained environments. You have successfully scaled manufacturing processes from prototype through production and have a track record of delivering high-reliability hardware on aggressive timelines.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

 

  • Lead the development, documentation, and continuous improvement of manufacturing processes for PCBAs, box-level assemblies, electro-optical instruments, and integrated spacecraft systems, ensuring compliance with space-grade standards (IPC-610/620 Class 3, NASA-STD-8739 series)
  • Drive Design for Manufacturability (DFM/DFA) initiatives from concept through production, partnering with design engineers to optimize producibility, yield, and cost while providing hands-on technical leadership to manufacturing technicians
  • Own quality assurance for assigned manufacturing processes, lead root cause analyses (RCA) and corrective actions for non-conformances, and proactively mitigate risks through PFMEA, process validation, and quality planning
  • Specify, qualify, and deploy advanced assembly tools, fixtures, test equipment, and automation solutions, including custom tooling design using CAD/3D modeling capabilities
  • Implement and optimize Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), ERP/MRP workflows, and digital manufacturing tools to enhance traceability, efficiency, and data-driven decision-making
  • Establish and manage technical relationships with suppliers and contract manufacturers, conducting assessments, audits, and qualification activities while driving quality improvements and manufacturability enhancements
  • Lead or participate in design reviews (PDR, CDR), manufacturing readiness reviews (MRR), and production readiness reviews (PRR) for flight hardware programs
  • Collaborate across engineering disciplines (systems, electrical, mechanical, optical, test, quality) and communicate effectively with program management, supply chain, and executive leadership on manufacturing status, risks, and mitigation strategies
  • Analyze production data and lead scaling efforts from low-rate to high-rate production, implementing continuous improvement programs (Lean, Six Sigma) to optimize throughput, reduce cycle times, and enhance product reliability while reducing costs
  • Define manufacturing strategy for spacecraft product lines, mentor and develop junior engineers and technicians, and represent Manufacturing Engineering in cross-functional leadership forums and strategic planning session

 

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS 

 

  • 12+ years of manufacturing engineering experience in aerospace, space systems, aviation, defense, or other high-reliability industries, with a proven track record leading complex manufacturing programs from development through production
  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or related technical discipline required
  • Deep knowledge of aerospace and high-reliability electronics standards, including IPC-610/620 Class 3, IPC J-STD-001 Space Addendum, and NASA-STD-8739 series (soldering, wire harness, conformal coating)
  • Expert-level understanding of PCBA manufacturing processes (SMT, through-hole, conformal coating, potting, component selection/screening) and strong technical knowledge of box-level assembly (cabling, harnessing, mechanical integration, thermal management, EMI/EMC)
  • Hands-on experience implementing and optimizing Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES), ERP/MRP systems (SAP, Oracle, Odoo, Aligni), digital work instructions, and manufacturing process controls (SPC, Lean, Six Sigma)
  • Demonstrated expertise in root cause analysis (8D, 5-Why, Fishbone, PFMEA), driving corrective/preventive actions (CAPA), and developing/executing process validation, first article inspection (FAI), and manufacturing qualification plans
  • Ability to influence design for manufacturability and collaborate with electrical, mechanical, and systems design teams, with experience designing or specifying custom tooling, fixtures, and test equipment for complex assemblies
  • Strong technical communication skills with ability to present to cross-functional teams and executive leadership, and proven ability to lead cross-functional initiatives across engineering, quality, supply chain, and operations
  • Experience mentoring and developing junior engineers and technicians
  • Proven success in fast-paced, startup, or rapid development environments while maintaining meticulous attention to detail and quality, with a hands-on mindset and willingness to work directly on the manufacturing floor alongside technicians
  • Must be eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Top Secret security clearance

 

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 

 

  • Master's degree or equivalent advanced experience
  • Direct experience manufacturing satellites, spacecraft, or space-based instruments (flight hardware), including spacecraft environmental testing (TVAC, vibration, shock, acoustics) and launch site integration support
  • Familiarity with space-grade materials, processes, and workmanship standards such as NASA-STD-8739 series, ECSS standards, and IPC Space Addendum requirements
  • Harness and cable assembly design capability, including schematic reading/drawing using tools like Altium, AutoCAD Electrical, or similar design software
  • Experience with electro-optical or infrared sensor assembly, including optical alignment, cleaning protocols, contamination control, and cleanroom manufacturing practices
  • Knowledge of advanced manufacturing technologies including selective soldering, automated optical inspection (AOI), X-ray inspection, conformal coating systems, and additive manufacturing (3D printing) for tooling or flight hardware
  • Proven track record scaling production from prototype/LRIP to high-rate production (tens to hundreds of units), with experience implementing automation or semi-automation solutions for electronics assembly
  • Lean Manufacturing or Six Sigma certification (Green Belt, Black Belt) with demonstrated project results and continuous improvement achievements
  • Experience managing technical relationships with PCBA suppliers, cable/harness vendors, and contract manufacturers, including supplier audits, qualification activities, and AS9100
  • Proficiency with CAD/3D modeling software (NX Design, SolidWorks, CREO, Fusion 360) and scripting tools (Python, MATLAB) for tooling design, DFM reviews, and data analysis
  • Experience leading multi-disciplinary manufacturing programs with P&L or budget authority and recognized subject matter expertise in spacecraft manufacturing or high-reliability electronics
  • Active Top Secret or TS/SCI clearance is a significant plus

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

The mission of Anduril’s Air Dominance and Strike Division is to fundamentally reshape the way future peer to peer conflicts are fought by developing next generation collaborative combat aircraft, advanced effects, and the software that powers these autonomous weapons. Facilities - both office space and industrial space - can limit how fast we can grow. As programs ramp, we need to make decisions about where they can grow in our existing infrastructure. Looking further our - three to five years plus, we must make strategic big bets on real estate to enable our growth. As our supply chain and manufacturing process complexifies across AD&S, we need our real estate footprint to respond. As Strategic Planning Lead, you will own the answer to “how much space does AD&S need, of what type, and where?”

Key Responsibilities

  • Optimize supply, demand of our current real estate portfolio:
    • Establish Process and Structure. Define the requirements and process for raising space requests, vetting such requests, and ensuring AD&S space demand data is accurate, up-to-date, and can be trusted.
    • Pressure Test Demand. Challenge every request against headcount plans, program schedules, and production ramps. Know each program's status, product, and what it needs at each stage (engineering and lab space early, integration and test mid-stage, production at ramp) well enough to tell a firm need from a wish, and to advise program teams on what to ask for and when. Keep a record of how demand changes.
    • Match Demand to Supply. Size gaps against current and committed space by site and timeframe, and work with corporate Space Planning and Strategic Real Estate to close them: reassign programs, densify, expand sites, or add a building. Be the directly responsible person for making sure each program that needs space has it, or knows when and where it will be available.
    • Sequence the Moves. Build and own the plan for who goes where, and when. Account for classified and unclassified infrastructure, power and utilities, lab and production ramps, dependencies between moves, and construction and IT lead times. Re-plan quickly when a program slips or a ramp accelerates.
  • Create and execute longer-term real estate strategy:
    • Capital Investment. Own the three to five year model of where AD&S is going and growing, work with the corporate RE&F teams to justify these large scale infrastructure investments for the division across office space, industrial space, classified test sites, integrated suppliers and everything in between.
    • ‘Build Where’ Strategy. Work with production and engineering teams to strategize longer-term ‘build-where’ model for more complex hardware integration. It must consider current and future facility capabilities and limitations, type of talent in various geographies, and overall logistics and cost optimization.
    • Scenario Modeling. Model near-term scenarios (program slips, ramp changes, wins and losses, new sites) and their effect on space and cost, so the plan can be redone quickly when something moves.

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience
  • 6-10 years of experience in corporate real estate, facilities, strategy, business operations, program or operations management, or FP&A / capacity planning, with a clear interest in real estate and facilities and a record of enabling growth. Some experience leading or mentoring analysts/associates
  • Ability to see the big picture, apply it to day-to-day decisions, and do whatever the work requires, from strategic planning to boots-on-the-ground tasks
  • Ability to learn a program quickly (its product, schedule, and stage) and form a view on what space it needs and when. Some fluency in engineering and production processes preferred
  • High agency and low ego: you've taken an ambiguous problem with no playbook, owned it, and driven it to a decision
  • Excellent communication, with a demonstrated capacity to influence cross-functional teams and senior executives you don't report to
  • Ability to travel up to 10% for site visits and stakeholder meetings
  • Must be eligible to hold a US Top Secret clearance

Preferred Skills

  • Experience planning space through a manufacturing or R&D ramp, including forecasting from incomplete data and knowing what each stage of a hardware program needs from a facility
  • Experience sequencing moves or builds with many dependencies, including classified or secure space
  • Strong analytical modeling in Excel and Python or SQL, and hands-on use of LLMs and modern data platforms (Palantir Foundry or similar)

ABOUT THE JOB

Rendezvous and proximity operations are where spacecraft operations stop being a checklist and start
being a craft. You own that craft at Anduril. As a Spacecraft Operations Systems Engineer for RPO, you own how our spacecraft plan, rehearse, and
fly close to other objects.

You'll do this work well before launch. RPO campaigns are won in AI&T, on the flatsat, and in the
rehearsals, not just on-console. You'll validate procedures against hardware-in-the-loop testbeds, build
and run day-in-the-life and contingency sims, and push ops constraints back into the GNC, flight
software, and ground software designs while those designs can still change.
This role is directly tied to ongoing programs within Anduril's Space Business Line. We work with mission
partners and customers to deploy reliable and robust capabilities on operationally-relevant fielding
timelines to meet complex challenges across the DoD and IC.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Design and own RPO mission plans: relative motion design, approach and hold-point
    sequencing, delta-V budgets, and the timeline that ties them to comm passes, lighting, and
    ground contact
  • Build passive safety into every approach, so that a missed burn, a dropped pass, or an off-
    nominal state doesn't put the vehicle on a collision trajectory
  • Author the flight rules and procedures that govern close approach: keep-out volume
    enforcement, go/no-go gates, abort and breakout criteria, custody handoffs, and conjunction
    screening against both the target and third parties
  • Own the mission operations plans and procedures for spacecraft programs across all phases,
    including LEOP, commissioning, on-orbit checkout, and operations
  • Drive the pre-launch campaign from the ops side: write and run day-in-the-life and mission
    rehearsals, inject the failures, and turn every finding into a procedure change or a design change
  • Work with AI&T as the operations voice, validating procedures and command sequences on
    flatsats and hardware-in-the-loop testbeds before they touch flight hardware
  • Feed operational constraints back into GNC, flight software, ground software, and comms
    design
  • Create and analyze the metrics used to debug and monitor vehicle and campaign performance
  • Triage anomalies, root cause failures, and coordinate next steps under time pressure
  • Train operators and mission crews on Anduril spacecraft and on RPO execution specifically
  • Support demanding schedules during ground testing, launch windows, and on-orbit operations
  • Work with other teams and government agencies to obtain required licenses (FCC, NOAA) and
    comply with regulations for operating spacecraft, including proximity operations coordination

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Top Secret security clearance
  • Strong engineering background from industry or school, ideally in Aerospace Engineering,
    Astrodynamics, Computer Science, or another engineering field
  • 4+ years of professional spacecraft operations, mission planning, or flight dynamics experience
  • Direct RPO experience on a flown or near-flight mission, on either the planning or execution
    side: relative orbit design, proximity operations trajectory planning, maneuver planning and
    reconstruction, or close-approach execution on console
  • Experience taking a spacecraft through pre-launch operational readiness: AI&T support,
    procedure validation, mission rehearsals, day-in-the-life testing, and operational readiness
    reviews
  • Ability to quickly understand and navigate complex systems and detailed requirements
  • Capable of solving complex technical problems with little oversight
  • Clear written communication, including procedures, flight rules, and training material

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience on on-orbit servicing, inspection, docking, or refueling missions
  • Experience with autonomous or onboard relative navigation, including vision-based or optical
    relative nav
  • Flight dynamics depth: orbit determination, maneuver calibration, and maneuver reconstruction
  • Experience with conjunction assessment and space traffic coordination
  • Experience operating government, DoD, or IC spacecraft
  • Experience with STK/Astrogator, ODTK, MATLAB, or Simulink
  • Experience with Python and Linux systems
  • Experience with testing and validation on flatsats and hardware-in-the-loop testbeds
  • Exposure to ground station operations and providers
  • A desire to work on critical software in the space domain

  • Participate in peer-level and cross-discipline design reviews and help develop customer-facing system design documentation and presentations

This is a highly cross-functional individual contributor role with no people-management responsibility. It is built for someone who combines strategic judgment with hands-on execution: a curious storyteller who builds strong relationships, moves quickly, and turns ideas into finished work.

In this role, you will:

  • 10+ years of experience across partner marketing, product marketing, customer marketing, content marketing, communications, or related B2B technology marketing roles.

  • Exceptional storytelling and editorial judgment, with the ability to absorb substantial information quickly and turn it into a coherent narrative, strategy, and message.

  • Experience building customer reference or storytelling programs, including developing case studies, whitepapers, webinars, and thought leadership grounded in credible customer outcomes.

  • Strong business judgment and a track record of choosing marketing investments based on customer relevance, pipeline potential, adoption, and commercial impact.

  • A hands-on approach to execution. You are comfortable conducting interviews, drafting content, developing messaging, coordinating approvals, and getting work published.

About the Team

OpenAI's Safety Research organization works to ensure that our most capable AI models can be deployed safely and responsibly. As frontier models become increasingly capable and autonomous, developing reliable ways to monitor their behavior, identify emerging risks, and evaluate the effectiveness of safety systems becomes increasingly important.

Our work focuses on advancing the research and evaluation methods needed to understand model behavior and ensure that monitoring systems remain effective as model capabilities evolve. We combine rigorous empirical research with practical safety interventions, working closely with research, engineering, and deployment teams to translate findings into improvements across OpenAI's models and products.

About the Role

We are looking for a senior researcher to lead technical work on misalignment monitoring for frontier AI systems. You will develop methods to evaluate the effectiveness of AI monitors, understand their limitations, and improve our ability to detect and stop concerning model behavior reliably.

This role combines research leadership with hands-on technical execution. You will set research priorities, design rigorous evaluations, investigate monitoring failures, and develop approaches for stress-testing and improving monitoring systems. A key focus will be understanding where monitors produce false positives, miss important behaviors, or become less effective as models grow more capable.

You will work closely with researchers and engineers across OpenAI to turn monitoring research into practical improvements to our safety systems. We are looking for someone with strong research judgment, technical depth, and the ability to independently drive ambiguous problems from initial investigation through measurable results.

In this role, you will:

  • Lead the research and technical direction for evaluating and improving the misalignment monitoring of frontier AI systems.

  • Design and execute rigorous evaluations that measure monitor effectiveness, identify failure modes, and assess the reliability of monitoring signals.

  • Develop methods to stress-test and red-team monitors, including identifying behaviors that evade detection or expose weaknesses in existing approaches.

  • Investigate false positives, missed detections, and other monitoring failures to improve the accuracy and usefulness of safety evaluations.

  • Build scalable evaluation frameworks and experimental tools that enable ongoing measurement of monitoring performance as model capabilities evolve.

  • Translate research findings into actionable improvements, working with partner teams to strengthen monitoring systems and inform broader safety decisions.

  • Establish research priorities and guide technical execution, balancing foundational research questions with practical deployment needs.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have a strong background in machine learning research, particularly in model evaluations, AI safety, alignment, robustness, or related areas.

  • Have demonstrated the ability to lead technically challenging research projects, from identifying important questions through designing experiments and delivering results.

  • Bring strong experimental judgment and understand how to design evaluations that are rigorous, reproducible, and difficult to game.

  • Have hands-on experience building or evaluating machine learning systems, including working with large language models or other frontier AI systems.

  • Enjoy investigating complex failure modes and developing methods to distinguish meaningful safety signals from misleading measurements.

  • Are comfortable working on open-ended research problems where the right methodology or success criteria may not be obvious at the outset.

  • Combine strong research instincts with practical engineering ability and can independently build experiments, analyze results, and iterate quickly.

  • Communicate technical findings clearly and enjoy collaborating across research, engineering, and safety teams.

  • Are motivated by OpenAI's mission and the challenge of developing reliable oversight mechanisms for increasingly capable AI systems.

Nice to have:

  • Experience with AI monitoring, automated evaluations, adversarial testing, or red-teaming.

  • Research experience in scalable oversight, AI control, model behavior analysis, or interpretability.

  • Experience developing monitoring or evaluation systems that are used in real-world deployments.

  • A track record of technical research leadership, including mentoring researchers or coordinating cross-functional research initiatives.

You will work with customers, platform engineering, and forward deployed teams to build capabilities customers need, productize work developed in the field when it has broader value, and improve how teams build, deploy, and operate AI applications.

What you'll do

  • Own the platform strategy and roadmap. Prioritize across developer experience, capabilities customers need, and productizing work built in the field where it has broader value. Sequence investments against customer value, commitments, and dependencies.
  • Define how the product should work. Work with users and engineers to write clear requirements and vibe code prototypes, user journeys, and measure success through customer outcomes, capability adoption, delivery time, and production performance, and follow through on gaps after launch.
  • Align teams across the business. Work with platform engineering, forward deployed PMs, and business leaders to agree on shared capabilities, rollout priorities, and necessary differences across environments. Make clear what is available, where it works, and what remains to be delivered.
  • Build and lead a strong PM team. Establish clear ownership across related product areas, hire and coach PMs, and raise the quality of product thinking and written requirements. Stay directly involved in the most consequential decisions.

What we're looking for

  • A track record of owning platform, infrastructure, or developer products from problem definition through launch and sustained production use.
  • Experience managing and developing product managers, setting direction across multiple related product areas, and remaining hands-on with important product decisions.
  • Strong product judgment. You can explain which problems you chose to solve, what you decided against, how you sequenced the work, and what changed for users as a result.
  • Technical depth to work credibly with engineers on APIs, runtime behavior, identity and authorization, deployment, observability, and data isolation. You can reason through architectural tradeoffs and their consequences for users, security, and operations.
  • Experience driving adoption across teams with different needs and constraints. You can reach decisions, establish ownership, and follow through when progress depends on people outside your reporting line.
  • Clear, precise writing and communication. You can turn an ambiguous problem into requirements engineers can act on and explain priorities and tradeoffs to customers and executives.

Nice-to-Haves

  • Experience with AI platforms, including agent runtimes, workflow orchestration, evaluation, datasets, human review, or production AI observability.
  • Experience building products for regulated industries or deploying into on-premises, air-gapped, or classified environments.
  • Experience turning capabilities developed for individual customers into reusable platform products.

As the world adjusts to this new reality, leading platform companies are scrambling to build LLMs at billion scale, while large enterprises figure out how to add it to their products. To make them safe, aligned and actually useful, these models need human eval and reinforcement learning through human feedback (RLHF) during pre-training, fine-tuning, and production evaluations. This is the main innovation that’s enabled ChatGPT to get such a large headstart among competition.

At Scale, our products include the Generative AI Data Engine, SGP, Donovan, and others that power the most advanced LLMs and generative models in the world through world-class RLHF, human data generation, model evaluation, safety, and alignment. The data we are producing is some of the most important work for how humanity will interact with AI.

At the foundation of these products is the Platform Engineering team. In this role, you will support the design and development of shared platforms used across Scale. This includes designing our foundational data platforms and lifecycle, architecting Scale’s core cloud infrastructure and orchestration stack, and redefining how engineers develop, build, test, and deploy software at Scale. You’ll also get widespread exposure to the forefront of the AI race as Scale sees it in enterprises, startups, governments, and large tech companies.

You will:

  • Drive the design, and implementation of our foundational platforms and systems, working closely with stakeholders and internal customers to understand and refine requirements.

  • Presenting technical information to teams and stakeholders, providing guidance and insight on development processes and technologies.

  • Show a track record of independent ownership of successful engineering projects.
  • Possess excellent communication and collaboration skills, and the ability to translate complex technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders.
  • Experience working fluently with standard containerization & deployment technologies like Kubernetes, Terraform, Docker, etc.
  • Experience with orchestration platforms, such as Temporal and AWS Step Functions.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

We are seeking a hands-on, safety-focused Megapack Field Technician to support the operation, maintenance, and expansion of our Megapack energy storage fleet powering SpaceXSI's AI infrastructure in Memphis. Working directly with the Energy Storage Asset Manager, you will own the low-voltage side of the fleet, support daily medium-voltage switching operations, and help manage construction and commissioning across multiple sites for one of the largest and most critical battery deployments powering AI training.

This is a full-time, onsite role based in Memphis, Tennessee, with regular travel between Memphis-area sites.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Own the low-voltage (LV) side of the Megapack fleet, including AC and DC LV systems, 480V auxiliary power, breakers, and LV terminations.
  • Perform Megapack enable/disable, isolation, and return-to-service procedures in support of maintenance, switching, and construction activities.
  • Troubleshoot Megapack-side faults and alarms in the field, gather logs, data, and photos, and drive issues to resolution with OEM field service and support engineering.
  • Act as an onsite point of contact for Tesla Field Service technicians, coordinating access, isolations, and work scope to remove blockers and ensure high-quality, timely completion of work.
  • Support execution of the daily medium-voltage (MV) switching plan, including de-energizing and re-energizing Megapack strings in coordination with MV electricians, testing contractors, and site operations.
  • Perform and verify lockout/tagout (LOTO) and maintain switching and isolation records in accordance with site safety procedures.
  • Provide day-to-day oversight of electrical and civil contractors, verifying work against drawings, specifications, and schedule.
  • Perform quality checks on LV and MV terminations, installations, and repairs, and document findings for correction and closeout.
  • Coordinate installation and commissioning activities for new Megapack deployments and their integration with SpaceXSI facilities.
  • Build, track, and close out punch lists, performing field verification before items are closed.
  • Use drawings, single-line diagrams, and project management platforms (e.g., Procore) to track RFIs, submittals, and site issues.
  • Support transformer issue intake and documentation, and assist with dehumidification and environmental controls during outages and construction.
  • Conduct routine site walks and inspections to identify safety, reliability, and serviceability issues before they impact operations.
  • Maintain accurate records of field work, switching activity, service events, and equipment status.
  • Ensure full compliance with all safety protocols, NFPA 70E requirements, manufacturer guidelines, and local regulations.
  • Provide on-call support for urgent operational and maintenance issues as required.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 3+ years of field service, commissioning, or maintenance experience on utility-scale battery energy storage systems (BESS) or comparable power infrastructure.
  • Hands-on experience with low-voltage AC/DC electrical systems, breakers, and terminations, including safe isolation and verification of energy states.
  • Working knowledge of NFPA 70E, arc flash safety, and lockout/tagout procedures.
  • Ability to read and work from electrical drawings, single-line diagrams, and equipment documentation.
  • Strong communication and organizational skills with the ability to coordinate multiple contractors and vendors in the field.
  • Comfortable working onsite in an industrial/data center and active construction environment.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Utility-scale BESS field service experience (Megapack preferred), including Megapack 2 / 2XL installation, commissioning, service, and troubleshooting.
  • Experience with OEM service and diagnostic tools, firmware updates, and site controller workflows.
  • Experience supporting medium-voltage switching operations, string energization, or utility/data center switching programs.
  • Construction management or field engineering experience, including contractor oversight, QA/QC, punch lists, and Procore or similar platforms.
  • Familiarity with pad-mount transformers, medium-voltage cable and terminations, and fire protection standards for energy storage.
  • Previous experience in 24/7 operational environments with on-call responsibilities.

ADDITIONAL REQUIREMENTS:

  • Position is subject to pre-employment and annual post-employment background checks.
  • Comfortable working in an environment requiring exposure to noise, outdoor weather, and industrial conditions.
  • Available to work evenings, weekends, and provide on-call support as needed for urgent operational issues and planned outages.
  • Ability to lift 50+ pounds, climb, and work at heights and in confined spaces as required.
  • Valid driver's license and ability to travel between Memphis-area sites.

We are seeking an experienced and strategic Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) team member to help scale our GRC program as SpaceXSI grows. This critical role will ensure that SpaceXSI operates within regulatory, ethical, and operational boundaries while fostering a culture of integrity and resilience.

The primary focus of this role is to provide and sustain deep expertise in the NIST Risk Management Framework (RMF), FedRAMP, and Impact Level 4/5 (IL4/IL5) authorization processes. The ideal candidate will apply these frameworks end-to-end through the full authorization and certification lifecycle, with a strong command of the underlying technical implementation. RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Oversee audits, certifications, third-party assessments, and vulnerability management to maintain compliance and operational credibility.
  • Design and implement risk mitigation strategies, including monitoring systems, contingency plans, vulnerability scans, Plan of Action and Milestones (POAMs), and STIGs.
  • Ensure the implementation, oversight, monitoring, and maintenance of security configurations, practices, and procedures throughout the project lifecycle.
  • Serve as a liaison between system owners, security personnel, and cross-functional teams to facilitate effective communication, collaboration, and control implementation.
  • Lead Risk Management Assessment and Authorization (A&A) processes, cloud system risk assessments, compliance reviews for new products/changes/features, and process enhancements.
  • Conduct regular risk assessments, scenario analyses, and proactive evaluations of emerging threats, certifications, requirements, and technologies in the AI landscape.
  • Act as a subject matter expert, providing guidance on risk, compliance, and cybersecurity matters; translate business and technical risks for leadership.
  • Create and present regular reports on GRC performance, risks, and compliance status to senior leadership and stakeholders.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor's degree in computer science, Information Security, Cybersecurity, or in an engineering/STEM field
  • 3+ years of experience in governance, risk management, compliance, or technology audit roles.
  • At least 1 year of experience with FedRAMP/IL5 compliance, vulnerability management, and continuous monitoring.
  • Experience implementing and maintaining security compliance frameworks and cloud security controls.
  • Expert-level knowledge in at least one of the following domains: DoD Cloud Computing SRG IL5/IL6, FedRAMP Class D. and/or NIST 800-171/CMMC.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • 5+ years of security compliance or technology audit-related experience.
  • Active Top Secret (TS) clearance preferred.
  • Hands-on experience implementing technical controls (e.g., IAM, logging and monitoring, encryption, infrastructure hardening) and integrating compliance checks into CI/CD pipelines.
  • Exceptional analytical, problem-solving, organizational, and project management skills, with the ability to balance innovation, oversight, and taking projects from conception to launch.
  • Ability to evaluate control objectives with IT configurations.
  • Hands-on experience implementing technical controls (e.g., IAM, logging and monitoring, encryption, infrastructure hardening) — not just assessing them.
  • Experience in the tech or AI industry, particularly with startups or innovative organizations.
  • Experience with CI/CD pipelines and DevSecOps practices, including implementing compliance-as-code (e.g., policy-as-code frameworks like OPA, automated control validation, continuous compliance monitoring integrated into the deployment pipeline).
  • Excellent communication, stakeholder management, and translation skills, with experience influencing cross-functional teams and communicating risks to leadership.
  • Experience with commercial compliance programs (e.g., ISO 27001, ISO 42001, SOC 2, NIST CSF, NIST 800-53, or similar compliance framework is a plus.

Job Description:

The Compensation Director, Aircraft Engineering and Manufacturing, serves as the strategic compensation leader for the Aircraft division, providing enterprise-level oversight for compensation programs supporting manufacturing, production, operations, supply chain, logistics, customer success, and skilled trades. This role defines compensation strategy for large, complex employee populations while ensuring programs are competitive, scalable, compliant, and aligned with business objectives. 

As the organization's subject matter expert for manufacturing and operations compensation, the Director partners closely with business leaders, Px Business Partners, Finance, and Legal to design compensation programs that enable business growth, talent attraction, workforce scalability, and operational excellence. 

The ideal candidate brings deep expertise in manufacturing compensation strategy, non-exempt workforce design, market intelligence, and executive consulting, with a demonstrated ability to influence enterprise decisions and build compensation frameworks that support rapidly growing operations. 

What you'll do:

    Compensation Strategy & Enterprise Leadership 
  • Develop and lead the compensation strategy supporting Aircraft manufacturing, production, operations, supply chain, logistics, customer success, and skilled trades populations.  
  • Serve as the SME on manufacturing and operations compensation, shaping long-term compensation philosophy and governance.  
  • Partner with business leadership to align compensation strategy with business growth, workforce planning, organizational design, and operational priorities.  
  • Drive compensation initiatives supporting facility expansions, new business models, geographic growth, and workforce transformation.  
    • Manufacturing & Operations Compensation 
  • Lead the design and evolution of compensation structures supporting large non-exempt employee populations.  
  • Establish wage structures, geographic differentials, shift premium strategies, progression frameworks, and other compensation programs that balance external competitiveness with internal equity.  
  • Oversee market pricing methodologies utilizing Radford, Mercer, WTW, and specialized manufacturing compensation surveys alongside complementary market intelligence.  
  • Develop innovative compensation approaches to attract and retain highly competitive manufacturing, technical, and operational talent. 
    • Executive Partnership & Business Consulting 
  • Serve as the trusted compensation advisor to Aircraft executives and business leaders.  
  • Consult on organization design, workforce investments, location strategy, and talent acquisition decisions with significant financial and organizational impact in partnership with the Px Business Partner.  
  • Provide strategic guidance on compensation implications of organizational changes, acquisitions, new facilities, and business expansion.  
  • Present compensation recommendations and analyses to executive leadership with clear business rationale and risk assessments.  
    • Compensation Analytics & Insights 
  • Lead enterprise compensation analyses including market competitiveness, pay equity, workforce cost modeling, and incentive effectiveness.  
  • Translate complex compensation data into actionable insights for executive stakeholders.  
  • Anticipate market trends and proactively recommend compensation strategies that strengthen organizational competitiveness.  
    • Governance, Compliance & Program Excellence 
  • Establish governance frameworks, policies, and administration standards for manufacturing compensation programs.  
  • Ensure compliance with federal, state, and local wage and hour regulations while mitigating organizational risk.  
  • Partner with Legal, Finance, and People Operations on complex compensation matters and regulatory changes.  
  • Lead continuous improvement initiatives to simplify compensation processes, improve scalability, and enhance operational efficiency. 
    • Leadership 
  • Champion best practices in compensation design, analytics, governance, and operational excellence.  
  • Build organizational capability through knowledge sharing, coaching, and development of compensation expertise across the People function. 

Required qualifications:

  • Bachelor's degree in Human Resources, Finance, Business, Economics, or a related field.  
  • 15+ years of progressive compensation experience, including significant leadership supporting manufacturing, production, operations, or supply chain organizations.  
  • Deep expertise designing enterprise compensation strategies for large non-exempt employee populations.  
  • Extensive knowledge of wage and hour regulations, compensation governance, and manufacturing compensation practices.
  • Demonstrated experience designing wage structures, progression frameworks, geographic differentials, and premium pay programs.  
  • Advanced analytical, financial modeling, and executive presentation skills.  
  • Proven ability to influence senior executives and drive enterprise-wide compensation decisions.  
  • Experience leading large, cross-functional compensation initiatives with significant organizational impact. 

Preferred qualifications:

  • Certified Compensation Professional (CCP).  
  • Experience supporting both union and non-union manufacturing environments.  
  • Experience within global manufacturing or advanced technology organizations.  
  • Expertise utilizing Radford, Mercer, WTW, and specialized manufacturing compensation surveys.  
  • Experience with Workday, SAP SuccessFactors, or enterprise compensation planning systems.  
  • Lean, Six Sigma, or continuous improvement experience. 
  • Experience leading or mentoring compensation professionals.
