ABOUT THE TEAM 

The Space Ground Systems Engineering team solves the mathematical, physical, and algorithmic problems at the core of next-generation missile defense and fire control systems. We tackle dynamic battle-management challenges: fusing real-time sensor streams into track data, optimizing weapon-target assignment under uncertainty, and feeding high-confidence fire-control schedules back to the warfighter. 

ABOUT THE JOB 

We are looking for a Systems Engineer - Machine Learning to join our rapidly growing team in Huntsville, AL or Colorado Springs, CO. In this role, you will be responsible for bridging systems engineering, applied physics, and mathematical and machine learning to solve complex missile defense problems. You will design track-fusion pipelines, build threat-assignment algorithms, and conduct deep sensitivity analyses across complex architectures. This will require proficiency in applied math, physics, and algorithm development using Python or C++, alongside an understanding of sensor data and battle management workflows. If you are someone who moves quickly, loves diving deep into the math behind the system, and can operate autonomously to deliver verified, defensible technical solutions, then this role is for you.

WHAT YOU’LL DO 

  • Machine Learning: Research, develop, and deploy complex machine learning models such as generative ai, reinforcement learning, deep neural networks, physics based neural models.
  • Algorithm Design and Development: Formulate and solve complex physics problems using mathematical techniques.
    • Ex: Object detection, tracking, and discrimination.  Weapon-Target Assignment (WTA), sensor allocation, and fire control scheduling.
  • Sensor Fusion & Tracking: Work on the components of system architecture that ingest raw/processed sensor data, execute track fusion, and perform threat classification.
  • Parametric & Sensitivity Analysis: Design, conduct, and defend rigorous trade studies, sensitivity analyses, and parametric evaluations to determine system boundaries and validate performance.
  • Prototyping & Modeling: Rapidly translate mathematical equations into clean, functional code (Python / C++) to run non-customer-facing modeling, simulation, and algorithm verification.
  • Mission Systems Architecture: Bridge the gap between low-level physics/threat intelligence inputs and high-level mission outputs.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Currently possesses and is able to maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance
  • Experience: 5+ years of relevant engineering experience
  • Bachelor’s, Master’s, or Ph.D. in Aerospace Engineering, Applied Mathematics, Physics, Electrical Engineering, Machine Learning, Artificial Intelligence, or a related quantitative field.
  • Core Foundation: Strong mastery of applied mathematics, physics, and programming.
  • Algorithmic Programming: Proficiency in Python and/or C++, Pytorch (or TensorFlow), Coding GPU's, multi-agent reinforcement learning, mathematical modeling, experience implementing foundation models, and algorithm development (you don’t need to be an enterprise software engineer, but you must be able to write robust code to solve math problems).
    • Windows, Linux, MATLAB, 
  • Domain Knowledge: Exposure to missile defense concepts, radar/sensor processing, flight dynamics, TOM, threat intelligence, discrimination algorithms, sensor tracking algorithms, kill assessment, integrated algorithms into operational systems, or fire control systems (GMD, NGI, SM3, Aegis, IBCS, C2BMC, SBI)
    • Military or defense operations experience is a strong plus.
  • Security Clearance: Active U.S. Secret clearance required

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Top Secret / SCI eligible preferred.

About the role

We are looking for a versatile corporate and regulatory lawyer to join Cohere’s Legal team. Reporting to our Senior Governance Counsel, this role will support a global portfolio of corporate governance, entity and intercompany matters, together with cross-border regulatory, trade and compliance workstreams.

This role is designed for a lawyer with a strong corporate foundation who has also developed meaningful regulatory and trade experience. You should be comfortable moving between different types of legal work including:

  • supporting global corporate governance and entity matters, including subsidiary governance, entity establishment and restructuring, intercompany arrangements and delegated authorities;

  • supporting cross-border regulatory workstreams, including foreign investment and national-security reviews, regulatory diligence and filing coordination;

  • helping the business navigate export-control, sanctions and related compliance requirements; and

  • supporting legal and regulatory issues arising from public-sector and regulated-market opportunities, particularly where sovereignty, procurement, security or other market-access requirements come into play.

You will work closely with colleagues across Legal, Finance, Tax, People, Security, Government Affairs and commercial teams, as well as with specialist external counsel in multiple jurisdictions. The role requires sound judgment, curiosity and the ability to take ownership of a workstream, identify when specialist advice is needed, and turn that advice into practical action.

What you’ll do

  • Support Cohere’s global corporate governance and entity matters, including subsidiary governance, entity establishment and restructuring, board and shareholder matters, corporate approvals, delegated authorities, signing frameworks and ongoing entity maintenance.

  • Support Cohere’s intercompany legal architecture, including intercompany agreements and other cross-border operating arrangements, working closely with Finance, Tax, People and local counsel to ensure Cohere’s entities are structured and operated appropriately across jurisdictions.

  • Support cross-border regulatory workstreams, including foreign investment screening, national-security reviews, regulatory diligence, filing coordination and the implementation of regulatory commitments arising in connection with acquisitions, investments, restructurings and other significant matters.

  • Support Cohere’s export-control, sanctions and related compliance matters, including coordinating specialist external advice and translating regulatory requirements into practical internal guidance, controls and documentation.

  • Support legal and regulatory workstreams arising from public-sector and regulated-market opportunities, particularly where sovereignty, procurement, security or other market-access requirements need to be understood and operationalised.

  • Coordinate internal stakeholders and external counsel across jurisdictions, ensuring that legal and regulatory workstreams are appropriately scoped, progressed and implemented.

  • Take ownership of matters within the role’s remit and help develop practical, scalable approaches as Cohere’s international footprint grows.

What we’re looking for

  • A qualified lawyer with approximately 4–8 years of relevant experience, gained at a leading law firm, a sophisticated in-house legal team, or preferably a combination of both.

  • A strong corporate and cross-border legal foundation, with experience across areas such as subsidiary governance, entity structuring and reorganisations, intercompany arrangements, delegated authorities, corporate approvals and other aspects of international corporate practice.

  • Meaningful exposure to cross-border regulatory matters, particularly foreign investment screening, national-security reviews, export controls, sanctions, international trade or related corporate compliance issues. Deep specialism in any one of these areas is not required.

  • Experience working across multiple jurisdictions, including coordinating local and specialist external counsel and bringing different legal, regulatory and business inputs together into a coherent internal position.

  • Strong judgment, range and commercial awareness, with the ability to get quickly up to speed on unfamiliar issues, identify what matters most and distinguish issues that can be handled internally from those requiring specialist advice.

  • The ability to take ownership of an internal legal workstream, ask the right questions of specialist counsel, digest complex advice and translate it into clear, practical next steps for the business.

  • Clear and practical communication skills, including the ability to work effectively with stakeholders across Legal, Finance, Tax, People, Security, Government Affairs and commercial teams.

  • A collaborative and pragmatic approach, with comfort moving between different subject areas and working across functions, jurisdictions and time zones.

  • Experience in technology, AI or another regulated industry would be helpful, but is not essential.

  • Exposure to public-sector, government-facing or regulated-market matters is a plus but is not a prerequisite.

Nice to have

  • Experience in technology, AI, cloud or infrastructure, or another regulated industry.

  • Experience supporting a multinational organisation with a growing international entity footprint, particularly where legal, tax, finance and operational considerations intersect.

  • Exposure to public-sector, government-facing or regulated-market matters, including procurement, digital sovereignty, security, accreditation or related market-access requirements.

  • Familiarity with North American, UK or EU regulatory frameworks relevant to cross-border technology businesses.

What success looks like

  • You can move comfortably between corporate and regulatory matters, identify the core issue quickly and make progress even where the work does not fit neatly into a single legal category.

  • You can take ownership of a complex cross-border workstream, bring together the right internal stakeholders and external advisers, and drive it through to a practical outcome.

  • You know when specialist advice is needed, can frame the right questions for external counsel, and can turn complex advice into clear, actionable guidance for the business.

  • You become a trusted execution partner across Cohere’s corporate governance and regulatory portfolio, taking meaningful ownership of workstreams and creating capacity for more strategic, cross-functional and government-facing work at the senior level.

  • A weekly lunch stipend of $75/£75 or equivalent in your local currency for lunch.

  • Full health and dental benefits, including a separate budget for mental health.

  • RRSP matching, 401K, Pension Scheme.

  • 100% Parental Leave top-up for up to 6 months, for either parent.

  • Annual enrichment benefits:

    Arts & culture, fitness/wellness, quality time, and a workspace improvement credit.

    Education & learning stipend for conferences, courses, and coaching.

  • 6 weeks of paid vacation (30 working days!)

  • Budget for traveling to other offices if you are remote, plus an annual company offsite.

How and Where We Work:

  • Cohere is remote-friendly, but we also have offices in Toronto, London, New York City, San Francisco, Montreal, Paris, Berlin and Seoul with more opening soon.

  • For those in the office: a daily lunch program, plenty of snacks, and regular community and social events.

  • For those not near an office: a co-working benefit so you can work alongside others in your city.

  • Everyone receives a $500 home office stipend to set up your workspace properly.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Air Dominance and Strike Low Observables Team are advancing into the next generation of LO Technology to enhance the survivability and effectiveness of unmanned air systems. Our Low Observables engineering team is responsible for designing, analyzing, testing, and sustaining stealth features that reduce radar (RCS) and infrared (IR) signatures, ensuring our systems remain undetectable in contested environments.

ABOUT THE ROLE

This is an early career role open to engineers with a degree in aerospace, electrical, or mechanical engineering. Low Observables work sits at the intersection of all three: the shape of the air vehicle, the electromagnetic behavior of its surfaces, and the materials and processes used to build it.

You do not need prior stealth experience. Almost nobody arrives with it, because most of it cannot be taught outside a cleared program. We will teach you the LO-specific methods. What we are looking for is strong engineering fundamentals, comfort picking up unfamiliar analysis tools, and the judgment to tell a real result from a bad one.

You will be paired with an LO engineer and start on a scoped piece of a live program, not a training exercise.

WHAT YOU'LL DO:

  • Run broadband Radar Cross Section (RCS) analysis on components and full air vehicles, and learn to judge when a prediction can be trusted
  • Support the design and development of Low Observable unmanned air systems, from early configuration trades through detailed design
  • Build and improve the analysis tools, scripts, and validation workflows the team runs on
  • Model LO materials and treatments, and help select and optimize them for specific components
  • Support manufacturing and validation planning, including tolerances, inspection methods, and what is actually producible at rate
  • Help plan and execute RCS measurement campaigns in indoor chambers and on outdoor ranges, then reduce and interpret the data
  • Compare measured results against predictions, chase down the disagreements, and feed what you learn back into the models

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS  

  • Must be pursuing or have recently completed a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, or a related field. 
  • Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export-controlled information or facilities; U.S. clearance eligibility may be required depending on program.
  • Able to start in 2027.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Coursework in at least one of: electromagnetics or RF, aircraft or vehicle design, or materials and manufacturing processes
  • Working knowledge of a scripting or analysis language such as MATLAB, Python, or C++
  • Familiarity with a 3D CAD package such as NX, CATIA, SolidWorks, or Creo
  • Demonstrated hands-on engineering work: a capstone or senior design project, internship, undergraduate research, or a student competition team
  • Ability to explain a technical result clearly, in writing and in a design review
  • Exposure to any electromagnetic simulation tool, such as HFSS, CST, FEKO, or COMSOL. X-Patch, SENTRi, and McMoM2D are government codes and we do not expect you to have used them
  • Coursework or project experience with composites, additive manufacturing, casting, or injection molding
  • Experience with laboratory RF measurement: network analyzers, anechoic chambers, or antenna pattern measurement
  • Experience reducing, visualizing, and sanity-checking measured data sets
  • A prior internship or co-op in aerospace, defense, or another hardware-heavy environment

We are looking for a Channel Relationship Manager to own a a strategic channel relationship end to end for 75% of their role and perform joint team efforts the remaining 25% of their time. This partner is crucial for expanding Anduril's reach, developing niche solutions, and accelerating platform adoption across various segments of the Department of Defense and allied governments. This role serves as the single point of accountability for all aspects of your assigned partner pipeline, joint pursuits, integration delivery, and executive alignment. While you won't own every task yourself, you will be accountable for every outcome across your portfolio. This role is focused on growth.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Quarterback a relationship with a key channel partner. You are the single point of accountability for the outcomes of your assigned channel partner — including joint pipeline, influenced revenue, successful integrations, and executive engagement. You will manage the overall performance and health of your portfolio, identifying growth opportunities and addressing challenges
  • Portfolio of Channel Partners management. You will work as a team to cover a large portfolio of other channel partners to drive growth for CW.
  • Own joint pipeline and pursuits across your portfolio. Establish and run a structured cadence with partner field teams. Surface deals, unblock them, and convert pipeline to bookings, ensuring appropriate source-tag governance for all partner-influenced deals.
  • Coordinate the supporting functions efficiently. Ensure internal teams are involved in key initiatives ranging from product line owners to marketing. You are not running their work — you are making sure their work is leveraged to maximize overall outcomes.
  • Be present where your partner operate. You will travel regularly to key partner offices in the National Capital Region (NCR) and other strategic locations, as well as to customer sites where our partners are delivering solutions. This role requires active engagement and on-site presence, not just remote management.
  • Build the trust layer. Partnership velocity across your portfolio is a function of trust between specific people. You will build and maintain strong relationships at various levels within each partner organization (e.g., sector leads, account managers, technical leads, program managers) to foster collaboration and mutual growth.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 5+ years in alliances, partner sales, or business development, with at least 3 years focused on managing a portfolio of multiple mid-tier Systems Integrators, regional integrators, vertical ISVs, or Cloud Service Providers, particularly within the federal space.
  • Deep working knowledge of how diverse federal and commercial partners operate: understanding varying business models, market sectors, organizational structures, and go-to-market strategies of different partner types.
  • Deep knowledge of how channel sales works across resellers and distributors
  • Proven ability to drive joint pipeline with multiple partners simultaneously — not just relationship maintenance. You can show closed deals where you were the partner-side quarterback across a portfolio.
  • Comfort working across multiple internal functions (sales, engineering, product, contracts) without needing formal authority over them. You influence, you don't escalate, and you can effectively prioritize needs across a diverse set of partners.
  • Strong written communication. You can write concise deal memos, comprehensive QBRs (Quarterly Business Reviews) for a portfolio, and credible executive briefs without help.
  • High-ownership, high-energy, low-ego. This is a quarterback role for a portfolio. Quarterbacks take the hit when the team loses.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Prior experience at a regional Systems Integrator, vertical ISV, or a Cloud Service Provider, especially in a business development, alliances, or capture role.
  • Existing relationships within the mid-tier federal SI, regional integrator, or ISV ecosystem across national security, defense, or intelligence sectors.
  • Familiarity with various partner enablement programs, joint solution development, and co-sell motions scalable across a portfolio of partners.
  • Background in C2/C4ISR, edge compute, or DDIL operating environments.
  • Prior military, intelligence community, or DoD civilian experience.

ELIGIBILITY

  • Eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Top Secret/SCI clearance.
  • Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export-controlled information or facilities.
  • Willing to travel 30–50%, with travel spread across the National Capital Region (NCR) and various partner/customer sites nationwide.

Anduril Industries is a defense technology company with a mission to transform U.S. and allied military capabilities with advanced technology. By bringing the expertise, technology, and business model of the 21st century’s most innovative companies to the defense industry, Anduril is changing how military systems are designed, built and sold. Anduril’s family of systems is powered by Lattice OS, an AI-powered operating system that turns thousands of data streams into a realtime, 3D command and control center. As the world enters an era of strategic competition, Anduril is committed to bringing cutting-edge autonomy, AI, computer vision, sensor fusion, and networking technology to the military in months, not years.

ABOUT THE TEAM

Anduril's Maritime Division is transforming American sea power to meet the defining national security challenges of our era and secure our future of maritime dominance.

We are scaling at an historic pace, anchored by Arsenal-2, our new software-defined shipyard being built in Baltimore County, Maryland. It's part of a new $6.6 billion investment in America's submarine industrial base.

Arsenal-2 is purpose-built to break long-standing industrial bottlenecks and scale production of critical components for the Navy's Virginia-class attack submarines to support fleet requirements. At the same time, it will build the industrial muscle to field our next-generation AUVs at scale.

We aren't waiting for the new shipyard to be completed. The work on this transformation starts right now, with development inside our new 160,000 square foot Proto-Factory in Orange County, California, where the team is already laying the foundation. As the prototyping hub for Arsenal-2, this facility gives us a multi-year head start, proving out the advanced manufacturing methods, digital workflows, and quality systems that will scale across our broader shipyard network.

In Anduril's Maritime Division, we are actively building America's next decisive advantage at sea—and this is the moment to join us.

ABOUT THE JOB

You will own the Cognitive subsystem for a maritime autonomous vehicle, owning navigation and control, the vehicle management system, communications, and protective systems. Reporting to the Vehicle Systems Lead, you will set architecture for how the vehicle navigates, communicates, manages itself, and protects itself across long-range autonomous operations.

Your spectrum of support will be diverse in nature and require you to leverage your technical expertise as well as leadership skills to set objectives, build cross-functional teams, and rapidly drive to completion. The ability to leverage your intuition and prior experience will be key in making sure the right design, analysis, and test steps are completed to ensure success. The ideal candidate will leverage their experience executing and successfully completing prior highly optimized multi-disciplinary projects.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Own the Cognitive subsystem architecture: navigation and control, VMS, communications, and protective systems
  • Drive GN&C design including inertial navigation, safe navigation systems, and actuation control software
  • Drive Vehicle Management System design including route planning and casualty monitoring
  • Own communications architecture across BLOS, LOS, and acoustic domains
  • Define protective systems for vehicle survivability
  • Define interfaces between cognitive subsystem and body, energy, and mission systems
  • Manage subsystem schedule and cost performance across prototype, LRIP, and FRP phases
  • Provide technical mentorship to engineers across cognitive disciplines
  • Drive design-for-manufacturability in coordination with Production
  • Represent the cognitive subsystem in technical and customer meetings
  • Interface with Vehicle Systems Lead and Chief Engineer on technical decisions
  • Travel up to 25% to test sites and customer locations

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, Robotics, or equivalent
  • 8+ years of experience in GN&C, vehicle autonomy, or embedded systems for marine, aerospace, or robotic platforms
  • Experience taking navigation, control, or communications systems through full product development cycles
  • Demonstrated experience with navigation systems, control systems, or communications architectures
  • Experience transitioning designs from prototype to production
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience with autonomous underwater or surface vehicles
  • Working knowledge of inertial navigation, GPS-denied navigation, or acoustic communications
  • Experience with vehicle management systems or flight management systems
  • Familiarity with safety-critical software and system design
  • Experience in defense or maritime robotics

Anduril’s Planning team is seeking a world-class Demand & Supply Planner to join our team. The Demand & Supply Planner has an integral role at Anduril, having material flow responsibility throughout the entire value chain, from raw materials to finished goods shipped to customers. They will have full ownership of certain assemblies and product lines, and will be ultimately responsible for sending the correct signals to Purchasing and Manufacturing on what and when to buy or build. This hire will be instrumental in signaling and forecasting accurate demand, planning inventory levels, and ensuring that Anduril supports its hardware requirements via Enterprise Resource Planning (ERP) software and other associated tools.

The right person for this role has demonstrated ownership and experience solving complex operational challenges with creative solutions in a fast-paced, resource-limited environment. This person will be flexible to provide support wherever needed to ensure products are built and shipped under stringent quality standards. If you are someone who thrives in such an environment, then this role is for you!

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Manage day-to-day demand signaling, ordering, and inventory for various product lines.
  • Identify and resolve supply issues by collaborating with Engineering, Purchasing, and Manufacturing teams.
  • Lead Sales and Operations Planning (S&OP) discussions for Supply Planning on designated product lines.
  • Work with Business Development and Growth teams to align forecasts with actual demand plans.
  • Report on and analyze supply and material health to inform key decisions for Engineering, Purchasing, Manufacturing, and Business Development.
  • Develop and maintain processes within MRP systems and associated master data.
  • Drive strategic initiatives towards best practices, including demand shaping, advanced modeling, and inventory optimization.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree in a technical field (i.e. manufacturing, engineering, analytics, computer science, etc.) or business field (i.e. finance, economics, supply chain management, business administration, marketing, etc.)
  • 3+ years of experience in a supply chain or production role within a fast-paced manufacturing environment with complex mechanical and/or electrical assemblies.
  • Complete ownership of a complex value chain, coordinating between multiple internal and internal parties to ensure on-time deliveries and adherence to quality standards.
  • Technical expertise including ability to read technical documentation and understanding hardware manufacturing processes.
  • Experience with ERP systems such as Oracle, Netsuite, and CRM systems like Salesforce.
  • Ability to travel up to 10% of the time.
  • Ability to relocate, if not already local to be onsite in Costa Mesa, CA.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Master’s degree or other higher education.
  • 6+ years of experience in a supply chain or production role within a fast-paced manufacturing environment with complex mechanical and/or electrical assemblies.
  • Strong experience with SQL databases, including building custom queries for production and inventory metrics.
  • Proficiency in data analysis and reporting tools such as Tableau, Power BI, or Qlikview.
  • Knowledge of supply chain planning systems like Blue Yonder and best practices in demand planning, inventory management, and S&OP.
  • Experience with lean manufacturing, continuous improvement, six sigma principles, and big data evaluation techniques.
  • Proactive, able to take substantial responsibility across various functions, with a focus on speed and accuracy.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. TS clearance.

ABOUT THE JOB

The Director, Strategic Supply Chain supports engineering and production teams with the development and execution of sourcing plans. As the Director of Strategic Supply Chain this individual will be the central point of contact for all supply chain needs in the product development process internally and externally. In this role, you will work with engineering, product program office and the broader production leadership team to support strategic sourcing initiatives and planning in pursuit of program and manufacturing goals, and lead cross-functional projects to achieve cost, quality, and delivery targets.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Lead and scale the Strategic Sourcing team, building a high-performing organization that drives strategic sourcing for nascent products and develops an industrial strategy to support supply chain through production and sustainment. Attract, develop, and retain top talent; hold a high bar through coaching, feedback, and accountability.
  • Partner with chief engineers and program managers of our most nascent programs to ensure the products they are defining are designed and pitched with a supply chain capable of delivering on their cost, schedule, and performance targets.
  • Identify opportunities for strategic agreements and partnerships with suppliers that capture cost savings, enable roadmap alignment, and strengthen the supply base for AD&S’s products.
  • Align supplier roadmaps with AD&S’s portfolio vision and roadmap, to enable the supply base to support AD&S as it expands.
  • Drive optionality and competition into the supply base, ensuring the supply base can support Anduril today and in the future.
  • Collaborate cross-functionally with Supplier Industrialization, Procurement, Program Management, Quality, Manufacturing, and Finance to align strategic sourcing activities with program milestones and business objectives.
  • Define and monitor key performance indicators (KPIs) and supplier scorecards to track industrial base health. Provide regular executive-level reporting on risks, opportunities, and performance.
  • Proactively identify and mitigate potential risks to the supply chain, such as disruptions to supply or changes in market conditions.
  • Develop and implement supply chain strategies that align with overall business goals, aiming for supply continuity, quality, efficiency and cost optimization while enabling the business to scale significantly.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree in supply chain, engineering, or related technical field.
  • 10+ years experience in a fast-paced manufacturing environment specifically in a supply chain or production-related role focused on complex mechanical and/or electrical assembly. At least 5+ years experience in a leadership position.
  • Strong communication skills with the ability to communicate effectively across all levels of the organization.
  • Ability to travel up to 20%.
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • MBA or Master’s degree in supply chain, engineering, or related technical field.
  • Previous experience in defense, aerospace, automotive, high tech, or another related industry.
  • Proven leadership in driving and influencing large teams toward common goals.
  • Strong team player who can adapt to different roles to support team progress, including individual contributor tasks while managing a small team.

We are looking for a Electrical Test Engineer to join our Manufacturing organization in Santa Ana, California. In this role, you will design and build complex test systems and PCBA platforms that ensure our products meet stringent quality standards before shipping to customers. You will own full-cycle PCB design for test hardware — from requirements capture and schematic design through component selection, layout, bring-up, debug, and integration with production test environments. 

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Design circuits and schematics for test automation platforms, including FPGA-based data acquisition boards, MCU data interfaces, breakout boards, wiring harnesses, and peripheral modules.
  • Own full-cycle PCB design for test hardware — collecting requirements, capturing schematics, selecting components, supervising or completing layout, and driving designs through fabrication and assembly.
  • Architect and source circuit board test fixtures, integrating custom designs with internally developed and off-the-shelf data acquisition equipment.
  • Bring up, debug, and characterize circuits across low-speed interfaces (I2C, SPI, CAN) and high-speed signals (RF, memory, USB).
  • Apply DFT best practices to new products, to enable comprehensive tester design
  • Work with firmware engineers to enable board support packages for embedded Linux and bring up MCU RTOS platforms.
  • Integrate designs into configuration management systems, using proper control and release processes.
  • Continuously improve test automation methods, throughput, user interfaces, and data analytics.
REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS
  • Bachelor’s degree in Electrical/Electronics, Computer, Mechanical Engineering, or related fields OR 6+ years of advanced knowledge acquired through work experience and/or intellectual instruction in lieu of degree
  • 4+ years of professional experience in electrical hardware design with emphasis on products that have gone to manufacturing.
  • Expertise in PCBA design — ability to design and fabricate your own boards or guide contract manufacturing resources.
  • Full understanding of PCB layout techniques to meet mechanical, electrical, and manufacturing requirements.
  • Experience with Altium Designer or equivalent E-CAD tools for schematic capture and layout.
  • Familiarity with standard interfaces such as Ethernet, CAN, I2C, SPI, USB, and common MCU/FPGA devices.
  • Familiarity with electronics test equipment including power supplies, electronic loads, oscilloscopes, function generators, spectrum analyzers, and data acquisition sensors.
  • Familiar with Product Life Cycle (PLM) systems and releasing designs for production.
  • Excellent communication skills and ability to work effectively in a multi-disciplinary team.
  • Currently possesses and is able to maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance.

  • Experience with FPGA PCBA platforms — RTL, design synthesis, and bare-metal coding.
  • Experience with Python scripting for test configuration and automation.
  • Master's degree in Electrical/Electronics Engineering or related field.

  • Effectively distill and communicate complex scenarios to executives for strategic decision-making and alignment

  • 3+ years of experience managing a direct team
  • Demonstrated ability to completely own complex value chains from start to finish, coordinating between multiple internal and internal parties to ensure on-time deliveries and adherence to quality standards
  • Experience with ERP systems such as Oracle, Netsuite, and CRM systems like Salesforce
  • Ability to demonstrate a willingness to take on substantial responsibility across supply chain, logistics, engineering, and supply planning functions with a bias towards speed and accuracy

  • Knowledge of supply chain planning systems like Blue Yonder and best practices in demand planning, inventory management, and S&OP
  • Experience with lean manufacturing, continuous improvement, six sigma principles, and big data evaluation techniques
  • Proactive, able to take substantial responsibility across various functions, with a focus on speed and accuracy

ABOUT THE TEAM

As a Software Manufacturing Test Engineer, you will build, scale, and maintain the software that drives our manufacturing test systems. In this role, your primary focus will be developing production software that directly tests complex hardware systems, integrates with laboratory instrumentation and DAQs, and manages the data these stations produce. You will bridge low-level hardware control with high-level test automation by writing robust, reliable production code in Python and C# targeting Linux/Unix (and ideally NixOS) runtime environments.
To ensure our hardware meets mission-critical quality and production throughput demands, every Software Manufacturing Test Engineer is expected to derive software test requirements from hardware schematics and system specifications, author automated test sequences, and deploy complete software suites to factory test racks. You will work closely with development and firmware engineers to refine test coverage as product designs evolve, resolve complex hardware-software integration failures on the floor, and ensure deterministic software deployments across our manufacturing line.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Maintain ownership of software manufacturing test activities in production, ensuring test station uptime, operator usability, and smooth factory throughput
  • Develop and maintain PLC-integrated station control software — commanding industrial controllers over Modbus TCP for rig actuation, interlocks, and sensor acquisition — and maintain the tag/address index as PLC programs evolve, including tooling that imports controller tag exports and validates them against the station's expected schema
  • Build hardware-free simulation environments (containerized station images, virtual CAN replay, device simulators) so test software is developed and regression-tested without occupying hardware
  • Design, build, and maintain production software manufacturing test suites primarily in Python (for hardware control, test sequencing, and instrument automation) and C# (for test executives, operator interfaces, and background services)
  • Integrate software manufacturing test applications directly with sensors, DAQs, programmable power supplies, electronic loads, and vehicle compute hardware
  • Implement low-level hardware communication using embedded protocols including UART, CAN, and RS-485 / RS-232 to command, flash, and validate devices under test (DUTs)
  • Deploy, configure, and debug software manufacturing test systems running on Linux/Unix platforms using terminal command-line tools, SSH, and network debugging utilities
  • Leverage Nix and NixOS to manage reproducible software manufacturing test environments, eliminating dependency drift between engineering development benches and production line stations
  • Collaborate with hardware and firmware engineers during early-stage product development (NPI) to define software manufacturing test requirements, coverage, APIs, and pass/fail limits
  • Automate software manufacturing test execution across various levels of assembly, from PCBA-level functional test (FCT) up to full-system and Environmental Stress Screening (ESS) checkouts
  • Provide hands-on troubleshooting and root-cause analysis (RCCA) for complex electrical, firmware, and software manufacturing test issues found on the line
  • Log parametric test data and integrate software manufacturing test stations with database systems (using SQL queries as needed) and Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES) to maintain complete hardware traceability
  • Develop clear operator interfaces, error-handling mechanisms, and software manufacturing test troubleshooting logs to assist technicians during hardware failures
  • Support continuous improvement initiatives to optimize software manufacturing test sequences, shorten cycle times, and increase test coverage without sacrificing quality

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or related fields
  • Python or C programming
  • 3+ years of relevant industry experience as a Software Manufacturing Test Engineer, or in an equivalent role with an emphasis on software development for hardware test automation, lab automation, or manufacturing environments
  • Strong proficiency writing production code in Python for software manufacturing test automation, device control, and data handling
  • Working knowledge of C# (.NET) for developing software manufacturing test applications, operator UIs, or system services
  • Strong Linux/Unix systems knowledge, including terminal proficiency, shell scripting, SSH, and network configuration/debugging
  • Demonstrated hands-on experience interfacing software manufacturing test suites with embedded communication protocols: UART, CAN, and RS-485 / RS-232
  • Familiarity with controlling standard test equipment (programmable power supplies, DMMs, oscilloscopes, electronic loads, and DAQ devices) via software
  • Strong root-cause analysis skills for diagnosing hardware-software boundary issues using log files, terminal outputs, and basic bench tools
  • Experience integrating software manufacturing test platforms with Manufacturing Execution Systems (MES) and database backends
  • Excellent written, verbal, and interpersonal communication skills to collaborate with hardware, software, and operations teams
  • Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Experience with Nix and NixOS for declarative software manufacturing test environment management and deployment
  • C programming knowledge
  • Familiarity with SQL for direct database querying and test record validation
  • Basic familiarity with HTML/CSS for formatting internal software manufacturing test run reports or local dashboard views
  • Experience working with contract manufacturers in software manufacturing test execution for PCBA and electronic assemblies
  • Familiarity with hardware protocols such as Ethernet, USB, PCIe, and SPI/I2C
  • Experience developing software manufacturing test solutions for aerospace, defense, or automotive hardware under environmental stress conditions (Thermal, Vibration, Burn-in)
  • Active U.S. Secret or Top Secret security clearance

Anduril's Space team is dedicated to expanding our AI-powered capabilities into the final frontier, enhancing Space Domain Awareness, Space Control, and Command and Control for U.S. military and allied partners. We're developing fully integrated hardware and software systems, including Lattice for Space Missions and modular payloads, to address growing threats in space and ensure our Guardians maintain a decisive advantage in this contested warfighting domain.

ABOUT THE JOB

You'll own the production readiness of space hardware — take maturing and flight-proven designs and drive them to repeatable, higher-rate manufacturing. Intelligently pace design changes with a holistic view of the program and its build schedule.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Use first principles as a basis for decisions and continuously look for opportunities to simplify designs, reduce part count, and design for manufacturing, assembly, and test (DFM/DFA/DFT) — improving producibility, repeatability, and reliability at higher production quantities
  • Modify and mature existing designs to resolve problems realized in production – fit, tolerance, assembly, and yield issues
  • Update designs to reduce build and test cycle times, improve first-pass yield, and remove bottlenecks from assembly, integration, and test (AI&T) operations
  • Own bills of material (BOMs) and engineering drawings – release and maintain part and assembly drawings, GD&T, and BOM structure; process engineering changes (ECO/ECN) and manage revisions and effectivity
  • Propagate engineering changes through assembly hierarchies — revise parent assembly models, drawings, and BOMs when subcomponent designs change, ensuring next-higher-level documentation stays current and consistent
  • Act as the Responsible Engineer for your hardware in production: disposition non conformances, author red-lines and rework/retrofit instructions
  • Partner with manufacturing, supply chain, and test engineering to transition designs from low-rate to higher-rate production and to stand up repeatable work instructions, tooling, and fixtures
  • Build and validate prototypes and production trial builds, analyze failures, and feed lessons learned back into the design and the build process
  • Travel to test sites, production facilities, and vendors as needed
  • Create excellent technical documentation – assembly and work instructions, procedures, test plans and reports, vendor specifications and statements of work, etc.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • BS or higher degree in engineering or a hard science
  • CAD skills (any platform) and ability to make high quality engineering drawings that meet common industry standards, including GD&T
  • Experience taking hardware designs into manufacturing and production – design for manufacturing/assembly and drawing release. Experience transitioning hardware from prototype or low-rate to higher-rate production
  • Working knowledge of BOM structures, revision control, and engineering change orders (ECO/ECN), ideally within a PLM/PDM system
  • Demonstrated hands-on fabrication and assembly skills. Experience working with hand tools, mill, lathe, etc.
  • Strong understanding of engineering fundamentals: heat transfer, statics, solid mechanics, materials
  • Familiarity with tolerance analysis and inspection methods
  • Excellent attention to detail
  • Highly motivated, self-starting, and able to perform duties autonomously without supervision
  • Very organized and willing to establish scope and requirements for ill-defined problems
  • Passion for defending the United States and her allies
  • Be able to obtain and hold a U.S. Top Secret security clearance

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • 4+ years of mechanical design or production/sustaining engineering experience in a professional setting with space hardware
  • Experience in NX/Teamcenter or equivalent CAD/PLM
  • Experience with nonconformance disposition and Material Review Board, root cause and corrective action (RCCA), and first article inspection (FAI)
  • Experience designing tooling, fixtures, and ground support equipment to improve build and test throughput
  • Ability to integrate electronic components (PCBAs, motors, sensors, etc.) into mechanical designs
  • Experience developing code in higher-level languages (e.g. Python, MATLAB, C++) for analytical models, data acquisition, and automation
  • Experience with statistical process control, tolerance stack-ups, or design of experiments (DOE) to improve yield

ABOUT THE TEAM
The Connected Warfare Division is integrating advanced computing, AI-driven decision-making, and warfighter-centric technology into a single, cohesive ecosystem to revolutionize modern combat. We create joint, time-sensitive, multi-domain, connected mesh systems that connect every robot, human, and sensor across every domain—bringing together hundreds of thousands of endpoints globally.

Within Connected Warfare, our Warfighter Systems division is pioneering a future where mixed reality and advanced sensing create immersive, intuitive, and life-saving technologies. By integrating real-time data with cutting-edge visualization and targeting tools, we empower warfighters with unparalleled situational awareness, enhanced lethality, and operational superiority.

ABOUT THE JOB
We're seeking a Staff Technical Program Manager to drive the design, development, and production scaling of our Advanced Targeting System—a rugged, mission-critical product that fuses sensing, optics, weapon integration, and connected battlefield data to deliver decisive advantage to the warfighter. You'll take immediate ownership of a product already in the field, driving its evolution, scalability, and transition to full-rate production.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Program Management: Align roadmaps, manage timelines, and allocate resources across mechanical, electrical, firmware, and optics teams while balancing competing priorities in a fast-paced startup environment.
  • Cross-functional Collaboration: Serve as the primary liaison between engineering, manufacturing, product, and external stakeholders—including defense contractors and government entities.
  • Technical Leadership: Navigate the architecture and trade-offs of ruggedized targeting systems—LiDAR, weapon mounts, power, thermal, and embedded electronics—while ensuring compliance with ITAR, RMF, and other regulations.

  • Stakeholder Management: Manage relationships with suppliers, customers, and government agencies; deliver clear program updates and technical briefs to internal and external audiences.

  • Warfighter Engagement: Travel to exercises and live-fire assessments to gather operator feedback and translate it into program requirements.

  • 6+ years managing complex hardware development programs across the full development lifecycle
  • 8+ years combined experience as a TPM, Product Manager, Engineering Manager, or Engineer in commercial tech or aerospace & defense
  • Hands-on experience leading ruggedized electromechanical systems—ideally targeting, sensing, optics, or weapon-integrated platforms
  • Strong technical fluency across mechanical, electrical, and firmware domains, with the ability to manage trade-offs across a complex system
  • Experience owning a complex BOM, engineering drawings, and change management within a PLM tool
  • Proven experience in component sourcing, vendor management, and DFM/DFA coordination with manufacturing partners
  • Exceptional communication skills, able to translate technical complexity into business-impacting insights
  • Willingness to travel up to 25%, including to field exercises and customer sites
  • U.S. Person status required (export-controlled data)

ABOUT THE JOB

Anduril's Sentry Planning team is looking for a Supply Planner to own the supply and production strategy for a set of complex hardware assemblies and product lines. This person sets the supply strategy, shaping what we need to build, in what quantity, and how far ahead of demand signals, so that annual production commitments and customer ship dates are achievable. Material Planning owns clear-to-builds and day-to-day material execution; You own the strategy that puts Planning and your product lines in a position to succeed.

To be clear about scope: you do not own the demand forecast, you own what supply plan to support it. Demand signals here move fast. The right person for this role has ownership and experience solving complex operational challenges with creative solutions in a fast-paced, resource-limited environment. This person will be flexible to provide support wherever needed to ensure products are built and shipped under stringent quality standards. If you are someone who thrives in such an environment, then this role is for you!

WHAT YOU'LL DO

  • Lead Sales and Operations Planning (S&OP) discussions for Supply Planning on designated product lines.
  • Work with Demand Planning and Production Program Management partners to align production throughput and build plans with actual demand plans.
  • Own the end-to-end supply and production plan for assigned assemblies and product lines, translating volatile, incomplete, and sometimes conflicting demand signals into a firm supply plan.
  • Set the inventory strategy and production plan for your scope, including safety stock, lead time offsets, production throughput, and proposing weekly production work orders.
  • Sequence the build schedule and allocate constrained material across programs when supply can't cover all build signals.
  • Protect Annual Planning commitments and customer ship dates. Pressure-test requests that put them at risk, and escalate early with options.
  • Drive recovery with cross-functional partners when supply breaks. Partner with Material Planning and Purchasing to expedite, de-expedite, or re-source; work with Engineering on substitutions and change timing; keep Manufacturing Engineering and Production partners current on what's moving and when.
  • Report on supply and material health in a way that forces decisions rather than describing status, covering coverage, risk, aging, and excess, along with your recommendation on each.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Bachelor’s degree in a technical field (i.e. manufacturing, engineering, analytics, computer science, etc.) or business field (i.e. finance, economics, supply chain management, business administration, marketing, etc.)
  • 3+ years of experience in a supply chain or production role within a fast-paced manufacturing environment dealing with complex assemblies.
  • Complete ownership of a complex value chain, coordinating between multiple, high volume of departments and teams to ensure on-time deliveries and adherence to quality standards.
  • Strong analytical capabilities - create and analyze complex models that automate the identification of any supply shortfalls
  • Proactive, able to take substantial responsibility across various functions, with a focus on speed and accuracy.
  • Experience with ERP systems such as Oracle, NetSuite, and CRM systems like Salesforce
  • Strong experience with Slack/Teams and Microsoft PowerPoint and Excel
  • Ability to travel up to 10% of the time.
  • Ability to relocate, if not already local to be onsite in Irvine, CA.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Master’s degree or other higher education
  • Strong experience with SQL databases, including building custom queries for production and inventory metrics.
  • Proficiency in data analysis and reporting tools such as Tableau, Power BI, or Qlikview.
  • Technical expertise including ability to read technical documentation and understanding hardware manufacturing processes.
  • Knowledge of supply chain planning systems like Blue Yonder and best practices in demand planning, inventory management, and S&OP.
  • Experience with lean manufacturing, continuous improvement, six sigma principles, and big data evaluation techniques.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. TS clearance.

ABOUT THE JOB

We are looking for a technical trainer to join our rapidly growing team in Morrisville, NC. In this role, you will be responsible for the orientation and training of new hires as well as ongoing technical training for our composite techs. You will assist with developing new training and refining our existing courses on our digital platform. You will also work closely with our manufacturing team to make sure changes in SOP are passed on to our composite teams. This position may require occasional travel to our headquarters in Costa Mesa or other facilities around the country. This will require composite layup, bonding and assembly experience as well as excellent communication skills. If you are someone who excels at communication, teamwork, adaptability, problem-solving, critical thinking, and leadership then this role is for you.

What you’ll do:

  • Conduct comprehensive onboarding and initial 2-week training programs for new hires, ensuring a solid foundation in company processes and technical skills.
  • Deliver recurring training sessions on critical operational areas, including Quality Management Systems (QMS), Business Process Standards (BPS), Foreign Object Debris (FOD) prevention, and Safety protocols.
  • Provide effective On-the-Job Training (OJT) and mentorship to newly promoted technicians, facilitating their transition and skill enhancement.
  • Prepare and develop controlled samples and practical testing materials for hands-on training (e.g., carbon angle layups for tapes, carbon for bond preparation, filler application, adhesive mixing, double cupping techniques) to ensure practical skill validation.
  • Design and develop engaging training videos, and regularly review existing video content to ensure alignment with current specifications, procedures, and best practices.
  • Maintain accurate and up-to-date training records and documentation in a timely manner, ensuring compliance and traceability.

Required Qualifications:

  • Minimum of 3 years of hands-on experience as a technician in a relevant manufacturing or production environment.
  • Proven ability to effectively demonstrate technical procedures and communicate complex information clearly in both one-on-one and group training settings.
  • Comfortable and proficient in public speaking, capable of delivering engaging presentations to large groups.
  • Exceptional verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to interact clearly and concisely with peers, management, and all levels of the organization.
  • A strong work ethic and the ability to contribute to production tasks or shop duties during periods between formal training sessions.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Previous experience in a training, mentoring, or lead technician role.
  • Familiarity with Learning Management Systems (LMS) or training software.
  • Certifications related to Quality Management (e.g., QMS principles), Safety (e.g., OSHA), or specific manufacturing processes.

About the Team

OpenAI’s mission is to ensure that artificial general intelligence benefits all of humanity. The Creative Partnerships team supports that mission by building trusted relationships with creators, experts, and organizations to help them explore valuable uses of AI.

We work across OpenAI to develop partnerships grounded in trust, usefulness, and measurable impact. Our work goes beyond individual launches and includes product education, partner feedback, and collaborative programs that create lasting value for partners and OpenAI.

About the Role

We’re looking for an experienced partnerships leader to develop and scale high-touch onboarding and enablement experiences for creators, brands and institutions.

You will help partners move from initial curiosity to meaningful, hands-on use of OpenAI’s products. This includes understanding their work and ambitions, designing tailored onboarding experiences, helping them develop authentic use cases, and ensuring they have the support needed to engage confidently over time.

You will serve as a trusted bridge between external partners and teams across OpenAI. You’ll translate product capabilities into relevant creative possibilities, bring actionable feedback and cultural insights back to the company, and develop an operating model that combines highly personalized support with the systems needed to scale.

In this role, you will:

  • Define the strategy, partner journey, operating model, and quality bar for high-touch onboarding, creating clear pathways from introduction and education to experimentation, adoption, and long-term engagement.

  • Design and lead tailored onboarding sessions, workshops, product demonstrations, and ongoing enablement that help creators, brands, institutions and their teams apply OpenAI’s products to their work.

  • Learn how each partner works and develop authentic use cases aligned with their creative goals, audiences, and values, helping turn early experimentation into compelling examples of creativity, expression, and connection.

  • Serve as a consistent, trusted point of contact for partners and their representatives, anticipating needs, resolving challenges, and providing thoughtful support with discretion, care, and sound judgment.

  • Partner with internal teams to explore broader collaborations where there is strong mutual value and authentic alignment.

  • Bring actionable product feedback, emerging behaviors, creative workflows, and cultural insights to Product, Research, Marketing, Communications, Policy, and other teams. Help stakeholders understand partner needs and identify recurring opportunities or friction points that could inform product development and company strategy.

  • Create feedback loops that show partners how their perspectives are heard and acted upon.

  • Develop playbooks, enablement materials, partner briefs, follow-up plans, escalation paths, and reusable resources that balance personalized engagement with repeatable systems.

  • Establish clear ownership and handoffs across Partnerships, Product, Marketing, Communications, Legal, Policy, and Support as the program scales.

  • Define and track meaningful measures of success, including partner engagement, time to activation, depth of use, relationship health, actionable product feedback, and partnership outcomes. Use qualitative and quantitative insights to improve, expand, and scale the program.

You might thrive in this role if you:

  • Have 10+ years of experience in creator or talent partnerships, strategic partnerships, platform partnerships, product enablement, client services, or another highly relationship-driven field.

  • Have experience supporting creators, brands, or other high-profile partners and their representatives.

  • Build exceptional relationships through the judgment, discretion, and responsiveness required to earn trust over time.

  • Bring strong cultural fluency and a nuanced understanding of how creators, talent, platforms, and communities influence one another.

  • Translate complex or emerging technology into clear, relevant, and inspiring possibilities for non-technical audiences.

  • Develop authentic use cases around a partner’s real goals rather than applying a one-size-fits-all approach.

  • Align cross-functional stakeholders, manage dependencies, and create clarity in ambiguous environments.

  • Communicate and facilitate effectively, whether leading intimate working sessions or engaging senior and high-profile audiences.

  • Bring hands-on fluency with AI products and curiosity about how they can support creative work, expression, and connection.

  • Have strong program-management discipline, including experience developing workflows, standards, measurement, and scalable resources.

  • Move comfortably between highly personalized partner engagement and the behind-the-scenes operational work required to deliver it well.

  • Take a thoughtful, data-informed approach and distinguish surface-level engagement from durable trust, meaningful adoption, and genuine partnership potential.

ABOUT THE ROLE:

This team owns 100% GPU uptime, end to end, 24/7, across both compute and facility. It owns incident response and the engineering behind it, holds central control authority from the customer back to the facility, runs day-to-day sustainment of live datahalls, and leads deployment engineering for new datahall bring-up. The team will also build the automation for continuous response improvement. The team is expected to have system level knowledge about the whole datacenter site, end to end. The team engineers solutions to enable GPU uptime, working directly with technicians in the datahalls and field to execute the team’s engineering planning.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Own monitoring architecture, alerting, signal quality, and automation of monitoring across GPU and host telemetry (DCGM, Prometheus/Grafana) and facility telemetry (BMS, EPMS, DCIM, SCADA, CDU / direct liquid cooling).
  • Own compute hardware change incorporation - physical, firmware, software.
  • Be part of 24/7 iincident response, mitigation, and control authority - end to end - from customer impact back to the facility.
  • Own day-to-day site sustainment operations, including resolving issues impacting rack-level compute and facility infrastructure.
  • Disposition daily issues across both Site Operations (rack compute) and Facility Operations (power and cooling).
  • Lead acceptance and deployment testing campaigns to bring new data halls fully online.
  • Develop production automation for new datahall bring-up, automation behind alerting and automated incident response.
  • Develop and maintain standard operating procedures and planning for facility and site technicians. Includes change / upgrade incorporation planning on both rack level and facility.
  • Own and document the live, changing state of datahall operation as new halls come online.
  • Enable Site Operations and Facility Operations technicians to do their day to day jobs more efficiently and safely to increase GPU uptime.
  • Create predictive and responsive automation to alerts and incidents to enable your response to be faster and more impactful.
  • Lead cross-functional reliability projects spanning compute, network (InfiniBand/RoCE), storage, and facility signal boundaries, including grey failures that cross those boundaries (e.g., NVLink flapping, thermal throttling, power sequencing).
  • Truly root cause systemic and design failure classes across hardware and integrated facility and operations systems: turn fleet data (MTBF/AFR, repeat-RMA trends) into proactive alerting, standard responses, vendor RCA inputs, and supplier corrective actions.

BASIC QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Electrical, or Computer Engineering or a related scientific discipline and 2+ years of experience in data center, critical facilities, power plant, or large-scale compute operations; or 6+ years of equivalent experience in those environments.

PREFERRED SKILLS AND EXPERIENCE:

  • Hands-on experience with at least one of: Prometheus/Grafana, NVIDIA DCGM, or industrial telemetry and controls (SCADA, BMS/BAS, EPMS, DCIM, PLCs, Modbus/BACnet).
  • Experience in datacenter site reliability, systems engineering, plant operations, or large-scale production operations.
  • Experience running acceptance test campaigns for integrated products.
  • Experience in AI/ML infrastructure or supercomputing environments: GB200/NVL72 or H100/H200-class GPU fleets, NCCL, InfiniBand/RoCE, Slurm or Kubernetes.
  • Fleet firmware and BMC management (Redfish, IPMI), including firmware release validation and staged rollouts.
  • Familiarity with data center hardware and plant signals (servers, GPUs, networking, power, cooling) in addition to software telemetry.
  • Proven large-scale incident command experience and calm technical leadership on a bridge, whether from an SRE/NOC bridge or a plant control room.
  • Experience writing and operating playbooks, runbooks, or standard operating procedures, methods of procedure, emergency operations procedures.
  • Proficiency in scripting (Python, Bash) for automation and analysis, plus general experience in at least one systems language (C, C++, Java, Go, Rust, or similar).
  • Ability to work collaboratively with cross-functional, cross-country, multi-disciplinary teams.

We are seeking an Operational Analyst to drive the modeling, simulation, and analysis of Shield AI’s autonomous aircraft systems. This role is pivotal in evaluating the mission effectiveness, survivability, and operational impact of our next gen UAS and other autonomous platforms. You will work closely with engineering, product development, and defense stakeholders to inform design trade-offs, assess system performance, and optimize mission capabilities.

This position requires a deep understanding of military operations, wargaming, modeling & simulation (M&S), and operational analysis techniques. Your work will directly shape Shield AI’s strategy by identifying how our AI-powered aircraft can best serve the evolving needs of modern warfare.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

  • Develop and execute operational analysis strategies to assess the effectiveness of autonomous aircraft in real-world military scenarios.
  • Lead modeling, simulation, and wargaming efforts to evaluate system performance, mission impact, and survivability in contested environments.
  • Work closely with engineering teams to translate operational insights into design decisions and system improvements.
  • Conduct trade studies and sensitivity analyses to assess system performance under varying operational conditions and threats.
  • Utilize advanced modeling & simulation tools (e.g., AFSIM, STK, MATLAB, Python) to develop high-fidelity mission models.
  • Analyze force-on-force engagements, sensor effectiveness, and autonomy-driven decision-making to optimize mission success.
  • Collaborate with DoD stakeholders, operators, and warfighters to understand mission needs and align system capabilities with operational requirements.
  • Develop and present technical reports, briefings, and recommendations to senior leadership, customers, and government agencies.
  • Support concept of operations (CONOPS) development for new AI-driven aircraft capabilities.
  • Identify emerging threats and operational challenges, ensuring Shield AI’s systems remain ahead of adversary capabilities.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 10+ years of experience in operational analysis, modeling & simulation (M&S), or military operations research.
  • Expertise in military mission analysis, operational planning, and wargaming methodologies.
  • Proficiency with AFSIM, STK, MATLAB, Python, or other M&S tools used for aerospace and defense applications.
  • Deep understanding of air combat, ISR, electronic warfare, or autonomous systems in contested environments.
  • Experience working with DoD stakeholders, warfighters, and government agencies to align capabilities with mission requirements.
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret large datasets and translate findings into actionable insights.
  • Excellent communication and briefing skills, with experience presenting to senior leadership, customers, and military personnel.
  • Ability to work in a fast-paced, agile development environment with shifting priorities.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Prior experience in force-on-force analysis, CONOPS development, or military campaign modeling.
  • Familiarity with DoD acquisition processes, Joint Capabilities Integration and Development System (JCIDS), and military operational testing.
  • Experience integrating AI-driven decision-making algorithms into operational analysis frameworks.
  • Prior military service or experience working with U.S. Air Force, Navy, or Special Operations Forces.
  • Active Secret clearance (or ability to obtain one).

As a Staff Fluid and Mechanical Systems Engineer, you will be a hands-on multi-disciplinary owner of fluid-system layouts, thermal transport hardware, and adjacent mechanical design for a Group 5 UAV fighter aircraft. You will apply first-principles engineering to develop ram-air circuits, liquid cooling systems, ECS/TMS fluid architecture, and supporting mechanical installations that are buildable, maintainable, and ready for vehicle integration. This position requires a balance of technical rigor, rapid decision-making, and hands-on engineering to efficiently transition concepts into operational capability. The ideal candidate is comfortable solving complex problems, taking ownership, working within an accelerated aircraft development environment, and is motivated by getting meaningful capability into the hands of operators quickly.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Experience: 6+ years of fluid systems design, thermal systems analysis, or mechanical systems installation experience in aerospace or a comparable regulated industry.
  • Education: B.S. or M.S. in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
  • Core Fundamentals: Deep mastery of thermodynamics, fluid dynamics, heat transfer, mechanical design fundamentals, and tolerance stack-up methodologies.
  • Modeling and Analysis: Demonstrated capability with fluid system sizing and analysis, including pressure drop, flow networks, heat transfer, and 1D fluid or thermal system modeling.
  • System Layout and Integration: Demonstrated ability to create fluid-system layouts and mechanical installations that satisfy routing, packaging, maintainability, structural-interface, and vehicle-integration requirements.
  • CAD and PLM: Experience in 3D CAD modeling, routing, layouts, and drawing release with Siemens NX, CATIA, Creo, SolidWorks, or equivalent PLM workflows.
  • Mechanical Design: Hands-on capability designing brackets, mounts, supports, and installation hardware using hand calculations, tolerance analysis, and basic structural analysis.
  • Hardware and Supplier Execution: Proven track record sourcing COTS/custom aerospace components, driving suppliers to schedule, and assembling benchtop or vehicle-level test setups.
  • Autonomy: Demonstrated ability to self-direct, prioritize technical tasks without oversight, and deliver functional hardware under tight timelines.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Aircraft ram-air, liquid cooling, hydraulic, fuel, or thermal transport loop design experience.
  • ECS or thermal management system design and integration experience.
  • Experience with electro-mechanical or electro-hydrostatic actuation systems and associated mechanical installations.
  • Familiarity with MIL-STD-810, MIL-HDBK-516, and airworthiness verification planning for fluid and mechanical systems.
  • Hands-on prototype-build, fabrication, or mechanical assembly experience in a rapid R&D environment.
  • Eligible to obtain a Secret clearance.

Partner Operations is obsessed with making direct delivery simpler for new content partners and the Netflix teams who receive and launch their titles day-to-day. We evaluate what the partner can deliver, how those assets might move through fulfillment and launch systems, and what it takes to support the deal day to day.

As a Partner Operations Manager, you will be the operational lead across an assigned slate of deals. You will assess what a partner can deliver, decide the appropriate delivery path, guide the partner through first deliveries and set up a process that Operations teams can run day to day. You will balance the partner experience with the work required of Netflix teams and vendors, and make the important decisions and handoffs clear.


In this role, you will:

  • Clarify deal goals, asset and localization needs, timing, partner contacts and open questions with Business Development, Regional Merchandising and Content teams as deals move into delivery planning.
  • Assess the partner’s ability to meet our specs. Compare their needs with Netflix’s current system and operational capabilities; identify what is missing, what may need to be built and the effort required from integration through stable operations.
  • Apply gateway eligibility criteria agreed with Engineering to determine delivery through UI, API or a vendor route. Work with Ops Vendor Management on the vendor model and cost, considering the effort for the partner and Netflix teams.
  • Lead pre-qualification across long-form and promotional assets. Coordinate sample and quality reviews, then determine which assets Netflix can accept or conform, what the partner must change and whether vendor or post-vendor QC is needed.
  • Turn partner context and deal nuance into clear technical and operational requirements for Product and Engineering. Frame the problem, define the workflow and write user stories where useful, making timing, constraints and trade-offs clear.   • Prepare partners to meet spec, coordinate tests and work through first deliveries. Answer delivery and spec questions clearly, bring in technical specialists when needed and remove early blockers.
  • Keep partners, vendors and internal teams aligned on decisions, risks, owners and next steps. Communicate early and on time, and anticipate what each team will need before it becomes a problem.
  • Hand off the partner profile, setup and open risks to the Launch Ops project manager once delivery is reliable.

  • BS / MS / PhD in EE, CE, or related (or equivalent experience).

This is a unique opportunity to build at the intersection of organizational strategy, enablement, operating model design, talent and capability development, and enterprise transformation.

 

You will lead the organizational strategy and enablement capabilities that help Frontier translate its business ambition into organizational structure, clearly defined roles, and the capabilities our people need to succeed. Working across the organization, you will shape and evolve role architecture, workforce capabilities, skilling and development, and the mechanisms that turn strategy into sustained ways of working as Frontier grows and evolves.

Future Workforce Strategy

Microsoft AI Experiences (AIX) builds the end-user AI experience at Microsoft, spanning Copilot, Search, Browser, Content, Commerce, and Monetization. AIX is roughly 7,000 people working from core hubs in Redmond, Mountain View, and New York City, engineering centers across India and China, and established teams in Vancouver, San Francisco, Barcelona, Cairo, and other locations. The organization moves quickly and ships on a fast, high-visibility rhythm. 

AIX Ops keeps the organization running so the team can stay focused on building great products. We are a small, fast-moving team that supports each other, operates with integrity and inclusivity, and makes decisions based on evidence rather than opinion. Every day looks a little different, and the work has real and immediate impact on how a 7,000-person organization plans, hires, and spends. 

Microsoft's mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond. 

Role Overview 

The Executive Events and Programs Lead will shape and deliver experiences, plus strategic programs for Microsoft AIX executives, employees and stakeholders. This director-level employee will lead a global portfolio of internal and external executive events, build programs that strengthen the employee experience, and help define the organization’s culture through the eyes of its employees, while ensuring our stakeholders are on the journey with us. This role will help drive the strategic vision with operational excellence, translating business priorities into experiences and programs that increase leadership and employee engagement, organizational connection, and employee advocacy. 

 

AI Experiences employees who live within a 50- mile commute of a designated Microsoft Hub in the U.S. are expected to work from the office at least four days per week. This expectation is subject to local law and may vary by jurisdiction.
