The CISO organization represents the voice of the customer and the executive security buyer, focusing on enterprise security strategy, risk posture, and real-world security needs across industries. This team partners closely with product and engineering to ensure Microsoft Security solutions align with how organizations actually defend against threats, translating complex security challenges into actionable priorities and influencing how security is delivered at scale. It plays a critical role in shaping end-to-end security narratives, aligning product capabilities with customer outcomes, and driving trust with executives making high-stakes security decisions. 

CyberShield is the Microsoft Red Team program that extends our red team capability beyond Microsoft’s own estate to select external customers. Our mandate is to shift red teaming from point-in-time, human-led engagements to a software-driven, continuous model powered by agentic, AI-driven red teaming. CyberShield works across Microsoft and customer environments spanning cloud, identity, network, endpoint, hardware, and operational security domains.

We are looking for Senior and Principal Security Software Engineers to design and build the offensive platform, tooling, and capabilities that power CyberShield operations. You will partner with red team operators and security engineers to automate adversary tactics, techniques, and procedures; develop capabilities for autonomous reconnaissance, vulnerability discovery, exploitation, and post-exploitation; and turn emerging tradecraft into reliable systems that operate across Microsoft and customer environments. These roles will focus on one or more of the following areas: exploit development, implant development, and agent platform development. You will provide technical leadership across disciplines, mentor other engineers, and translate operational lessons into scalable capabilities that improve how CyberShield discovers and demonstrates security risk.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond. 
 


Responsibilities
  • Analyze data from Microsoft and customer engagement environments to identify potential security weaknesses and breach points, then partner with operational teams to execute targeted attacks that simulate real-world threat scenarios.
  • Design and build offensive tooling, implants, and agent-platform capabilities that automate reconnaissance, vulnerability discovery, exploitation, post-exploitation, and adversary emulation across Microsoft and customer environments.
  • Develop tools and techniques to scale and accelerate offensive emulation and vulnerability discovery
  • Analyze simulated adversary tactics and communications, enriching our defensive tactics and threat intelligence
  • Advocate for security change through building partnerships and clearly communicating impact of risks
  • Mentor and Guide more Software Engineers as they develop their skills and abilities
  • Successfully operate in uncertain and novel environments, and identify unknown risk areas


Qualifications

Required qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science or related technical field AND 4+ years technical engineering experience with coding in languages including, but not limited to, C, C++, C#, Java, JavaScript, or Python 
    • OR equivalent experience.


Other Requirements:
  • Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings:
    • Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft Cloud Background Check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter. 

 

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Master's Degree in Computer Science or related technical field AND 8+ years technical engineering experience with coding in languages including, but not limited to, C, C++, C#, Java, JavaScript, or Python 
    • OR Bachelor's Degree in Computer Science or related technical field AND 12+ years technical engineering experience with coding in languages including, but not limited to, C, C++, C#, Java, JavaScript, or Python 
    • OR equivalent experience.
  • 3+ years experience performing red team security assessments or red team adjacent role
  • 3+ years experience with cloud technologies such as Azure, AWS, GCP

Are you excited by the opportunity to help organizations get more value from technology while building a career in customer success? As a Customer Success Account Manager (CSAM) on the Americas Customer Success Consumption Excellence team, you will support established Americas customers with significant potential to expand their use of cloud and AI technologies. Many are earlier in their transformation journey, giving you the opportunity to engage at a pivotal stage, strengthen solution health, accelerate Azure and AI adoption, and help customers turn ambitious priorities into measurable business value and scalable long-term success.  

You will learn how Microsoft partners with customers, work alongside experienced account CSAMs, and contribute directly to customer programs and reviews. With coaching and clear playbooks, you will build stakeholder relationships, coordinate delivery activities, track progress, surface risks, and help customers achieve meaningful business outcomes. 

You do not need to arrive with prior professional experience or as a fully developed customer success expert. This role is designed to help you grow through structured onboarding, hands-on learning, mentoring, regular feedback, and increasing responsibility as your confidence, technical knowledge, and customer skills develop. 

 

To prepare for the role, you will be enrolled in the Early-in-Profession (EiP) Program. This program exemplifies the company’s commitment to developing early-career talent through robust onboarding and mentorship. These programs are designed to accelerate new hires’ productivity, integrate them into Microsoft’s culture, and set them on a path for long-term growth within the company. Participants in EiP benefit from a comprehensive onboarding experience that includes immersive training, structured job shadowing with colleagues, and continuous support from dedicated mentors. By investing heavily in the first six months of a new employee’s tenure, Microsoft ensures its early-in-career hires build essential skills, confidence, and professional networks that will enable them to excel.  



Responsibilities

Build customer relationships 

  • Learn how to engage customers, partners, and internal stakeholders and adapt your communication to different audiences and technical levels. 

  • Build foundational relationships with customer stakeholders and technical professionals, supported by experienced colleagues and account team leaders. 

  • Look beyond immediate support needs to understand each customer’s business objectives, technology roadmap, priorities, and opportunities for greater value. 

Help customers achieve success 

  • Support customer success planning, customer-facing reviews, engagement prioritization, and conversations with technical stakeholders. 

  • Learn Microsoft delivery methods, processes, and tools while helping assess operational health and turn customer priorities into actionable programs of work. 

  • Help identify and address customer blockers, including security and compliance risks, by connecting customers with the right Microsoft solutions, services, and expertise. 

  • Coordinate delivery resources, contribute to internal program reviews, and support clear, timely communication when issues need escalation. 

Connect customer priorities to Microsoft solutions 

  • Listen to customer conversations and help connect their goals with Microsoft technologies, services, and the current portfolio of work in their account. 

  • Develop your understanding of customer success strategy, Microsoft technology, and the business and technical changes customers are working to achieve. 

  • Participate in account-team planning and help connect Customer Success Plans with broader account priorities and deliverable programs of work. 

  • Work with account teams to shape practical programs that support adoption, value realization, security, and long-term success. 

Improve customer health and delivery quality 

  • Support account CSAMs in helping customers continuously improve the health and reliability of their Microsoft solutions by using available resources, support services, and proven practices. 

  • Support customer success and cloud-consumption planning through regular, well-prepared communication with customer and Microsoft stakeholders. 

  • Coordinate people and resources, follow quality standards, and help deliver a consistent customer experience that turns plans into measurable value. 

  • Track risks, dependencies, decisions, and commitments; raise concerns early and help teams maintain momentum through resolution. 

Grow your AI technical knowledge and influence 

  • Build technical aptitude and industry awareness so you can translate customer conversations into clear business impact and value. 

  • Bring curiosity and creativity to the design and execution of inclusive customer programs, services, and success initiatives. 

  • Learn to influence through collaboration by bringing together the right people, communicating clearly, and helping diverse teams move toward shared outcomes.

Bachelor's Degree in Business, Sociology, Psychology, Computer Science or related field OR equivalent experience.

Additional or preferred qualifications

  • Microsoft or competitor equivalent (e.g., AWS) certification in relevant technologies (e.g., Azure, 365).
  • Exposure to customer planning, project coordination, technology, data analysis, service delivery, or stakeholder communication in any academic, community, or professional setting.

Overview

Microsoft is building the next generation of agentic experiences, where customers can extend Copilot with trusted agents, plugins, skills, connectors, and tools. The opportunity is to make these capabilities easy to find, understand, acquire, and use wherever customers work, while giving developers and partners a clear path to reach Microsoft audiences at scale. 

We are seeking a Principal Product Manager to define and lead the product strategy for the Agent & Plugin Store and its evolution into a broader registry-powered discovery, distribution, and growth platform. This role will shape a unified Agent and Plugin Store across Microsoft Copilot experiences, extend marketplace discovery beyond any single product surface, and establish a compelling web-facing marketplace experience for plugins and agentic solutions. 

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.



Responsibilities

  • Define the multi-year product vision, strategy, and roadmap for a unified Agent & Plugin Store spanning Microsoft Copilot experiences and relevant standalone marketplace entry points. 

  • Lead the evolution from a single store experience to a registry-powered discovery and distribution platform for agents, plugins, skills, connectors, and related extensibility solutions. 

  • Drive a coherent customer model for discovering, evaluating, acquiring, sharing, managing, and reusing agentic capabilities across supported Microsoft experiences. 

  • Create a web-facing plugins marketplace experience that expands ecosystem reach, supports public discovery, and provides clear pathways into Microsoft Copilot experiences. 

  • Shape end-to-end marketplace experiences including information architecture, search, ranking, recommendations, categories, collections, product detail pages, acquisition, re-entry, and lifecycle management. 

  • Define the unified plugin and agent marketplace model, ensuring underlying capabilities can be packaged and presented as coherent customer solutions rather than fragmented technical components. 

  • Establish the product strategy for cross-surface distribution so publishers can reach multiple Microsoft experiences and customers can discover and acquire solutions through consistent flows. 

  • Own the growth strategy and experimentation roadmap across supply, discovery, acquisition, activation, sharing, engagement, retention, and repeat usage. 

  • Define a marketplace measurement framework and use usage, quality, relevance, reliability, and customer feedback signals to improve search, recommendations, merchandising, and product investment decisions. 

  • Partner with engineering, design, data science, research, business development, store operations, developer platform, governance, and Copilot product teams to deliver an integrated marketplace ecosystem. 

  • Align senior stakeholders around durable product decisions, resolve cross-organizational dependencies and tradeoffs, and communicate strategy and progress with clarity. 

  • Represent the needs of end users, administrators, developers, makers, ISVs, and Microsoft product teams while maintaining a simple and coherent customer experience. 

Key product outcomes 

  • A unified Agent & Plugin Store experience across Microsoft Copilot surfaces, with consistent concepts and customer journeys. 

  • A registry-powered discovery and distribution model that connects publishers, Microsoft experiences, and customers through a shared marketplace foundation. 

  • A compelling marketplace that broadens discovery and ecosystem reach for plugins and agentic solutions. 

  • A clear plugin product model that brings agents, skills, connectors, MCP capabilities, and other supported components together into customer-centered solutions. 

  • Measurable growth in marketplace supply, discovery, acquisition, activation, engagement, sharing, and sustained usage. 

  • Improved relevance through high-quality search, ranking, recommendations, curated collections, and personalized discovery. 

  • A scalable operating model for onboarding new artifact types, marketplace partners, Copilot surfaces, and distribution scenarios. 



Qualifications
  • Bachelor's Degree AND 8+ years experience in product/service/program management or software development
    • OR equivalent experience.
  • Bachelor's Degree AND 12+ years experience in product/service/program management or software development
    • OR equivalent experience.
  • 4+ years experience taking a product, feature, or experience to market (e.g., design, addressing product market fit, and launch, internal tool/framework).
  • 6+ years experience improving product metrics for a product, feature, or experience in a market (e.g., growing customer base, expanding customer usage, avoiding customer churn).
  • 6+ years experience disrupting a market for a product, feature, or experience (e.g., competitive disruption, taking the place of an established competing product).
  • Experience defining and delivering large-scale consumer, enterprise, marketplace, platform, ecosystem, or developer products.
  • Demonstrated ability to create a product vision, translate it into a roadmap, and drive execution across multiple teams and organizational boundaries.
  • Solid product sense for discovery, marketplace, search, recommendations, acquisition, engagement, and growth experiences.
  • Experience using qualitative and quantitative insights to identify opportunities, prioritize investments, and measure customer and business outcomes.
  • Ability to operate effectively in ambiguous, fast-moving environments and turn complex technical and organizational constraints into simple customer experiences.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to influence senior leaders and build alignment across engineering, design, business, and partner organizations.  
  • Experience with AI agents, plugins, skills, connectors, MCP, developer ecosystems, app stores, SaaS marketplaces, or enterprise software distribution.
  • Experience building platform capabilities that serve multiple first-party and third-party product experiences.
  • Experience with product-led growth, marketplace flywheels, experimentation, funnel optimization, and recommendation or relevance systems.
  • Understanding of enterprise discovery, entitlement, administration, trust, governance, and lifecycle considerations for extensibility ecosystems.
  • Experience leading products that span native application experiences and public web destinations.

Overview

Microsoft runs one of the largest and most complex cloud estates in the world. The Infrastructure Exposure Management (IEM) team in the Microsoft CISO organization finds and measures security risk in Microsoft's cloud infrastructure, then drives the work to reduce it across the company's corporate environment and its many production tenants.

We're looking for a Principal Technical Program Manager to lead the team that drives this work. You will have a team of program managers and service engineers and own the strategy and roadmap for cloud security posture management (CSPM) at Microsoft. You will work with engineering, security, Azure and M365 service teams to make sure exposure findings lead to real, measurable risk reduction.



Responsibilities
  • Lead and grow the team:
    Hire, coach and develop a high-performing team of program managers, and build an inclusive, accountable team culture.
  • Own the CSPM strategy:
    Set the vision, roadmap and success metrics for exposure management across corporate and production tenants. That includes coverage, control definitions, portfolio of scanner tools, how findings are prioritized, and posture reporting.
  • Drive large programs across many teams:
    Lead efforts that span several organizations, such as onboarding new tenants and resource types, near-real-time posture assessment, and bringing several security signals together into one prioritized view. Work with Microsoft Security product teams to drive enterprise security requirements into product capabilities.
  • Drive remediation:
    Partner with engineering and service owners to turn findings into action through scorecards, governance and escalation. Balance security rigor against the cost and friction it puts on engineering teams.
  • Run the operating rhythm:
    Own OKRs, KPIs, executive reviews and exception and risk-acceptance processes, and make sure the data behind them is trustworthy.
  • Represent the program to leadership:
    Explain complex technical risk clearly to senior leaders and influence decisions across the company.
  • Champion AI-first work:
    Use AI and automation to speed up control authoring, triage and posture insights.


Qualifications

Required/minimum qualifications

  • Bachelor's Degree AND 6+ years experience in engineering, product/technical program management, data analysis, or product development
    • OR equivalent experience.
  • 1+ year(s) project or people management experience.
  • 3+ years of experience managing cross-functional and/or cross-team projects.
Other Requirements
  • Ability to meet Microsoft, customer and/or government security screening requirements are required for this role. These requirements include, but are not limited to the following specialized security screenings: Microsoft Cloud Background Check: This position will be required to pass the Microsoft background and Microsoft Cloud background check upon hire/transfer and every two years thereafter.

Additional or preferred qualifications

  • Bachelor's Degree AND 12+ years experience engineering, product/technical program management, data analysis, or product development
    • OR equivalent experience.
  • 4+ years people management experience.
  • 8+ years of experience managing cross-functional and/or cross-team projects.
  • 1+ year(s) of experience reading and/or writing code (e.g., sample documentation, product demos).
  • Experience leading large, technically complex programs across multiple teams with measurable results.
  • Hands-on knowledge of public cloud infrastructure (Azure, AWS or GCP) and security posture concepts such as configuration baselines, CSPM, and vulnerability or exposure management.
  • Foundational understanding of security - core principles, threat modeling, applied cryptography, security protocols, etc.
  • Experience running CSPM, CNAPP or exposure management programs in a large or multi-tenant enterprise.
  • Familiarity with CIS Benchmarks, NIST CSF, the Microsoft Cloud Security Benchmark and attack-path-based risk prioritization.
  • Track record of defining executive-level security metrics and driving remediation across many teams.
  • Experience applying AI/LLM-based automation to security or engineering workflows.

In addition, you will also perform troubleshooting and diagnostics on equipment, as well as perform hardware decommissions for simple changes and refreshes following Standard Operating Procedures. This opportunity will allow you to deepen your understanding of Data Center standard processes and procedures, develop mentoring skills while providing guidance to peers, familiarizing yourself with security and data management procedures, and accelerate your career growth in the process.

As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development of all employees and offers training and growth opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion training and events, and professional certifications.

Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.

The Windows Servicing and Delivery (WSD) organization is responsible for delivering protected, productive, and predictable servicing experiences for Windows customers around the world. As security threats evolve and engineering systems grow in scale and complexity, WSD is investing in intelligent automation, large-scale quality analytics, and AI-powered validation platforms that improve the speed, quality, transparency, and reliability of the monthly security fixes delivered across the Windows ecosystem. 

The Validation team plays a critical role in validating Windows servicing releases, including the monthly security fixes shipped to customers. The team develops and operates modern validation platforms, automation frameworks, telemetry systems, and AI-powered engineering solutions that help identify regressions, quantify release quality, and reduce deployment risk across consumer, enterprise, cloud, and original equipment manufacturer (OEM) environments. 

Our mission is to help engineering teams make better release decisions faster through trusted validation signals, actionable insights, scalable automation, durable platform services, and responsible use of AI technologies. By transforming validation from a collection of isolated tests into an intelligent engineering platform, we help ensure that monthly Windows security releases meet rigorous standards for reliability, security, and customer quality. 

As a Software Engineer on the Validation team, you will contribute to software, services, automation systems, and AI-enabled solutions that improve validation effectiveness, engineering productivity, and the quality of monthly Windows security releases. 

You will work with experienced engineers, validation specialists, and cross-functional partners to design, implement, test, deploy, and maintain cloud services, automation frameworks, telemetry pipelines, quality analytics platforms, and agent-based engineering experiences used to assess release readiness and security-fix quality. 

This role provides an opportunity to build expertise in cloud-native services, engineering productivity systems, AI-assisted development workflows, large-scale reliability analysis, and modern validation technologies while helping deliver monthly Windows security updates at global scale. 

In this role, you will help modernize how the quality of Windows security fixes is validated and measured at scale. Your contributions will improve validation efficiency, strengthen confidence in monthly security releases, accelerate issue detection, and help deliver secure, reliable, and high-quality Windows updates to customers around the world.

Validation Platform Engineering

With a vision to build and sell Microsoft AI‑powered platforms, cloud services, and devices through a rich partner ecosystem, the Windows and Device Sales (WDS) organization brings together sales, technical expertise, and partners to help customers achieve real business outcomes with Microsoft technology.

 

WDS plays a critical role in shaping and delivering the endpoint platform that powers modern, secure, and AI‑enabled work. WDS works across Microsoft’s commercial ecosystem, including OEMs, silicon partners, distributors, resellers, and services partners - to drive Windows platform adoption, protect and grow share, and ensure customers realize long‑term value from their device and endpoint investments.

  

This role contributes to a multi‑billion‑dollar business and plays a direct role in defending and expanding Windows as the enterprise endpoint platform, enabling customers to modernize their environments, adopt AI‑driven workflows, and build confidence in Windows as the foundation for future innovation.

 

As a Windows Specialist, you will defend and grow Windows within Microsoft’s largest and most strategic customers. You will help them define and modernize their endpoint strategy in an era shaped by AI, security threats, and rapid platform competition. You will operate as a trusted advisor to senior IT and business leaders - anchoring engagement with the CIO while expanding influence across CTO, CISO, and AI transformation leaders - to ensure Windows remains the foundational platform for secure, AI‑driven work.

 

In this role, you will lead high‑impact, time‑bound customer engagements where Windows platform decisions are at risk or strategically critical. You will articulate differentiated Windows value across security, resiliency, management, and AI workloads; orchestrate partners and internal teams to deliver proof and outcomes; and convert lighthouse wins into repeatable evidence that scales across industries and partners.

 

This opportunity will allow you to deepen executive‑level consultative skills, build technical and platform credibility across the Windows ecosystem, and play a visible role in protecting and expanding Microsoft’s commercial footprint in priority accounts.

 

 

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more.   • Demonstrated capability and experience in leading technical and executive‑level customer conversations, translating complex platform concepts into clear, outcome‑oriented guidance for CIO, CTO, CISO, and AI transformation leaders.

Overview

The Microsoft 365 Core Copilot Infrastructure team is hiring a Principal Product Manager for its Capacity Management team, the group that puts the right AI infrastructure in the right places at the right time to power Copilot across Microsoft 365. The team plans, delivers, and scales the GPU and CPU fleet behind the M365 LLM platform, and it helps direct significant capacity investment each year. This is a broad role for a platform thinker with a strong customer mindset—someone who wants to move across the charter and take on the biggest open problems rather than hold a single fixed area.

The work spans demand forecasting, capacity investment planning, platform and hardware strategy, supply and demand balancing, capacity intake and delivery, and model onboarding and migration. AI growth is reshaping all of it. Demand is larger and less predictable than it has ever been, hardware and model choices carry more weight, and the cost of getting capacity wrong scales with the fleet. You will help the team decide where to invest, when to build, what to run it on, and how to keep the platform healthy and efficient as it grows—always anchored in what our Copilot customers and partner teams need.

This is an AI-first product management role. You will use agents, automation, and AI-driven analysis alongside standard PM tools to read telemetry, model tradeoffs, prototype solutions, and reach decisions faster. You will translate hard technical and financial tradeoffs into terms leaders can act on, and you will help move the team toward AI-forward ways of working, including evaluation sets and agent-based workflows built into how the work gets done.

You will partner closely with engineering leaders, architects, data scientists, finance, and supply chain across Microsoft. The role carries broad visibility and influence, and it depends on strong product sense, technical depth, data fluency, customer empathy, and clear judgment under uncertainty. As a senior leader on the team, you will also mentor other product managers and raise the bar for how the team works.

This position is based in Redmond, Washington and requires the employee be in the office a minimum of 3 days per week.

Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.



Responsibilities

  • Shape the strategy for the capacity and platform work that matters most across M365 Copilot and turn that direction into a roadmap teams can execute.

  • Take on high-impact problems across the charter, including capacity intake and planning, supply and demand balancing, buildout to SLA, GPU utilization and platform health, and model onboarding and migration, and drive them to a result.

  • Bring a strong customer mindset—partner with Copilot scenario teams to understand their needs and translate them into platform capabilities and capacity investments.

  • Use AI-driven analysis of demand signals, telemetry, and operational data to forecast more accurately, catch capacity and reliability issues early, and fix them at the root.

  • Use agents, automation, and AI Ops to analyze data, coordinate work, and act on what you learn—turning manual, ticket-driven intake and allocation into intelligent, self-service systems.

  • Model capacity and hardware tradeoffs with AI prototyping and scenario testing before committing investment, paired with solid product, engineering, and financial judgment.

  • Weigh cost, performance, and reliability against each other, and prioritize multi-year capacity investments with partners across engineering, finance, and supply chain.

  • Advance platform, model, and hardware transition strategy, and help the platform run more efficiently as AI workloads grow.

  • Set success metrics, OKRs (Objectives and Key Results), and KPIs (key performance indicators), and shape investment priorities with leadership.

  • Explain complex technical and financial tradeoffs to executives in a way that leads to decisions.

  • Mentor other product managers on the team, grow their capabilities, and move the team toward better, AI-forward ways of working.

  • Bachelor's Degree AND 8+ years experience in product/service/program management or software development
    • OR equivalent experience.

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Bachelor's Degree AND 12+ years experience in product/service/program management or software development
    • OR equivalent experience.
  • 4+ years experience taking a product, feature, or experience to market (e.g., design, addressing product market fit, and launch, internal tool/framework).
  • 6+ years experience improving product metrics for a product, feature, or experience in a market (e.g., growing customer base, expanding customer usage, avoiding customer churn).
  • 6+ years experience disrupting a market for a product, feature, or experience (e.g., competitive disruption, taking the place of an established competing product).
  • Proven ability to think at the platform level while keeping a strong customer mindset—translating customer and partner needs into durable platform capabilities.
  • Experience taking on ambiguous, high-stakes work and driving it from strategy through execution across organizations.
  • Experience leading large-scale cloud infrastructure, capacity planning, or distributed systems work, with grasp of hyperscale service delivery.
  • Experience with LLMs, model-serving platforms, GPU capacity planning, or large-scale AI-powered products.
  • AI fluency, including using AI agents, automation, and prototyping to speed up analysis, decisions, and product work.
  • Experience using telemetry, demand signals, and operational data to guide platform and investment decisions.
  • Experience mentoring and developing product managers and technical leaders.
  • Systems-level problem solving and clear communication, with the ability to influence senior leaders and align stakeholders across organizations.

The Missiles Manufacturing Engineering team at Anduril is dedicated to rewriting the playbook for precision strike and deterrent capabilities. Modern threats demand a paradigm shift in how tactical weapons are designed and produced, and our team is rapidly scaling production to deliver the unprecedented volume, speed, and affordability that U.S. and Allied forces require.
 
On this team, you will have the opportunity to work on groundbreaking programs like our Barracuda family of air-breathing missiles—including all of its highly adaptable sub-variants—as well as cutting-edge hypersonic missile systems and a pipeline of next-generation strike technologies. As a Manufacturing Engineer, you will own the production lifecycle of one of these critical weapons systems, driving high-rate assembly lines and leading rapid production ramps from prototype to scale.

In this role, you will be deeply embedded in the entire lifecycle of these state-of-the-art systems, bridging the gap between initial design and physical production. You will have the autonomy to take on massive, complex projects and own them from cradle to grave. We are looking for engineers with a fierce sense of ownership and an insatiable drive to push their technical boundaries. If you thrive in the face of ambiguity, welcome the challenge of complex engineering problems, and are excited to step outside of your comfort zone to build the future of defense, this is the place for you.
Your work will directly reshape global deterrence and change the balance of defense capabilities on a global scale. Apply now and become part of our mission to secure a safer tomorrow.


ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Manufacturing Engineer on the High-Speed Missiles team, you will be at the absolute bleeding edge of aerospace and defense technology. Hypersonic flight—sustained travel at speeds of Mach 5 and beyond—represents one of the most demanding engineering challenges of our time. To survive these extreme environments, our vehicles must withstand intense thermal, aerodynamic, and structural forces.

Historically, hypersonic systems have been built like low-volume, bespoke science projects. At Anduril, we are changing that. Your mission is to bridge the gap between cutting-edge physics and high-rate industrial output. You will be the bridge between design and production, transforming highly complex, next-generation hypersonic vehicles into manufacturable, repeatable, and scalable products. This is a high-impact, high-ownership role. You will not just be maintaining a pre-existing assembly line; you will be architecting the future of hypersonic production from the ground up.


WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Own the Production Line: Design, commission, and continuously optimize the assembly lines, work cells, and floor layouts for our hypersonic missile programs.
  • Bridge Design and Manufacturing: Collaborate intimately with design engineers during the early development phases to drive Design for Manufacturing (DFM) and Design for Assembly (DFA), ensuring the vehicle is optimized for high-rate production.
  • Pioneer Advanced Processes: Develop and scale manufacturing processes for exotic materials, advanced composite structures, thermal protection systems (TPS), and high-performance propulsion integration (such as rocket motors and air-breathing engines).
  • Design Tooling & Equipment: Architect, procure, and qualify custom assembly tooling, fixtures, and automated assembly equipment to increase throughput and quality.
  • Drive From Prototype to Rate: Lead the transition of hardware from first-article prototyping through Low-Rate Initial Production (LRIP) and into mature, high-rate manufacturing.
  • Solve Complex Shop-Floor Challenges: Act as the first line of defense for the manufacturing floor, rapidly troubleshooting and resolving complex engineering and production anomalies.
  • Author Technical Standards: Create and maintain work instructions, manufacturing bills of materials (MBOMs), routing, and quality documentation.

 

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Educational Background: B.S. or M.S. in Mechanical, Aerospace, Manufacturing, Industrial Engineering, a related STEM discipline or equivalent work experience.
  • Proven NPI Track Record: Direct, hands-on experience in at least one of the following capacities:
    • Owning a clean-sheet design/New Product Introduction (NPI) product from cradle to grave.
    • Owning a complex manufacturing process from cradle to grave across multiple products.
    • Owning a high-impact product from cradle to grave across multiple manufacturing processes.
  • Extreme Autonomy & Self-Sufficiency: A proven "drop-in" operator with a strong bias for action. You require minimal oversight, and you thrive in ambiguous environments by proactively hunting down information (digging into BOMs, driving design partners, and holding schedules accountable).
  • Early-Stage DFM/DFA: Strong experience collaborating with design engineering in the earliest phases of development to provide aggressive Design for Manufacturing (DFM) and Design for Assembly (DFA) feedback.
  • Production Infrastructure & Tooling Ownership: Proven ability to build a manufacturing footprint from scratch. This includes designing and setting up physical work centers, establishing factory layouts, authoring work instructions, designing or sourcing custom tooling and fixtures, and procuring capital equipment.
  • Travel: Willingness to travel occasionally (<10%) to support global manufacturing operations.
  • U.S. Person Status: Must be a U.S. Person due to required access to U.S. export-controlled information or facilities.
  • Clearance Status: Eligible to obtain and maintain an active U.S. Security clearance.
  • YoE: 8+ years of experience working in manufacturing or related field.

 

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Hypersonics Experience: Direct experience working on hypersonic vehicles, scramjets, rocket propulsion, thermal protection systems (TPS), or high-temperature structures/materials is highly valued.
  • Aerospace & Defense Domain Expertise: Experience working on complex aerospace systems, tactical missiles, launch vehicles, satellites, or high-performance automotive platforms.
  • High-Rate Scaling: Experience transitioning a highly complex hardware product from low-volume prototyping/LRIP (Low-Rate Initial Production) into automated, high-rate manufacturing.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The Maritime team at Anduril builds world-class autonomous maritime platforms - undersea and surface vehicles and systems and seabed sensors. The team is responsible for taking products like Dive-LD, Dive-XL, Copperhead, and Seabed Sentry from concept to operational systems. As part of this team, your role will involve building the Product Operations function within a larger deployment and sustainment group. We work in close coordination with specialist teams including engineering, program management, and field operations to ensure successful employment of these products and to advance the state-of-the-possible in subsea robotics.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Product Operations Manager for Maritime, you will play a critical role in ensuring the reliability and readiness of Anduril’s Maritime products. This family of intelligent, autonomous undersea systems work together to develop unmatched situational awareness, precision engagement, and scalable maritime dominance. You will be an integral piece to ensuring that Anduril meets this mission for our customers. In this role, you will support end users by building field failure discovery, mitigation, and resolution processes. You will identify failure modes that contribute to root cause analysis, and you will help deploy fixes and manage the incident lifecycle across the Maritime fleet. This position requires a strong problem-solving mindset and hands-on expertise in debugging and resolving complex electromechanical issues. If you are passionate about cutting-edge technology, advancing national security, and delivering best-in-class operational support, Anduril invites you to join the team.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Lead Product Operations: Guide and mentor a high-performing Product Operations team, setting the standard for how we triage, diagnose, and resolve technical incidents across our global Maritime fleet.
  • Drive Fleet Reliability: Partner directly with software and hardware engineering teams to translate real-world field telemetry and failure data into permanent system upgrades and design improvements.
  • Analyze System Telemetry: Oversee the collection and analysis of fleet health data using advanced data-driven tools, helping to predict and prevent failures before they happen.
  • Bridge the Gap: Act as the critical translator between deeply technical engineering teams, business development stakeholders, and military operators in the field.
  • Customer & Mission Support: Ensure exceptional technical support for our global users, managing communications around high-priority incidents and driving them to rapid resolution.
  • Build the Playbook: Standardize and scale our sustainment operations, creating the processes that will support Maritime as the fleet grows exponentially worldwide.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Proven Technical Leadership: 6+ years of professional experience managing, mastering, and supporting complex technical systems (maritime, aerospace, robotics, automotive, defense, or electromechanical systems).
  • Education: Bachelor's degree in a technical or related field, OR equivalent hands-on military, maritime, or industrial technical experience.
  • Problem-Solving Mindset: A proven ability to navigate ambiguous situations and lead teams through complex, unstructured technical challenges.
  • Leadership & Mentorship: Experience managing, coaching, or leading technical teams, with a focus on professional development and operational excellence.
  • Clearance & Location: Eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret Security clearance, and based in (or willing to relocate to) Quincy, MA
  • Travel: Ability to travel as needed to support customer operations and test events.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

We recognize that great leaders come from diverse backgrounds. We do not expect you to meet every single one of these criteria:

  • Experience supporting and/or deploying undersea munitions, vehicles, or unmanned undersea systems (UUVs) as a DoD contractor or military end-user.
  • Familiarity with conventional naval systems or military naval operations.
  • Hands-on experience with Linux command-line interfaces (CLI).
  • Familiarity with modern observability and ticketing tools (such as Grafana, Jira, or Git).
  • Experience leveraging data analytics (such as SQL or Palantir Foundry) to conduct trend analysis and drive business decisions.
  • Prior military, DoD civilian, or government agency experience.
  • A background in technical project management or operations consulting.

ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Product Operations Technical Specialist for Maritime, you will play an important role in ensuring the reliability and readiness of Anduril’s Maritime products. This family of intelligent, autonomous undersea systems work together to develop unmatched situational awareness, precision engagement, and scalable maritime dominance. You will be an integral piece to ensuring that Anduril meets this mission for our customers. In this role you will help support end users by following and improving field failure discovery, mitigation, and resolution processes. You will help identify failure modes that contribute to root cause analysis, and you will help deploy fixes and manage the incident lifecycle across the Maritime fleet. This position requires a strong problem-solving mindset and hands-on expertise in debugging and resolving complex electromechanical issues. If you are passionate about cutting-edge technology, advancing national security, and delivering best-in-class operational support, Anduril invites you to join the team.

WHAT YOU’LL DO

  • Own Incident Triage and Resolution: Be the first technical responder for issues across our global Maritime fleet. Dig into logs, telemetry, and system state to isolate faults across software, hardware, and network boundaries, and drive incidents to resolution.
  • Keep Customers Operational: When a full engineering fix will take time, identify and deploy interim mitigations and workarounds so customers can keep operating, while you manage the permanent fix in parallel.
  • Analyze Fleet Telemetry: Pull, query, and analyze fleet health data and logs yourself to spot trends, predict failures, and prevent issues before they reach the customer.
  • Drive Fleet Reliability: Partner directly with software and hardware engineering teams to turn real-world field data and failure analysis into permanent system upgrades and design improvements.
  • Bridge the Gap: Act as the critical translator between deeply technical engineering teams, business development stakeholders, and military operators in the field, explaining complex issues clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences.
  • Help Build the Playbook: Turn what you learn on real incidents into repeatable triage procedures, diagnostic tooling, and runbooks that scale as the Maritime fleet grows worldwide.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

  • Education: Bachelor's degree in a technical or related field, OR equivalent hands-on technical experience (military, maritime, industrial, or field support).
  • Systems Troubleshooting: Hands-on experience troubleshooting software-intensive or networked systems in a production, field, or customer-facing environment (for example: reading logs, isolating faults across software and hardware boundaries, reproducing issues).
  • Command Line and Data Skills: Working proficiency with the Linux command line, and comfort analyzing data beyond spreadsheets (SQL, Python, bash, or similar).
  • Problem-Solving Mindset: A proven ability to work through ambiguous, unstructured technical problems from first principles, including the instinct to deploy interim mitigations and workarounds that keep customers operational while permanent fixes are engineered.
  • Self-Driven: Self-starter with a record of high achievement in multiple domains, who learns new systems by getting hands-on with them.
  • Technical Communication and Collaboration: Ability to communicate and coordinate technical and non-technical efforts across business, engineering, and sustainment functions, influencing decision-making, resource allocation, and operational planning.
  • Clearance and Location: Eligible to obtain and maintain a U.S. Secret security clearance, and based in (or willing to relocate to) Quincy, MA.
  • Travel and Schedule: Ability to travel as needed to support customer operations and test events. Willingness to work non-standard hours and weekends as needed.

  • Experience supporting and/or deploying undersea munitions, vehicles, or unmanned undersea systems (UUVs) as a DoD contractor or military end-user.
  • Familiarity with naval systems or operations, or prior military, DoD civilian, or government agency experience.

In this role, you will contribute to the development, integration, and verification of flight controls and flight autonomy for our Ranger platform. Working alongside experienced GNC engineers, you will take ownership of defined algorithms, simulation components, and test activities that support stable, predictable aircraft performance from takeoff through recovery.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

  • Develop, implement, and test Auto-Taxi and Automatic Take off and Landing algorithms and supporting flight-mode logic.
  • Design and implement inner- and outer-loop flight control laws, guidance algorithms, and control allocation functions for conventional takeoff, wing-borne flight, and landing, with technical guidance and design reviews from senior engineers.
  • Support integration between flight autonomy and mission autonomy through A-GRA-aligned interfaces, implementing and testing command handling, flight-mode transitions, vehicle-status reporting, and contingency responses within the program’s defined architecture.
  • Develop and validate vehicle and subsystem models within an existing high-fidelity six-degree-of-freedom (6DOF) simulation environment, including aerodynamics, mass properties, propulsion, sensors, actuators, and ground-contact dynamics.
  • Execute verification activities, including linear and nonlinear analysis, Monte Carlo campaigns, sensitivity studies, disturbance and degraded-operation testing, and software- and hardware-in-the-loop testing.
  • Analyze simulation, ground-test, and flight-test results to identify discrepancies, investigate root causes, and verify updates to control algorithms and simulation models.
  • Support flight-test preparation and execution through pre-flight performance predictions, test-point analysis, telemetry review, and post-flight reconstruction.
  • Collaborate with propulsion, aerodynamics, actuation, state estimation, embedded software, and autonomy engineers to resolve integration issues. Document designs, assumptions, and test results, and participate in code and technical reviews.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • 2+ years of relevant experience in flight controls, GNC, aircraft simulation, or autonomous aircraft development. Directly relevant graduate research may be considered toward this experience.
  • A strong foundation in aircraft flight dynamics, feedback control, 6DOF equations of motion, coordinate transformations, and numerical methods.
  • Experience performing one or more of the following technical assignments:
  • Vehicle modeling and simulation: Implementing or validating mathematical models of aircraft or subsystem dynamics within a 6DOF simulation.
  • Control law design and allocation: Developing or evaluating fixed-wing control laws, actuator-command mixing, or control allocation functions.
  • Guidance and trajectory validation: Implementing or testing trajectory validation algorithms, path-following, or flight-mode sequencing algorithms.
  • Verification and test analysis: Performing simulation campaigns, sensitivity studies, test-data analysis, or comparisons between predicted and measured aircraft behavior.
  • Exposure to C++ development environments and implementing and debugging engineering algorithms.
  • Strong problem-solving and communication skills, with the ability to work through defined technical problems, communicate assumptions and limitations, and incorporate feedback from senior engineers.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Exposure to Auto-Taxi or ATOL algorithm development, including evaluation of approach and touchdown performance, crosswind response, runway tracking, go-around behavior, or degraded navigation conditions.
  • Direct experience implementing or testing A-GRA-aligned interfaces or integrating a flight-autonomy system with a separate mission-autonomy provider.
  • Strong C++ skills, including object-oriented development, unit testing, and implementation of algorithms subject to real-time execution constraints.
  • Familiarity with aircraft navigation, air data, altitude sensing, and the effects of sensor errors, latency, and data validity on flight control and ATOL performance.
  • Experience with software- or hardware-in-the-loop environments, Linux-based development, Git, and automated testing or CI/CD pipelines.
  • Exposure to propulsion modeling, including integration of steady-state or transient NPSS models or model outputs into a 6DOF simulation environment.
  • Familiarity with flight safety, airworthiness verification, and preparation of supporting artifacts such as simulation descriptions, verification reports, or flying-qualities analyses.
  • Experience working through iterative development and test cycles, including investigating discrepancies and verifying corrective changes

The Mission Systems Software Engineer will work on developing solutions of a real time system environment to provide mission computing support at the center of an autonomous aircraft with sensor and weapons. This role will work to establish a software architecture for a real time system that operates in a multi-level environment at real time. The role will require work with hardware, software and systems teams to come to a consensus design. This role will focus on development of new systems and software designs from PDR, CoDR, CDR to lab test, flight test and fielding.

WHAT YOU’LL DO:

  • Serve as a software mission systems engineer for a safety- and mission-critical real-time mission-computing system aligned with A-GRA and AMS-GRA principles, profiles, interfaces, and data standards.
  • Define and maintain the end-to-end software architecture, including mission applications, platform services, middleware, operating-system interfaces, hardware-abstraction layers, networking, data distribution, component boundaries, and APIs.
  • Architect for deterministic real-time performance by addressing scheduling, latency, jitter, synchronization, throughput, resource utilization, distributed processing, and CPU/GPU/accelerator allocation.
  • Develop architecture views, interface definitions, data-flow and deployment models, sequence and timing diagrams, resource budgets, trade studies, and technical decision records.
  • Integrate sensors, effectors, communications, navigation, autonomy, mission management, command-and-control, data-processing, and vehicle services in collaboration with hardware, FPGA, cybersecurity, safety, systems, integration, and test teams.
  • Design for mission resilience and assurance through fault detection and isolation, redundancy, graceful degradation, recovery, health monitoring, cybersecurity, airworthiness, certification, and requirements traceability.
  • Establish engineering practices for concurrency, synchronization, memory and resource management, deterministic execution, interface control, configuration management, and predictable component integration.
  • Define and execute verification strategies across HIL/SIL laboratories, simulations, test benches, flight-test environments, and deployed systems using automated, performance, stress, fault-injection, interface, and timing tests.
  • Maintain technical ownership throughout the system lifecycle by evaluating enabling technologies and supplier designs, analyzing performance, managing technical debt and modernization roadmaps, promoting reuse, and communicating architectural decisions.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, Computer Engineering, Systems Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a related technical field.
  • 8+ years of professional software-engineering experience, including 3+ years in software architecture, systems architecture, or technical leadership.
  • Experience developing embedded, distributed, real-time, safety-critical, or mission-critical software systems.
  • Proficiency in C, C++, Rust, or another strongly typed systems-programming language.
  • Strong understanding of real-time software principles, including scheduling, concurrency, synchronization, latency, jitter, memory management, and deterministic execution.
  • Experience with embedded operating systems or RTOSs, middleware, interprocess communication, networking, and data-distribution technologies.
  • Experience defining software architectures, APIs, interface-control documents, data flows, deployment models, and system resource budgets.
  • Experience integrating software with hardware, sensors, communications systems, navigation systems, effectors, or other mission-system components.
  • Experience supporting software through requirements development, design reviews, implementation, integration, verification, system test, and deployment.
  • Working knowledge of systems-engineering processes, requirements management, traceability, configuration management, and verification and validation.
  • Ability to analyze system performance using instrumentation, telemetry, traces, profiling, network captures, timing data, and resource-utilization measurements.
  • Strong cross-functional technical leadership, problem-solving, written communication, and presentation skills.
  • Ability to obtain and maintain a U.S. Department of Defense security clearance; U.S. citizenship may be required for clearance eligibility.

The wireless RFIC team architects, designs, and validates radio transceivers integrated into complex wireless SoCs. Our transceivers have powered wireless connectivity solutions for Apple wearable products, enabling the smallest form factor at the lowest power envelope. You will have the opportunity to do innovative development in transceiver design while working closely with systems and product teams at Apple. In this role, you will lead the RFIC validation and characterization team: set the validation strategy and plan, guide engineers through bring-up, characterization, and calibration development, and serve as the technical owner of RF silicon readiness for our wireless SoCs. You will stay hands-on in the lab and in the test code. Would you like to join us and lead this dynamic team?

Description

In this role, you will be a key leader of our team, delivering end-to-end RF integration solutions for our advanced wireless SoC products.
You will enable the entire product lifecycle, from pre-silicon emulation and design development through mass production.
You will own the critical first bring-up of the RF in our wireless SoCs, final silicon validation, and compliance with rigorous standards.
You will own the validation methodology and schedule across pre-silicon (emulation and simulation-based validation), first silicon, characterization, and the hand-off to production test.
You will report status and risk to design, systems, integration, and program management.
This is a unique opportunity to deepen your technical expertise across both hardware and software domains, including wireless transceiver architecture, RF systems, DSP, embedded systems, and the full productization of world-class products.
Your work will involve hands-on bench testing, debug, and system characterization to ensure our RF IPs meet and exceed performance targets.

Responsibilities

Own test plan development, bring-up preparation and execution: define the validation and characterization plan, coverage and exit criteria for each silicon revision, and track it to closure.
Plan and prioritize the team's work, allocate lab, equipment, and board resources, and keep the schedule realistic against tape-out, bring-up, and production milestones.
Mentor and develop engineers through technical guidance, design and code review, feedback, and growth plans; participate in hiring and interviews.
Drive the bring-up and functional validation of new wireless SoCs, from first silicon to final product.
Establish a clear flow between pre-silicon validation, post-silicon characterization, and ATE test development, so that tests, calibration code and lessons are reused rather than rewritten.
Perform and review hands-on bench testing, characterization, and debug of RF SoC IP, including transmitters, receivers, PLLs, power amplifiers, and ADCs/DACs.
Characterize and optimize key RF performance metrics such as EVM, spectral mask, phase noise, sensitivity, IP3, NF, and ACPR.
Automate RF measurements and data analysis by writing robust scripts (e.g., Python) to control test equipment and the device under test (DUT); define the common automation framework and coding standards for the team.
Design and develop radio calibrations, including algorithm creation and optimization.
Develop and support RF calibration and test routines for ATE mass production environments.
Debug complex chip-level and board-level issues, including desense and EMI problems; act as the escalation point for the hardest issues and drive root cause across design, systems, and integration.
Design external matching networks to optimize transmit (Tx) and receive (Rx) radio performance.
Collaborate with RF Systems, Design, and Integration teams on board layout, test methodology, and calibration programming.
Generate comprehensive RF design verification, characterization, and test reports.
Be the primary interface to RF Design, RF Systems, SoC Integration, Test/ATE, and Product teams; communicate status, risks, and findings to senior management.
Drive continuous improvement of test coverage, measurement accuracy, and turnaround time, and of the supporting documentation and tooling.

Minimum Qualifications

BS and a minimum of 10 years relevant industry experience.
Significant experience in RF test development, hands-on debug, performance characterization, and reporting, including ownership of a validation effort through at least one silicon bring-up.
Demonstrated technical leadership: leading a project or a small team, mentoring engineers, and driving cross-functional work to completion.
Strong scripting and automation skills in Python (highly desired), Perl, TCL, C++, or similar languages.
Hands-on experience with standard RF test equipment, including network analyzers, spectrum analyzers, vector signal analyzers, and signal generators.
Strong understanding of RF fundamentals, wireless transceiver architectures, and digital communication systems.
Strong knowledge of RF, PLL, and wireless system measurements (e.g., IP3, NF, ACPR, phase noise, lock time).
Experience with RF PCB design, layout, and debug.
Familiarity with RFIC block-level schematics and design/simulation environments.
Excellent written and verbal communication skills, including reporting to senior management.

Preferred Qualifications

Master's or PhD degree in electrical engineering or a related field.
Prior people management or large-scale project management experience, demonstrating strong leadership.
Strong RF background and a solid understanding of RF systems fundamentals.
Experience with wireless standards (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, Thread/802.15.4) and their compliance measurements.
Exposure to RFIC design and simulation/verification, including pre-silicon validation of RF and digital interfaces.
Exposure to SoC design and simulation/verification.
Experience developing production calibration and ATE test flows and handing them over to manufacturing.

At Apple, iCloud Platform Engineering builds the server stack behind Push Notifications, iMessage, FaceTime, iCloud, iCloud Private Relay and Private Cloud Compute (PCC), the backbone of Siri AI and Apple Intelligence. We are looking for an Engineering Manager to lead PCC inference routing. These systems send every inference request to the right compute across a global, multi-region fleet, while keeping latency low, availability high and PCC's privacy guarantees intact.

This is a technically grounded leadership role for someone who thrives at scale, can bring clarity to complex and fast-changing environments, and is energized by building both systems and teams. You'll guide architectural direction, scale operational practices and develop the engineers and leaders who will shape how Apple delivers cloud inference.

Description

Routing LLM inference at Apple's scale takes systems that adapt to changing demand, available capacity and failures while keeping latency low and accelerator utilization high. As the fleet grows across regions and cells, routing must account for capacity and health across the whole fleet, not just a single site. PCC adds a basic architectural requirement: request content stays encrypted outside trusted compute nodes. You'll lead the design of routing and scheduling strategies within this privacy model. Together with inference and security teams, you'll evaluate techniques such as cache-aware request placement and prefill/decode disaggregation. Your scope includes the inference AI gateway layer, where requests are authenticated, metered, prioritized and streamed back to clients, all without exposing request content.

This work has broad reach. Every improvement to routing makes Siri AI and Apple Intelligence faster and more reliable, and makes better use of Apple's inference capacity. In your first year, you'll be expected to grow a high-performing organization, set a clear technical roadmap, and measurably improve routing latency, availability and fleet utilization.

Responsibilities

Direct the recruitment, development, and leadership for engineers and engineering managers responsible for PCC’s inference routing and request scheduling services, fostering an inclusive culture
Establish technical strategy with senior engineers, guiding architectural decisions and complex trade-offs in global traffic management, capacity-aware placement, load balancing, and failover
Translate organizational objectives into actionable roadmaps, execution plans, and measurable results
Oversee delivery of adaptive routing, admission control, prioritization, and overload management to maintain service responsiveness and share capacity fairly across competing workloads
Evolve inference AI gateway capabilities, including —including authentication, token-aware rate limiting and quotas, model and version routing, fallback and retries, and streaming response delivery—operating on request metadata to preserve end-to-end encryption
Collaborate with model serving and infrastructure leaders to assess prefill/decode disaggregation and cache locality optimizations within PCC’s privacy architecture
Develop and scale robust operations through observability, service-level objectives (SLOs), testing, safe deployment, and incident management in partnership with Site Reliability Engineering (SRE)
Enhance efficiency via benchmarking and capacity-aware scheduling, leveraging queueing delay, latency, throughput, and utilization to guide investment
Provide senior leadership with transparent updates on team health, technical risk, and strategic trade-offs, converting complex technical issues into actionable decisions
Partner with Siri AI, Apple Intelligence, infrastructure, security, and SRE teams to deliver well-integrated routing capabilities

Minimum Qualifications

Extensive software engineering experience with a demonstrated track record of leading teams that design, build, and operate large-scale distributed systems in production environments—whether through direct management, indirect oversight, or a combination thereof
Proven ability to recruit, develop, and retain high-performing engineers and leaders
Experience delivering API gateways (preferably inference AI gateways), request routing, load balancing, scheduling, or traffic management systems at scale
Expertise of LLM inference serving, including request routing, KV-cache placement and reuse, prefill/decode disaggregation, and the tradeoffs between latency, throughput and accelerator use
A record of shipping highly reliable systems in high-availability environments, including leading incident management, on-call and reliability practices
Strong technical depth: capable of contributing meaningfully to architectural and design discussions with senior engineers, with a server development background in Java, C/C++, Go or Swift
Ability to drive alignment and execution across teams in complex, matrixed environments
Bachelor’s degree in an engineering discipline or equivalent professional experience

Preferred Qualifications

We are looking for a hands-on Evaluation leader to build and lead a team of applied scientists and machine learning engineers who measure the quality of a new, multi-year Apple initiative. You will join at the start as a key contributor to the evaluation function, working with other eval leaders to establish how the team knows the system is correct, relevant, and trustworthy before and after it ships. You will own specific components of the evaluation plan, including methods, datasets, and automated grading systems that turn product behavior into clear quality signals for engineering and executive leadership.

Description

You will lead a team that designs and runs evaluation for a conversational experience that understands what people ask for, finds and ranks the right results, and allows them to complete tasks. Quality in this product spans several layers: interpreting a request correctly, retrieving and ranking the right results, composing a grounded and accurate response, and executing actions correctly through integrations with external partners. You and your team will be key contributors to the overall evaluation plan for this service and will own the evaluation methods for the layers in your area.

Within your components, you will set the technical direction for large language model (LLM) based autograders and rubrics, including rubric design, evaluation set development, validation, and calibration. You will pair these with logging and instrumentation and online experimentation, working alongside the other eval leaders who own different parts of the plan. You will build the roadmap for your components, translate the broader evaluation strategy into concrete methods and deliverables, and make sure your results turn into measurable quality gains and clear inputs to release decisions.

This is a hands-on role. You will review designs and experiments, stay close to the data, and mentor a team of scientists and engineers while you recruit and grow it. You will partner with engineering, applied machine learning, quality assurance, and program management teams, and you will present quality status, risks, and trade-offs for your areas to senior leadership. The product, its architecture, and its quality bar are still taking shape, so you will operate with significant latitude and help shape what "good" and "shippable" mean as the work evolves.

We're looking for someone with a proven track record in:
Building automated grading systems that scale to large, frequently changing datasets and using them to drive
improvements in models and product features.
Defining metrics and evaluation sets that reflect real user behavior and predict real-world quality.
Turning evaluation findings into action by partnering with engineering and applied machine learning teams to diagnose failures and ship fixes.
Contributing evaluation results to release processes as explicit quality gates.
Growing senior individual contributors and technical leads from within a team, and recruiting strong talent in competitive hiring markets

Minimum Qualifications

6+ years of experience in machine learning, data science, or machine learning evaluation, including 3+ years of
direct people management of scientists or engineers.
Track record of hiring, developing, and leading teams of applied scientists, data scientists, or machine learning
engineers.
Hands-on experience building and deploying LLM-based autograders and rubrics, including rubric design, evaluation
set development, validation, and calibration.
Experience evaluating conversational AI, search, recommendation, or ranking systems, using both offline metrics
and online experimentation.
Strong command of statistics and experimental design, including A/B testing and interpreting noisy metrics.
Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, with a track record of influencing engineers and senior leaders

Preferred Qualifications

MS or PhD in Computer Science, Machine Learning, Statistics, or a related quantitative field, or equivalent
experience.
Experience evaluating agentic or tool-use systems that take real-world actions, including multi-turn behavior,
planning, and task completion.
Experience with relevance and ranking evaluation, including graded relevance judgments and ranking metrics.
Experience with groundedness and factuality evaluation of generated responses.

Experience generating and validating synthetic evaluation data.

In Places, we don’t sit back and let things happen, we make things happen, and we do this in service to all Apple employees and customers. Our team is a diverse and nimble group that manages Apple’s corporate and retail workplaces and workplace services. We develop and manage Apple’s global real estate portfolio, lead all related capital construction projects, provide outstanding facilities and site services, develop and lead sustainability initiatives to reduce the environmental impact of all Apple facilities, including commute and renewable energy programs, and do everything we can to ensure the health and safety of all Apple personnel, facilities, and customers in our facilities around the world.
The Critical Facilities Electrical team is responsible for the safe and reliable operation of electrical systems and critical infrastructure across Apple's NorCal Places portfolio. Our preventive program emphasizes early detection, root-cause analysis, and condition-based maintenance to keep mission-critical equipment running. We partner closely with engineering, operations, and capital projects to protect the people and work that depend on our electrical systems.

We are seeking a detail-oriented and safety-driven IR Scanning Electrician to join our team as the dedicated thermographer responsible for infrared inspections of electrical equipment across Apple's NorCal campuses. This role is essential to identifying anomalies before they become failures and to advancing our shift from reactive repair to predictive, condition-based maintenance.

Description

The IR Scanning Electrician will perform infrared thermographic surveys on switchgear, panelboards, transformers, motor control centers, and distribution equipment across Apple's NorCal campuses. They will document findings, prioritize remediation in partnership with the electrical operations team, and contribute to the Critical Facilities Electrical team's predictive maintenance program. The role reports to the Electrical Manager.

Responsibilities

Conduct routine and on-demand infrared thermographic scans on energized electrical equipment in accordance with NFPA 70E.
Identify, classify, and document thermal anomalies, producing inspection reports with severity ratings and recommended corrective actions.
Partner with the electrical operations team to schedule remediation and verify that corrective work resolves identified findings.
Maintain, calibrate, and care for thermal imaging equipment and supporting test gear.
Track scan history, findings, and trends in the team's reporting system to support condition-based decisions.
Support root-cause analysis on electrical incidents and near-misses, contributing thermal data and field observations.
Contribute to an inclusive environment through respecting each other's differences and maintaining curiosity to learn.
Foster and maintain excellent relationships with various stakeholders.

Minimum Qualifications

5+ years of commercial, industrial, utility, or critical-facilities electrical experience.
Current Level I infrared thermography qualification or certification from a recognized program aligned with an applicable industry standard or employer-approved written practice (e.g., ASNT SNT-TC-1A or equivalent).
Demonstrated experience conducting infrared inspections of energized electrical distribution equipment rated from 120/208 V through 12 kV.
Proficiency in using radiometric thermal-imaging cameras and infrared reporting software.
Ability to accurately interpret thermal patterns while accounting for load, emissivity, reflected temperature, environmental conditions, and equipment construction.
Ability to produce technically accurate, well-organized inspection reports and clearly communicate conditions requiring immediate escalation.
Ability to work independently while following established procedures and coordinating with site operations personnel.
Working knowledge of NFPA 70E electrical safe-work practices.
Ability to read and interpret single-line diagrams, panel schedules, and electrical drawings.
Ability to lift and carry up to 50 lbs and work from ladders or lifts as required.

Preferred Qualifications

Infrared Thermography Level II certification (or higher).
Mission-critical background: Proven track record conducting infrared surveys in high-reliability environments such as enterprise data centers or critical utility infrastructure.
Program development: Hands-on experience establishing or scaling a predictive, condition-based infrared inspection program.
Complex electrical apparatus: In-depth experience assessing switchgear, transformers, uninterruptible power supply (UPS) systems, automatic transfer switches (ATS), busway, and emergency/standby generation systems.

Description

As the PCB Materials Lab Manager, you'll provide daily oversight to a team of characterization engineers (a third-party managed service), steering priorities to keep the lab responsive and delivering results in a timely, dependable manner.
