Meta designs and deploys its own AI systems. MTIA — the Meta Training and Inference Accelerator — is Meta's family of in-house AI accelerator ASICs, running recommendation and ranking workloads in production across Meta's data centers today and expanding into generative AI inference and training as successive silicon generations land. The MTIA Software team is part of the AI & Compute Foundation (ACF) organization within Meta Infrastructure. We build the entire stack a chip vendor would normally supply — compiler and LLVM toolchain, runtime, kernel authoring frameworks and libraries, developer tooling, and deep PyTorch integration — co-designing it with the silicon teams generation over generation. Within that stack, the AI Kernels and Performance Optimization team (KORE) owns the layer where silicon architecture meets arithmetic. Our mission is roofline-level performance and programmability at scale: we design and implement high-performance compute and communication kernels (GEMM, attention variants, normalization, collectives, elementwise and reduction fusions, sparse and quantized paths) against novel architectural features including matrix engines, on-chip reduction fabrics, and software-managed memory hierarchies. We ship kernel libraries with broad PyTorch operator coverage, build C++ and Python kernel authoring frameworks and DSL surfaces, and write production kernels against new architectures long before first silicon — turning hardware proposals into measured roofline evidence while the design can still change. We are seeking a Software Engineering Manager to lead a team of kernel and performance engineers doing this work. You will own the performance of workloads that serve billions of people, drive technical strategy for kernel development and optimization, and build a team that can deliver roofline-level performance on MTIA accelerators. Your team will profile and root-cause performance across the full stack — instruction scheduling, memory hierarchy and DMA behavior, on-chip interconnect, multi-device collectives — and drive fixes to the right layer, whether that is the kernel, compiler, runtime, or hardware. You will partner closely with silicon architecture teams on hardware/software co-design, quantifying the value of proposed features with real kernels and advocating for the changes the software stack needs. This is a hands-on technical leadership role where you will contribute directly to architectural decisions while enabling your team to move with speed and clarity.

The Meta Reality Labs Research Team brings together a world-class team of researchers, developers, and engineers to create the future of AR and VR. The Surreal Vision group at RL Research is seeking exceptional Research Scientists to research and help build the egocentric machine perception functionalities and digital twins of 3D scenes that will underpin future VR and contextual-AI-enabled AR devices. This internship focuses on developing a learned model for motion analysis for swing sports as an alternative to heuristic, threshold-based methods. Research goals include: improving analysis accuracy, generalization across players and equipment, and generating interpretable feedback outputs. The intern will contribute to egocentric data collection using the team's simulator research setup, in addition to model development. Our internships are twelve (12) to twenty-four (24) weeks long and we have various start dates throughout the year. Some projects may require a minimum of 24 consecutive weeks.

Responsibilities

  • Operate egocentric data collections on our state-of-the-art in-lab simulator - instrument participants with Aria Gen 2 and Neural Band wearables, run capture sessions, and use the simulator's ground-truth as supervision and validation signal for your models.
  • Design and train models over multimodal egocentric time-series: Aria Gen 2 (SLAM/IMU, eye gaze, RGB) fused with Neural Band surface EMG and wrist IMU.
  • Tackle the core modeling problems: temporal swing phase segmentation (address → takeaway → impact → follow-through), kinematic/intent estimation from a head-mounted and wrist-worn viewpoint, and swing-quality scoring.
  • Build an evaluation harness that benchmarks the model against the existing threshold baseline on held-out players - accuracy, phase-boundary error, and cross-subject generalization.
  • Define the capture and labeling protocol, and handle the realities of small, noisy, personalized datasets (self-supervised pretraining, augmentation, subject-adaptive fine-tuning).
  • Integrate the winning model back into our prototype and demo it end to end.
  • Write up results; strong work is a candidate for publication or an internal tech report.

Minimum Qualifications

  • Currently has, or is in the process of obtaining a PhD degree in the domain of Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, Biomechanics, or a related field
  • Strong Python and hands-on experience training models in PyTorch
  • Working knowledge of sequence/time-series modeling (temporal CNNs, transformers, state-space models, HMM/CTC-style segmentation)
  • Experience working with real sensor data, not just curated benchmarks
  • Comfortable running hands-on hardware experiments with human participants in a lab setting
  • Must obtain work authorization in the country of employment at the time of hire, and maintain ongoing work authorization during employment

Preferred Qualifications

  • Experience designing and executing your own data collections with wearable or motion-capture hardware
  • Research experience with IMU-based human activity recognition, pose/motion estimation, or wearable biosignals
  • Experience with surface EMG: filtering, rectification, envelope extraction, electrode-shift and cross-session variability
  • Familiarity with egocentric perception (Project Aria, Ego4D/Ego-Exo4D, Aria Digital Twin) or multimodal sensor fusion
  • Background in sports biomechanics or motion analysis
  • self-supervised or few-shot learning for personalization
  • First-author publications at CVPR/ICCV/ECCV/NeurIPS/ICLR, or in biomechanics and wearables venues
  • Plays swing sports - genuinely helpful for labeling and sanity-checking feedback
  • Intent to return to a degree-program after the completion of the internship

Every day, people come to Meta to connect with friends and family, discover what's going on in the world, interact with businesses, find potential customers, and build community. Meta's Global Operations exists to support them. The Risk, Monitoring and Controls (RMC) team makes risk management operational and ensures Meta is protected from compliance and/or audit risks by implementing, overseeing, and enhancing internal and external controls for the purpose of identifying and mitigating risk. The team also protects user personal data through vetting and periodic developer reviews in order to detect apps that are not compliant with our platform policies. RMC designs and runs the processes, protocols, and monitoring that allow operational teams to execute their controls reliably, evidence them credibly, and surface issues early. We are not the risk assessors or policy setters; we are the team that makes risk management workable in the day-to-day. We're looking for someone who can translate risk and control frameworks into practical operating routines that operations teams will actually use, and who understands where first-line accountability ends and second-line oversight begins. Depending on audit outcomes, we may take a variety of actions; everything from implementing management action plans, which set requirements for remediation of identified risks and control gaps, to working with cross-functional teams to implement systems and/or engineering fixes, which ensure that the backend infrastructure is operating as intended. We are committed to protecting users' personal information and improving the overall platform experience. Meta is looking for a Risk and Control Manager who will be responsible for conducting recurring audits across its monitoring tactics to identify potential violations of our policies.   • Develop strong, productive working relationships with internal cross-functional areas. About the role

Anthropic is looking for a Communications Lead to own external communications for the Claude Platform, our API. You should understand how developers and enterprises actually build with APIs and be comfortable engaging with developer tools and hold a clear point of view on what makes a product land.

  • Strong instincts for which product moments deserve the spotlight and which don't, and genuine curiosity about what makes a launch land

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts.   • Demonstrated experience with Maintenance Task Analysis and development of maintenance planning data.
  • Expertise of Logistics Control Number structures and their use in provisioning, maintenance planning, and supportability analysis.
  • Experience with Reliability and Maintainability principles, including failure modes, maintainability drivers, reliability growth, availability metrics, and field performance analysis, and LORA development
  • Hands-on supply support experience, including spares planning, provisioning, inventory management, parts forecasting, repairables management, and sustainment execution.

  • Proven experience with integrated product support elements, including product support management, supply support, support equipment, manpower and personnel, facilities, maintenance planning,
  • Experience with provisioning, sparing, or supportability tools such as PowerLOG-J, SLICwave, COMPASS, CASA, OPUS10, EAGLE, or similar systems.
